items.ma-1307: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: I heard al-Qāsim ibn Abī Bazzah narrating from Abū al-Ṭufayl, he said: ʿAlī was asked: Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ single you out with anything? He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not single us out with anything that he did not extend to all the people, except what was in the sheath of this sword of mine. He said: Then he brought out a sheet on which was written: “May Allah curse whoever slaughters for other than Allah; may Allah curse whoever steals the boundary markers of the land; may Allah curse whoever curses his father; and may Allah curse whoever gives shelter to a muḥdith.”
items.ma-1308: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah, from Abū Ḥassān al-Aʿraj, from ʿAbīdah, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on the day of al-Aḥzāb: “O Allah, fill their houses and their graves with fire, as they kept us occupied from the middle prayer until the sun had set.”
items.ma-1309: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, he said: I heard Ḥujayyah ibn ʿAdī say: I heard ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, when a man asked him about the cow, and he said: [It is] on behalf of seven. And he asked him about the lame one, and he said: When it reaches the place of sacrifice. And he was asked about the horn? He said: It does not harm it. And ʿAlī said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to examine the eye and the ear closely.
items.ma-1310:
Bahz and ʿAffān narrated to us, the meaning, they said: Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, Simāk informed us, from Ḥanash ibn al-Muʿtamir: that ʿAlī was in Yemen, and they dug a pit for a lion; it came until a man fell into it, and he clung to another, and that one clung to another, and that one clung to another, until they became four. The lion wounded them in it; some of them died in it, and some of them were taken out and died. He said: So they disputed about that until they took up weapons. He said: So ʿAlī came to them and said: Woe to you! Would you kill two hundred people over four human beings? Come, let me judge between you with a judgement; if you are pleased with it [well and good], and if not, then take it up to the Prophet ﷺ. He said: So he ruled for the first a quarter of the blood-money, for the second a third of his blood-money, for the third half of his blood-money, and for the fourth the full blood-money. He said: Some of them were pleased and some disliked it, and he placed the blood-money upon the tribes of those who had crowded together.
He said: So they took it up to the Prophet ﷺ – Bahz said: Ḥammād said: I think he said: He was reclining, then sat hugging his knees – He said: “I will judge between you with a judgement.” He said: Then he was informed that ʿAlī ﵁ had ruled such and such, he said: So he upheld his ruling. ʿAffān said: “I will judge between you.”
items.ma-1311: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Ḥajjāj Ibn al-Shāʿir narrated to me, Shabābah narrated to us, Nuʿaym ibn Ḥakīm narrated to me, Abū Maryam narrated to me, and a man from the associates of ʿAlī, from ʿAlī: that the Prophet ﷺ said on the day of Ghadīr Khumm: “Whoever I am his mawlā, then ʿAlī is his mawlā.” He said: Then the people added afterwards: Befriend whoever befriends him, and be hostile to whoever is hostile to him.
items.ma-1312: Bahz ibn Asad narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, Salamah ibn Kuhayl informed us, from Ḥujayyah ibn ʿAdī: that ʿAlī was asked about the cow, and he said: [It is] on behalf of seven. And he was asked about the one whose horn is broken, and he said: There is no harm. And he was asked about lameness, and he said: As long as it reaches the place of sacrifice. Then he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to examine the eyes and the ears closely.
items.ma-1313:
ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Walīd al-Narsī narrated to me, ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Ziyād narrated to us, Saʿīd al-Jurayrī narrated to us, from Abū al-Ward, from Ibn Aʿbud, he said: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said to me: O Ibn Aʿbud, do you know what the right of food is? He said: I said: And what is its right, O Ibn Abī Ṭālib? He said: You say: In the name of Allah, O Allah, bless us in what You have provided us. He said: And do you know what its thanks is when you have finished? He said: I said: And what is its thanks? He said: You say: Praise be to Allah, Who fed us and gave us drink.
Then he said: Shall I not tell you about myself and Fāṭimah? She was the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and she was among the most honoured of his family to him, and she was my wife. She pulled the millstone until the millstone left a mark on her hand, and she drew water with the waterskin until the waterskin left a mark on her neck, and she swept the house until her garments became dusty, and she lit [a fire] under the pot until her garments became soiled. So harm reached her from that. Then captives – or servants – were brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: So I said to her: Go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and ask him for a servant to shield you from the heat of what you are in. So she went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and found with him servants – or attendants – so she returned and did not ask him … Then he mentioned the ḥadīth, and he said: “Shall I not direct you to what is better for you than a servant? When you take to your bed, glorify [Allah] thirty-three times, praise [Him] thirty-three times, and say takbīr thirty-four times.” He said: Then she put out her head and said: I am pleased with Allah and His Messenger – twice. Then he mentioned the like of the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿUlayyah from al-Jurayrī, or something like it.
items.ma-1314: Bahz narrated to us, Hammām narrated to us, from Qatādah, from Abū Ḥassān, from ʿAbīdah, he said: We used to think that the middle prayer was the Ṣubḥ prayer. He said: Then ʿAlī narrated to us: that on the day of al-Aḥzāb they fought, and they held us back from the ʿAṣr prayer, so the Prophet ﷺ said: “O Allah, fill their graves with fire – or: fill their bellies with fire – as they held us back from the middle prayer.” He said: So on that day we knew that the middle prayer is the ʿAṣr prayer.
items.ma-1315: Bahz narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Maysarah informed me, from Zayd ibn Wahb, from ʿAlī: that the Prophet ﷺ sent him a striped silk garment, so he put it on and went out to the people, and he recognised anger in his face, so he commanded him to cut it up among his women.
items.ma-1316: Bahz narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Maysarah, he said: I heard al-Nazzāl ibn Sabrah say: I saw ʿAlī pray Ẓuhr, then sit for the needs of the people. When the ʿAṣr arrived, a basin of water was brought to him. He took a handful from it and wiped his face, his forearms, his head and his feet, then took the remainder and drank it standing, and said: Some people dislike this, yet I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do it, and this is the wuḍūʾ of one who has not [yet] nullified it.
items.ma-1317: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from al-Shaʿbī: that ʿAlī said to Shurāḥah: Perhaps you were forced; perhaps your husband came to you; perhaps you …? She said: No. When she had given birth, he flogged her, then stoned her. It was said to him: Why did you flog her, then stone her? He said: I flogged her by the Book of Allah, and I stoned her by the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-1318: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Kāmil Fuḍayl ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, and Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd ibn Ḥisāb narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Ziyād narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, from al-Nuʿmān ibn Saʿd, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The best of you is whoever learns the Qurʾān and teaches it.”
items.ma-1319: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar narrated to me, Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Isḥāq al-Qurashī, from Sayyār Abū al-Ḥakam, from Abū Wāʾil, he said: A man came to ʿAlī and said: O Commander of the Believers, I am unable to pay my mukātabah, so help me. ʿAlī said: Shall I not teach you words that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught me, such that if you had upon you the like of Mount Ṣīr in dīnārs, Allah would pay it on your behalf? I said: Yes. He said: Say: O Allah, suffice me with Your lawful instead of Your forbidden, and make me independent by Your bounty of anyone other than You.
items.ma-1320: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Kāmil al-Jaḥdarī, Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr al-Muqaddamī and Rawḥ ibn ʿAbd al-Muʾmin al-Muqriʾ narrated to us. And Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd ibn Ḥisāb and ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar al-Qawārīrī narrated to us, they said: ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Ziyād narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, from al-Nuʿmān ibn Saʿd, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “O Allah, bless my ummah in its early mornings.”
items.ma-1321:
ʿAffān narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim ibn Kulayb, Abū Burdah ibn Abī Mūsā narrated to me, he said: I was sitting with Abū Mūsā, and ʿAlī came to us and stood over Abū Mūsā and commanded him with a matter from the affairs of the people. ʿAlī said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: “Say: O Allah, guide me and keep me straight, and bear in mind, by ‘guidance’, your guiding along the road, and bear in mind, by ‘straightness’, the straightening of the arrow.” And he forbade me to put my ring on this – and Abū Burdah gestured to the index finger or the middle finger – ʿĀṣim said: I am the one who was unsure which of the two he meant – and he forbade me the mīthara and the qassiyyah.
Abū Burdah said: I said: O Commander of the Believers, what are the mīthara and the qassiyyah? He said: As for the mīthara: it is something the women used to make for their husbands so that they would place it on their saddles; and as for the qassī: garments that used to come to us from al-Shām or Yemen – ʿĀṣim was unsure – with silk in them, with [patterns] like citrons. Abū Burdah said: When I saw the sabanī, I knew that it was that.
items.ma-1322: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn al-Minhāl, the brother of Ḥajjāj, narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Ziyād narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, from al-Nuʿmān ibn Saʿd, he said: A man said to ʿAlī: O Commander of the Believers, which month do you command me to fast after Ramaḍān? He said: I have not heard anyone ask about this after a man who asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, which month do you command me to fast after Ramaḍān? He said: “If you are fasting a month after Ramaḍān, then fast al-Muḥarram, for it is the month of Allah, and in it is a day on which He accepted the repentance of a people, and on which He will accept the repentance of [other] people.”
items.ma-1323: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Rawḥ ibn ʿAbd al-Muʾmin narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Ziyād narrated to us. And ʿAmr al-Nāqid narrated to me, Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Isḥāq, from al-Nuʿmān ibn Saʿd, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “O Allah, bless my ummah in its early mornings.”
items.ma-1324: ʿAffān narrated to us – I think [it was] from Abū ʿAwānah – from Khālid ibn ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Khayr, he said: I came to ʿAlī after he had prayed, and he called for purification water, and we said: What will he do with purification water when he has prayed? He wants nothing except to teach us. So a basin and a vessel were brought, and he lifted the vessel and poured over his hand and washed it three times; then he dipped his hand into the vessel, and rinsed his mouth and snuffed water into his nose three times; then he rinsed his mouth and snuffed from the palm from which he had taken; then he washed his face three times, and washed his right hand three times and his left hand three times; then he put his hand in the water and wiped his head once; then he washed his right foot three times and his left foot three times. Then he said: Whoever it pleases to know the purification of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, this is it.
items.ma-1325: Muʿādh narrated to us, Zuhayr ibn Muʿāwiyah Abū Khaythamah informed us, from ʿAbd al-Karīm al-Jazarī, from Mujāhid, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded me to take charge of his sacrificial camels, and to give in ṣadaqah their meat, their hides and their covers, and not to give the butcher anything of them. He said: “We give him from what we have.”
items.ma-1326: Muʿādh narrated to us, Sufyān al-Thawrī narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Karīm, from Mujāhid, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded me … the like of this, except that he did not say: “We give him from what we have.”
items.ma-1327: ʿAffān narrated to us, Hammām narrated to us, Qatādah informed us, from Abū Ḥassān, from ʿAbīdah al-Salmānī, from ʿAlī, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on the day of al-Aḥzāb: “May Allah fill their houses and their graves with fire, as they held us back from the middle prayer until the sun disappeared.” Or he said: “until the sun had set” – one of the two words.
items.ma-1328: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Abū Ẓabyān al-Janbī: that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was brought a woman who had committed zinā, and he commanded that she be stoned. So they took her away to stone her, and ʿAlī ﵁ met them and said: What is this? They said: She committed zinā, and ʿUmar commanded that she be stoned. So ʿAlī snatched her from their hands and sent them back. They returned to ʿUmar, and he said: What turned you back? They said: ʿAlī turned us back. He said: ʿAlī did not do this except for something he knows. So he sent for ʿAlī, and he came, looking somewhat angry, and said: What is the matter with you, that you turned these back? He said: Did you not hear the Prophet ﷺ say: “The pen is lifted from three: from the sleeper until he wakes, from the child until he grows up, and from the afflicted until he regains his reason”? He said: Yes. ʿAlī said: This is a woman afflicted, from [the family of] so-and-so; perhaps he came to her while she was in that state. ʿUmar said: I do not know. He said: And I do not know. So he did not stone her.
items.ma-1329: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to me, ʿAlī ibn Mushir narrated to us. And Rawḥ ibn ʿAbd al-Muʾmin narrated to me, ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Ziyād narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Isḥāq, from al-Nuʿmān ibn Saʿd, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “O Allah, bless my ummah in its early mornings.”
items.ma-1330: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar al-Qawārīrī narrated to me, ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Ziyād narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, from al-Nuʿmān ibn Saʿd, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, raising it: that he ﷺ forbade reciting the Qurʾān while bowing, and said: “When you bow, magnify Allah, and when you prostrate, supplicate, for it is fitting that you be answered.”
items.ma-1331: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Maʿmar narrated to me, ʿAlī ibn Mushir and Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to me, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Isḥāq, from al-Nuʿmān ibn Saʿd, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “O Allah, bless my ummah in its early mornings.”
items.ma-1332: Ibn Abī ʿAdī narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAwn, from Muḥammad, he said: ʿAbīdah said: I will not narrate to you except what I heard from him. Muḥammad said: Then ʿAbīdah swore to us three times, and ʿAlī swore to him, he said: He said: Were it not that you would become arrogant, I would inform you of what Allah promised those who kill them, on the tongue of Muḥammad ﷺ. He said: I said: Did you hear it from him? He said: Yes, by the Rabb of the Kaʿbah; yes, by the Rabb of the Kaʿbah; yes, by the Rabb of the Kaʿbah: among them is a man with a deformed hand, or a breast-like hand. I think he said: or a stunted hand.
items.ma-1333: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Suwayd ibn Saʿīd narrated to me, ʿAlī ibn Mushir informed us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Isḥāq, al-Nuʿmān ibn Saʿd narrated to us, he said: We were sitting with ʿAlī, and he recited this verse: {On the Day We gather the God-fearing to al-Raḥmān as a delegation} [Maryam: 85]. He said: No, by Allah, they will not be gathered on their feet, and a delegation is not gathered on its feet; rather, on she-camels the like of which the creatures have not seen, upon which are saddles of gold, and they will ride them until they knock on the doors of Paradise.
items.ma-1334: Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿAdī narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, Abān ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to me, from ʿIkrimah, he said: I stood with al-Ḥusayn, and I kept hearing him say: Labbayk, labbayk, until he threw [pebbles at] the jamrah. I said: O Abū ʿAbd Allāh, what is this ihlāl? He said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib making ihlāl until he reached the jamrah, and he narrated to me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made ihlāl until he reached it.
items.ma-1335: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Zuhayr Abū Khaythamah narrated to me, Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, from al-Nuʿmān ibn Saʿd, from ʿAlī, he said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, tell me of a month that I may fast after Ramaḍān. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “If you are fasting a month after Ramaḍān, then fast al-Muḥarram, for it is the month of Allah, and in it is a day on which He accepted the repentance of a people, and on which the repentance of others will be accepted.”
items.ma-1336: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Sharīk informed us, from Manṣūr, from Ribʿī, from ʿAlī, he said: Some people from Quraysh came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: “O Muḥammad, we are your neighbours and your allies, and some people from among our slaves have come to you; they have no desire for the religion and no desire for understanding; they only fled from our estates and our wealth, so return them to us.” He said to Abū Bakr: “What do you say?” He said: They have spoken truly; they are your neighbours. He said: So the face of the Prophet ﷺ changed. Then he said to ʿUmar: “What do you say?” He said: They have spoken truly; they are indeed your neighbours and your allies. So the face of the Prophet ﷺ changed.
items.ma-1337: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Suwayd ibn Saʿīd narrated to me in the year two hundred and twenty-six, ʿAlī ibn Mushir informed us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Isḥāq, from al-Nuʿmān ibn Saʿd, from ʿAlī, he said: A man asked him: “Shall I recite during bowing and prostration?” He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I have been forbidden to recite during bowing and prostration. So when you bow, magnify Allah, and when you prostrate, strive in the asking, for it is fitting that you will be answered.”
items.ma-1338: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿAbbād ibn Yaʿqūb al-Asadī, Abū Muḥammad, narrated to me, Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Isḥāq, from al-Nuʿmān ibn Saʿd, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed in Paradise there are chambers whose insides are seen from their outsides, and whose outsides are seen from their insides.” A Bedouin said: “O Messenger of Allah, for whom are they?” He said: “For whoever makes speech good, feeds food, and prays to Allah by night while the people are asleep.”
items.ma-1339: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Rawḥ ibn ʿAbd al-Muʾmin al-Muqriʾ narrated to me, ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Ziyād narrated to us; and ʿAbbād ibn Yaʿqūb al-Asadī narrated to me, Ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, both together from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Isḥāq, from al-Nuʿmān ibn Saʿd, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “O Allah, bless my ummah in its early mornings.”
items.ma-1340: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Abū Bakr reported to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sabuʿ, he said: ʿAlī addressed us and said: “By the One who split the grain and created the soul, this will surely be dyed from this.” He said: The people said: “Let us know who he is. By Allah, we will surely destroy him”—or “we will surely destroy his kin”—. He said: “I adjure you by Allah that anyone other than my killer be killed.” They said: “If you know that, then appoint a successor.” He said: “No, but I leave you to that to which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ left you.”
items.ma-1341: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd narrated to us, Zāʾidah reported to us, from al-Suddī, from Saʿd ibn ʿUbaydah, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, he said: ʿAlī addressed [the people] and said: O people, establish the ḥudūd upon your slaves, whoever of them is muḥṣan and whoever is not muḥṣan. For a female slave of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ committed zinā, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered me to establish the ḥadd upon her. I came to her and found that she had only recently given birth, so I feared that if I flogged her she would die. So I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and mentioned that to him, and he said: “You did well.”
items.ma-1342: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Ḥārithah ibn Muḍarrib, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me to Yemen, and I said: “You are sending me to a people who are older than I am, to judge between them.” He said: “Go, for Allah will guide your heart and make your tongue firm.”
items.ma-1343: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to me, Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Isḥāq, from al-Nuʿmān ibn Saʿd, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed in Paradise there is a market in which there is no buying and no selling, except the images of women and men. When a man desires an image, he enters into it. And indeed in it there is a gathering-place of the ḥūr ʿīn; they raise voices the like of which the creatures have never seen, saying: We are the everlasting, so we do not perish; we are the pleased, so we are not displeased; we are the delighted, so we are not distressed. Ṭūbā for whoever is ours and we are his.”
items.ma-1344: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Zuhayr Abū Khaythamah narrated to me, Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed in Paradise there is a market …” and he mentioned the hadith, except that he said: “When a man desires an image, he enters it,” he said: “And in it is the meeting-place of the ḥūr ʿīn; they raise voices …” and he mentioned the like of it.
items.ma-1345: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Abān al-Balkhī narrated to me, ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū Ḥayyah ibn Qays, from ʿAlī: that he performed wuḍūʾ three times each, then wiped his head, then drank the remainder of his wuḍūʾ [water], then said: “Whoever is pleased to look at the wuḍūʾ of the Prophet ﷺ, let him look at this.”
items.ma-1346: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Suwayd ibn Ghafalah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “In the last of time there will be a people who recite the Qurʾān; it does not pass beyond their collarbones. They pass out of Islam as the arrow passes out of the game. Fighting them is a right upon every Muslim.”
items.ma-1347: Abū Kāmil narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, Abū Isḥāq narrated to us, from Ḥārithah ibn al-Muḍarrib, from ʿAlī. Yaḥyā ibn Ādam and Abū al-Naḍr narrated to us; both said: Zuhayr narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Ḥārithah ibn Muḍarrib, from ʿAlī, he said: When the fighting reddened and the people met the people, we would protect ourselves by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and none of us would be nearer to the people than he.
items.ma-1348:
Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAyyāsh, from Zayd ibn ʿAlī, from his father, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Rāfiʿ, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood at ʿArafah and said: “This is the standing-place, and the whole of ʿArafah is a standing-place.” Then he seated Usāmah behind him, and he went at a quick pace on his she-camel while the people were striking their camels to the right and to the left; he did not turn to them, and he said: “Calmness, O people.” And he set off when the sun had set, and came to Jamʿ, and prayed there the two prayers—meaning the Maghrib and the ʿIshāʾ—then spent the night there. When morning came, he stood at Quzaḥ and said: “This is Quzaḥ, and it is the standing-place, and the whole of Jamʿ is a standing-place.” He said: Then he proceeded, and when he came to Muḥassir he struck her and she trotted until he crossed the valley; then he held her back and seated al-Faḍl behind him. Then he proceeded until he came to the jamrah and threw at it; then he came to the place of slaughter and said: “This is the place of slaughter, and the whole of Minā is a place of slaughter.”
Then a young woman from Khathʿam came to him and said: “My father is an old man who has become senile, and the obligation of Allah in Ḥajj has reached him; does it suffice if I perform Ḥajj on his behalf?” He said: “Yes, so perform it on behalf of your father.” He said: And he turned the neck of al-Faḍl. Al-ʿAbbās said to him: “O Messenger of Allah, why did you turn the neck of your cousin?” He said: “I saw a young man and a young woman, and I feared Satan for them both.”
He said: And a man came to him and said: “I made the ifāḍah before I shaved.” He said: “Shave, or shorten, and there is no harm.”
He said: And he came to Zamzam and said: “O Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, [draw] your watering-place; were it not that the people would overpower you over it, I would have drawn.”
items.ma-1349: Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, Hāshim—meaning Ibn al-Barīd—narrated to us, from Ismāʿīl al-Ḥanafī, from Muslim al-Baṭīn, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, he said: ʿAlī ﵁ took me by the hand, and we set off walking until we sat on the bank of the Euphrates. ʿAlī said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no soul given breath except that wretchedness or happiness has already been decreed for it from Allah.” A man stood and said: “O Messenger of Allah, then for what do we act?” He said: “Act, for each is eased toward that for which he was created,” then he recited this verse: {As for him who gives and is God-fearing and believes in the best, We will ease him toward ease. But as for him who is stingy and considers himself free of need and denies the best, We will ease him toward hardship.}
items.ma-1350: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Isḥāq ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Wakīʿ narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū Ḥayyah al-Wādiʿī, he said: I saw ʿAlī urinate in al-Raḥabah, then he called for water and performed wuḍūʾ. He washed his palms three times, rinsed his mouth and sniffed water into his nose three times, washed his face three times, washed his forearms three times each, wiped his head, and washed his feet three times each. Then he said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do as you saw me do.
items.ma-1351: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Zuhayr Abū Khaythamah narrated to me, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū Ḥayyah, from ʿAlī: that the Prophet ﷺ performed wuḍūʾ three times each.
items.ma-1352: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to me, Abū al-Aḥwaṣ narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū Ḥayyah, he said: I saw ʿAlī perform wuḍūʾ; he cleaned his palms, then washed his face three times, and his forearms three times, and wiped his head, then washed his feet up to the ankles; then he stood and drank the remainder of his wuḍūʾ [water]; then he said: I only wanted to show you the purification of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-1353: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Suwayd ibn Saʿīd narrated to me, Marwān al-Fazārī narrated to us, from al-Mukhtār ibn Nāfiʿ, Abū Maṭar al-Baṣrī—and he had met ʿAlī—narrated to me: that ʿAlī bought a garment for three dirhams, and when he put it on he said: “Praise be to Allah who provided me from the finery that with which I adorn myself among the people and cover my private parts.” Then he said: “Thus I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say.”
items.ma-1354: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Saʿīd ibn Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Qurashī narrated to me, my father narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū Ḥayyah al-Hamdānī, he said: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: “Whoever is pleased to look at the wuḍūʾ of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, let him look at me.” He said: So he performed wuḍūʾ three times each, then wiped his head, then drank the remainder of his wuḍūʾ [water].
items.ma-1355: Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, Mukhtār ibn Nāfiʿ al-Tammār narrated to us, from Abū Maṭar: that he saw ʿAlī come to a young lad, a youth, and buy from him a shirt for three dirhams, and he wore it down to what is between the wrists and the ankles, saying as he wore it: “Praise be to Allah who provided me from the finery that with which I adorn myself among the people and cover my private parts.” It was said: “Is this something you relate from yourself, or from the Prophet of Allah ﷺ?” He said: “This is something I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saying at the time of clothing: ‘Praise be to Allah who provided me from the finery that with which I adorn myself among the people and cover my private parts.’”
items.ma-1356: Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, Mukhtār narrated to us, from Abū Maṭar, he said: While we were sitting with the Commander of the Believers ʿAlī in the mosque at the door of al-Raḥabah, a man came and said: “Show me the wuḍūʾ of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ”—and this was at the decline [of the sun]—so he called Qanbar and said: “Bring me a jug of water.” He washed his palms and his face three times, rinsed his mouth three times, putting some of his fingers into his mouth, sniffed water into his nose three times, washed his forearms three times, and wiped his head once. And he said: “The inside of the two of them is from the face, and the outside of the two of them is from the head.” And [he washed] his feet up to the ankles three times, while his beard was dripping onto his chest. Then he sipped a sip after the wuḍūʾ. Then he said: “Where is the one who asked about the wuḍūʾ of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? Such was the wuḍūʾ of the Prophet of Allah ﷺ.”
items.ma-1357: Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd and Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us; both said: Misʿar narrated to us, from Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm, from Ibn Shaddād, he said: I heard ʿAlī say: I never heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ combine his father and his mother for anyone except for Saʿd. Abū Nuʿaym said: “his two parents for anyone.”
items.ma-1358: Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Saʿd ibn ʿUbaydah, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAlī, he said: I said: “O Messenger of Allah, why do you choose carefully among Quraysh and do not marry from us?” He said: “And do you have anything?” I said: Yes, the daughter of Ḥamzah. He said: “That is the daughter of my brother by nursing.”
items.ma-1359: Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb narrated to us, from Abū al-Khayr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zurayr, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, he said: A mule was given as a gift to the Prophet ﷺ and he rode it. One of his Companions said: “What if we were to acquire the like of this?” He said: “Do you want to have donkeys mount horses? Only those who do not know do that.”
items.ma-1360: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn Muḥammad ibn Bukayr al-Nāqid narrated to me, al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Hilāl al-Raqqī narrated to us, ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Abī Unaysah, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū Ḥayyah, he said: ʿAlī said: “Shall I not show you how the Prophet of Allah ﷺ used to perform wuḍūʾ?” We said: “Yes.” He said: “Then bring me a basin and a pitcher of water.” So he washed his hands three times, sniffed water into his nose three times, blew it out three times, washed his face three times, washed his hands up to the elbows three times, wiped his head three times, and washed his feet three times.
items.ma-1361: Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, Saʿīd ibn Salamah ibn Abī al-Ḥusām narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAqīl narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Akbar, that he heard his father ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I have been given four that none of the prophets of Allah was given: I was given the keys of the earth, and I was named Aḥmad, and the soil was made for me a purifier, and my ummah was made the best of the nations.”
items.ma-1362: Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Abū Ẓabyān, that ʿAlī said to ʿUmar: “O Commander of the Believers, did you not hear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: ‘The pen has been lifted from three: from the sleeper until he wakes, from the young child until he grows up, and from the afflicted until he comes to reason’?”
items.ma-1363: Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, Abū Isḥāq narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Shall I not teach you words which, if you say them, you will be forgiven, even though [it] is forgiven for you: There is no deity except Allah, al-ʿAlī, al-ʿAẓīm; there is no deity except Him, al-Ḥalīm, al-Karīm; glory be to Allah, Rabb of the Great Throne; praise be to Allah, Rabb of the worlds.”
items.ma-1364: Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, Hushaym narrated to us, Ḥuṣayn ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from al-Shaʿbī, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed the one who consumes ribā, the one who feeds it, its two witnesses, its writer, the muḥill and the muḥallal lahu, the woman who tattoos and the woman who has herself tattooed, and the one who withholds ṣadaqah; and he forbade wailing.
items.ma-1365: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, he said: Yūnus ibn Abī Isḥāq informed me, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū Juḥayfah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever commits a sin in the world and is punished for it, then Allah is more just than to repeat His punishment upon His servant; and whoever commits a sin in the world and Allah conceals it for him and pardons him, then Allah is more generous than to return to something He has pardoned.”
items.ma-1366: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Khaythamah narrated to me; and Isḥāq ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us; both said: Jarīr narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Maysarah, from al-Nazzāl ibn Sabrah, he said: We prayed the Ẓuhr with ʿAlī, and he went to a sitting-place of his where he used to sit in al-Raḥabah; he sat, and we sat around him. Then the ʿAṣr [prayer] arrived, and a vessel was brought; he took a handful from it, rinsed his mouth, sniffed water into his nose, wiped his face and his forearms, wiped his head, and wiped his feet; then he stood and drank the remainder of his vessel; then he said: “I have been told that some men dislike that one of them drink while standing. I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do as I have done.”
items.ma-1367: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim ibn Kulayb, from Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī: that ʿAlī said: I have seen myself with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ tying a stone upon my belly from hunger, and today my ṣadaqah is indeed forty thousand.
items.ma-1368: Aswad narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim ibn Kulayb, from Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī, from ʿAlī … and he mentioned the hadith, and he said in it: and indeed the ṣadaqah of my wealth reaches forty thousand dīnārs.
items.ma-1369: Yaḥyā ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, from Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm, from Salamah ibn Abī al-Ṭufayl, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: “Do not follow one glance with another glance, for the first is for you, and the last is not for you.”
items.ma-1370: Zakariyyā ibn ʿAdī narrated to us, ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAmr reported to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAqīl, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAlī, he said: When al-Ḥasan was born, he named him Ḥamzah; and when al-Ḥusayn was born, he named him after his uncle Jaʿfar. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called me and said: “I have been commanded to change the names of these two.” I said: Allah and His Messenger know best. So he named them Ḥasan and Ḥusayn.
items.ma-1371: ʿAffān narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from ʿUthmān ibn al-Mughīrah, from Abū Ṣādiq, from Rabīʿah ibn Nājidh, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gathered—or the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called—the Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, among whom was a group each of whom would eat a young sheep (jadhaʿah) and drink a faraq. He said: So he prepared for them a mudd of food, and they ate until they were full. He said: And the food remained as it was, as though it had not been touched. Then he called for small cups, and they drank until they were quenched, and the drink remained as though it had not been touched or had not been drunk. Then he said: “O Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, I have been sent to you in particular, and to the people in general, and you have seen from this sign what you have seen; so which of you will pledge allegiance to me on the condition that he be my brother and my companion?” He said: No one stood up to him. He said: So I stood up to him, and I was the youngest of the people. He said: “Sit.” He said it three times, each time I stood up to him and he said to me: “Sit,” until the third time he struck his hand upon my hand.
items.ma-1372: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, Ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Maysarah, from al-Nazzāl ibn Sabrah, from ʿAlī: that he drank while standing, then said: Thus I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-1373: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, from Salamah ibn Abī al-Ṭufayl, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, that the Prophet ﷺ said to him: “O ʿAlī, you have a treasure from Paradise, and you are the possessor of its two horns. So do not follow one glance with another glance, for you only have the first, and the last is not for you.”
items.ma-1374: Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, from ʿAlī, he said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ slaughtered his sacrificial camels, he slaughtered thirty with his own hand, and he ordered me, so I slaughtered the rest of them, and he said: “Distribute their meat among the people, and their hides and their coverings, and do not give the butcher anything of it.”
items.ma-1375: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, he said: I heard ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah say: We asked ʿAlī about the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the daytime, and he said: You cannot bear that. He said: We said: Whoever of us can bear that. He said: When the sun was from here like its appearance from here at the ʿAṣr, he would pray two rakʿahs; and when the sun was from here like its appearance from here at the Ẓuhr, he would pray four; and he would pray four before the Ẓuhr and two after it, and four before the ʿAṣr, and he would separate every two rakʿahs with the taslīm upon the angels brought near and the prophets, and whoever followed them among the believers and the Muslims.
items.ma-1376:
Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: Surayj ibn Yūnus Abū al-Ḥārith narrated to me, Abū Ḥafṣ al-Abbār narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, from al-Ḥārith ibn Ḥaṣīrah, from Abū Ṣādiq, from Rabīʿah ibn Nājidh, from ʿAlī, he said: The Prophet ﷺ said to me: “There is in you a likeness to ʿĪsā: the Jews hated him until they slandered his mother, and the Christians loved him until they placed him in the position in which he is not.”
Then he said: Two men will perish concerning me: an excessive lover who praises me with what is not in me, and a hater whose enmity toward me drives him to slander me.
items.ma-1377:
ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Muḥammad Sufyān ibn Wakīʿ ibn al-Jarrāḥ ibn Malīḥ narrated to me, Khālid ibn Makhlad narrated to us, Abū Ghaylān al-Shaybānī narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, from al-Ḥārith ibn Ḥaṣīrah, from Abū Ṣādiq, from Rabīʿah ibn Nājid, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called me and said: “Indeed there is in you a likeness to ʿĪsā: the Jews hated him until they slandered his mother, and the Christians loved him until they placed him in the position in which he is not.”
Beware, two will perish concerning me: an extravagant lover who praises me with what is not in me, and a hater whose enmity toward me drives him to slander me. Beware, I am not a prophet, and revelation is not revealed to me, but I act by the Book of Allah and the sunnah of His Prophet ﷺ as far as I am able. So whatever I command you of obedience to Allah, then obedience to me is a right upon you, in what you like and what you dislike.
items.ma-1378: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Khaythamah Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb narrated to me, al-Qāsim ibn Mālik al-Muzanī narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim ibn Kulayb, from his father, he said: I was sitting with ʿAlī, and he said: I entered upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and there was no one with him except ʿĀʾishah, and he said: “O son of Abū Ṭālib, how will you be with a people of such and such?” He said: I said: Allah and His Messenger know best. He said: “A people who will come out from the east; they recite the Qurʾān, it does not pass beyond their collarbones; they pass out of the religion as the arrow passes out of the game; among them is a man with a deformed hand, as if his hands were the breast of an Abyssinian woman.”
items.ma-1379: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Ismāʿīl Abū Maʿmar narrated to me, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Idrīs narrated to us, ʿĀṣim ibn Kulayb narrated to us, from his father, he said: I was sitting with ʿAlī when a man wearing travelling clothes entered upon him and asked ʿAlī for permission while he was speaking to the people, so he was occupied from him. ʿAlī said: I entered upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while ʿĀʾishah was with him, and he said to me: “How will you be with a people of such and such?” I said: Allah and His Messenger know best. Then he repeated it, and I said: Allah and His Messenger know best. He said: “A people who will come out from the direction of the east; they recite the Qurʾān, it does not pass beyond their collarbones; they pass out of the religion as the arrow passes out of the game; among them is a man with a deformed hand, as if his hand were the breast of an Abyssinian woman.” I adjure you by Allah, did I inform you that he is among them? … and he mentioned the hadith in full.
items.ma-1380: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Sufyān ibn Wakīʿ ibn al-Jarrāḥ narrated to me, my father narrated to us, from his father, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū Ḥayyah al-Wādiʿī, from ʿAmr dhī Murr, he said: We saw ʿAlī ﵁ perform wuḍūʾ; he washed his hands, and rinsed his mouth and sniffed water into his nose—he said: And I doubt whether he mentioned three times for the rinsing and the sniffing or not—and he washed his face three times, and his hands three times, each one of them three times, and wiped his head and his ears; one of the two said: Then he took a handful and wiped his head with it, then stood up straight and drank the remainder of his wuḍūʾ [water], then said: Thus the Prophet ﷺ used to perform wuḍūʾ.
items.ma-1381: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Nāfiʿ ibn ʿUmar and ʿAbd al-Jabbār ibn Ward narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Mulaykah, he said: Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbayd Allāh said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “How excellent a household: ʿAbd Allāh, Abū ʿAbd Allāh, and Umm ʿAbd Allāh.”
items.ma-1382: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Nāfiʿ ibn ʿUmar and ʿAbd al-Jabbār ibn al-Ward narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Mulaykah, he said: Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbayd Allāh said: I do not narrate anything from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, except that I heard him say: “Indeed ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ is among the righteous of Quraysh.” He said: And ʿAbd al-Jabbār ibn Ward added, from Ibn Abī Mulaykah, from Ṭalḥah, he said: “How excellent a household: ʿAbd Allāh, Abū ʿAbd Allāh, and Umm ʿAbd Allāh.”
items.ma-1383: Muḥammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir narrated to me, from Muʿādh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿUthmān al-Taymī, from his father ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿUthmān, he said: We were with Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbayd Allāh while we were in iḥrām, and a bird was given as a gift to us, while Ṭalḥah was asleep. Some of us ate, and some of us abstained and did not eat. When Ṭalḥah woke up, he agreed with those who had eaten it, and said: We ate it with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-1384: Asbāṭ narrated to us, Muṭarrif narrated to us, from ʿĀmir, from Yaḥyā ibn Ṭalḥah, from his father, he said: ʿUmar saw Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbayd Allāh looking heavy, and said: What is the matter with you, O Abū so-and-so? Perhaps the emirate of your cousin has displeased you, O Abū so-and-so? He said: No, except that I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ a hadith, and nothing prevented me from asking him about it except [my] ability over it, until he died. I heard him say: “Indeed I know a word that no servant says at his death except that his complexion shines because of it, and Allah relieves his distress.” He said: ʿUmar said: Indeed I know what it is. He said: And what is it? He said: Do you know a word greater than the word that he commanded his uncle to say at death: There is no deity except Allah? Ṭalḥah said: You have spoken truly; it is—by Allah—it.
items.ma-1385: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Ismāʿīl, he said: Qays said: I saw Ṭalḥah, his hand paralysed; he had protected the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with it on the day of Uḥud.
items.ma-1386: Ibrāhīm ibn Mahdī narrated to us, Ṣāliḥ ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, from Muṭarrif, from al-Shaʿbī, from Yaḥyā ibn Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, from his father: that ʿUmar saw him sorrowful and said: What is the matter with you, O Abū Muḥammad, sorrowful? Perhaps the emirate of your cousin has displeased you?—meaning Abū Bakr. He said: No—and he praised Abū Bakr—but I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “A word that no servant says at his death except that Allah relieves his distress, and his complexion shines.” And nothing prevented me from asking him about it except [my] ability over it, until he died. ʿUmar said to him: Indeed I know it. Ṭalḥah said to him: And what is it? ʿUmar said to him: Do you know a word greater than the word he commanded his uncle to say: There is no deity except Allah? Ṭalḥah said: It is—by Allah—it.
items.ma-1387: ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Maʿn al-Ghifārī narrated to me, Dāwūd ibn Khālid ibn Dīnār informed me: that he and a man called Abū Yūsuf, of Banū Taym, passed by Rabīʿah ibn Abī ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. He said: Abū Yūsuf said to him: We find with others than you hadith that we do not find with you. He said: Indeed I have a great deal of hadith, but Rabīʿah ibn al-Hudayr said—and he used to keep close to Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbayd Allāh—that he never heard Ṭalḥah narrate from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ any hadith at all except one hadith. Rabīʿah ibn Abī ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: I said to him: And what is it? He said: Ṭalḥah said to me: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until, when we overlooked Ḥarrat Wāqim, he said: we drew near it, and behold, there were graves in a bend, and we said: O Messenger of Allah, are these the graves of our brothers? He said: “The graves of our companions.” Then we went out until we came to the graves of the martyrs. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “These are the graves of our brothers.”
items.ma-1388: ʿUmar ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, Simāk ibn Ḥarb narrated to us, from Mūsā ibn Ṭalḥah, from his father, he said: We used to pray while the animals passed in front of us, so we mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: “The like of the rear of a saddle, when it is in front of one of you, then what passes over it does not harm him.” ʿUmar said once: “in front of him.”
items.ma-1389: Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm, from Abū Salamah, he said: Two men from the people of Yemen stayed with Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbayd Allāh. One of them was killed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then the other remained after him for a year, then died on his bed. Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbayd Allāh was shown that the one who died on his bed had entered Paradise before the other by a while. Ṭalḥah mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “How long did he remain after him?” He said: A year. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “He prayed one thousand eight hundred prayers and fasted Ramaḍān.”
items.ma-1390: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, Mālik narrated to us, from his paternal uncle, from his father, that he heard Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbayd Allāh say: A Bedouin came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, what is Islam? He said: “Five prayers in a day and a night.” He said: Is there anything upon me besides them? He said: “No.” And he asked him about fasting, and he said: “The fasting of Ramaḍān.” He said: Is there anything upon me besides it? He said: “No.” He said: And he mentioned zakāh. He said: Is there anything upon me besides it? He said: “No.” He said: By Allah, I will not add to them, nor will I diminish from them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “He has succeeded if he is truthful.”
items.ma-1391: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from al-Zuhrī, from Mālik ibn Aws: I heard ʿUmar say to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, Ṭalḥah, al-Zubayr and Saʿd: I adjure you by Allah, by whom the heaven and the earth stand—and Sufyān once said: by whose permission they stand—do you know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “We are not inherited from; what we leave is ṣadaqah”? They said: O Allah, yes.
items.ma-1392: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir narrated to me, from Muʿādh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿUthmān al-Taymī, from his father, he said: We were with Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbayd Allāh while we were in iḥrām, and a bird was given as a gift to him, while Ṭalḥah was asleep. Some of us ate, and some of us abstained. When Ṭalḥah woke up, he agreed with those who had eaten it, and said: We ate it with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-1393: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from Mūsā ibn Ṭalḥah, from his father, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked: What screens the one who prays? He said: “The like of the rear of a saddle.”
items.ma-1394: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Isrāʾīl, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from Mūsā ibn Ṭalḥah, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ, the like of it.
items.ma-1395: Bahz and ʿAffān narrated to us; both said: Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from Simāk, from Mūsā ibn Ṭalḥah, from his father, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by some people at the tops of date-palms and said: “What are these doing?” They said: They are pollinating it; they put the male into the female. He said: “I do not think that avails anything.” They were informed of that and left it. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was informed, and he said: “If it benefits them, let them do it, for I only supposed a supposition, so do not hold me to account for supposition; but if I inform you about Allah ﷿ of something, then take it, for I will never lie about Allah in anything.”
items.ma-1396: Muḥammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, Mujammiʿ ibn Yaḥyā al-Anṣārī narrated to us, ʿUthmān ibn Mawhab narrated to us, from Mūsā ibn Ṭalḥah, from his father, he said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, how is the ṣalāh upon you? He said: “Say: O Allah, send ṣalāh upon Muḥammad and upon the family of Muḥammad, as You sent ṣalāh upon Ibrāhīm; indeed You are Ḥamīd, Majīd. And bless Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, as You blessed the family of Ibrāhīm; indeed You are Ḥamīd, Majīd.”
items.ma-1397: Abū ʿĀmir narrated to us, Sulaymān ibn Sufyān al-Madīnī narrated to us, Bilāl ibn Yaḥyā ibn Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbayd Allāh narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather: that the Prophet ﷺ, when he saw the new moon, would say: “O Allah, cause it to rise over us with good fortune and īmān, and safety and Islam. My Rabb and your Rabb is Allah.”
items.ma-1398: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Zāʾidah, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from Mūsā ibn Ṭalḥah, from his father, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “One of you places in front of himself the like of the rear of a saddle, then he prays.”
items.ma-1399: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Isrāʾīl informed us, from Simāk, that he heard Mūsā ibn Ṭalḥah narrating from his father, he said: I passed with the Prophet ﷺ through the date-palms of Madīnah, and he saw some people at the tops of the palms pollinating the palms, and he said: “What are these doing?” He said: They take from the male and put it in the female, pollinating with it. He said: “I do not think that avails anything.” That reached them, so they left it and came down from them, and that year [the palms] bore nothing. That reached the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: “It was only a supposition that I supposed. If it avails anything, then do it, for I am only a human being like you, and supposition errs and is right; but whatever I say to you: ‘Allah said,’ then I will never lie about Allah ﷿.”
items.ma-1400: Abū al-Naḍr narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, Simāk ibn Ḥarb narrated to us, from Mūsā ibn Ṭalḥah, and he mentioned it.
items.ma-1401:
Wakīʿ narrated to us, Ṭalḥah ibn Yaḥyā ibn Ṭalḥah narrated to me, from Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaddād: that a group of Banū ʿUdhrah, three [men], came to the Prophet ﷺ and became Muslims. He said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Who will suffice me in regard to them?” Ṭalḥah said: I will. He said: So they were with Ṭalḥah, and the Prophet ﷺ sent out an expedition, and one of them went out in it and was martyred. He said: Then he sent out another expedition, and another went out in it and was martyred. He said: Then the third died on his bed.
Ṭalḥah said: I saw these three who had been with me in Paradise, and I saw the one who died on his bed in front of them, and I saw the one who was martyred last next to him, and I saw the one who was martyred first as the last of them. He said: So something of that entered me. He said: So I came to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned that to him. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “And what did you find objectionable in that? No one is more excellent with Allah than a believer who is given long life in Islam, for his tasbīḥ, his takbīr and his tahlīl.”
items.ma-1402: Yazīd ibn ʿAbd Rabbih narrated to us, al-Ḥārith ibn ʿUbaydah narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mujabbir narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather: that ʿUthmān ﵁ looked down upon those who had besieged him and greeted them with salām, but they did not return it. ʿUthmān said: Is Ṭalḥah among the people? Ṭalḥah said: Yes. He said: Indeed we belong to Allah and indeed to Him we return! I greet a people among whom you are, and they do not return it? He said: I did return it. He said: This is not the return; I make you hear and you do not make me hear! O Ṭalḥah, I adjure you by Allah, did you hear the Prophet ﷺ say: “Nothing makes lawful the blood of a Muslim except one of three: that he disbelieves after his īmān, or commits zinā after being muḥṣan, or kills a soul and is killed for it”? He said: O Allah, yes. ʿUthmān said the takbīr, and said: By Allah, I have not denied Allah since I came to know Him, and I did not commit zinā in the jāhiliyyah nor in Islam; I left it in the jāhiliyyah out of distaste, and in Islam out of abstinence, and I have not killed a soul for which my killing would be lawful.
items.ma-1403:
Qutaybah ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, Bakr ibn Muḍar narrated to us, from Ibn al-Hād, from Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm, from Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbayd Allāh: that two men came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and their becoming Muslim was together, and one of them was more intense in striving than his companion. The one who strove among them went on an expedition and was martyred, then the other remained after him a year, then died.
Ṭalḥah said: I saw, in what a sleeper sees, as though I were at the door of Paradise, and behold, I was with the two of them, and one who came out from Paradise gave permission to the one who died last of the two, then came out and gave permission to the one who was martyred. Then the two returned to me and said to me: Return, for it is not yet time for you. So Ṭalḥah rose in the morning narrating it to the people, and they were amazed at that. That reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: “At which of that are you amazed?” They said: O Messenger of Allah, this one was more intense in striving, then was martyred in the way of Allah, and this one entered Paradise before him! He said: “Did this one not remain after him a year?” They said: Yes. He said: “And he reached Ramaḍān and fasted it?” They said: Yes. He said: “And he prayed so many prostrations in the year?” They said: Yes. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Then what is between the two of them is farther than what is between the heaven and the earth.”
items.ma-1404: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, Sālim ibn Abī Umayyah Abū al-Naḍr narrated to us, he said: An old man from Banū Tamīm sat with me in the mosque of al-Baṣrah, with a sheet of his in his hand—he said: and this was in the time of al-Ḥajjāj—and he said to me: O servant of Allah, do you think this document will avail me anything with this authority? He said: I said: And what is this document? He said: This is a document from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ which he wrote for us: that there be no transgression against us in our ṣadaqāt. He said: I said: No, by Allah, I do not think it will avail you anything; and how was the matter of this document? He said: I came to Madīnah with my father, while I was a young lad, with camels of ours that we were selling, and my father was a friend of Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbayd Allāh al-Taymī, so we stayed with him, and my father said to him: Go out with me and sell these camels of mine for me. He said: He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has forbidden that a town-dweller sell for a desert-dweller, but I will go out with you and sit, and you display your camels, and when I am satisfied with a man's fidelity and truthfulness among those who bargain with you, I will order you to sell to him. He said: So we went out to the market and stopped our mounts, and Ṭalḥah sat nearby; men bargained with us, until a man offered us what we were pleased with. My father said to him: Shall I conclude the sale with him? He said: Yes, I am satisfied for you with his fidelity, so conclude the sale with him. So we concluded the sale with him, and when we had received what was ours and finished our need, my father said to Ṭalḥah: Get for us a document from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: that there be no transgression against us in our ṣadaqāt. He said: He said: This is for you and for every Muslim. He said: Even so, I like to have with me a document from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: So he went out until he came with us to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and said: O Messenger of Allah, this man from the people of the desert is a friend of ours, and he would like you to write him a document that there be no transgression against him in his ṣadaqah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “This is for him and for every Muslim.” He said: O Messenger of Allah, he would like to have with him a document from you regarding that. He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote us this document.
items.ma-1405:
Sufyān narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr, from Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥāṭib, from Ibn al-Zubayr, from al-Zubayr ﵁, he said: When it was revealed: {Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, with your Rabb, will dispute} [al-Zumar: 31], al-Zubayr said: O Messenger of Allah, along with our disputes in the world? He said: “Yes.”
And when it was revealed: {Then you will surely be asked that Day about the delight} [al-Takāthur: 8], al-Zubayr said: O Messenger of Allah, about which delight will we be asked, when it is only—meaning: the two of them—the two black ones: dates and water? He said: “Indeed, that will come to be.”
items.ma-1406: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from al-Zuhrī, from Mālik ibn Aws: I heard ʿUmar say to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, Ṭalḥah, al-Zubayr and Saʿd: I adjure you by Allah, by whom the heaven and the earth stand—and Sufyān once said: by whose permission they stand—do you know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “We are not inherited from; what we leave is ṣadaqah”? He said: They said: O Allah, yes.
items.ma-1407: Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth narrated to us, from Hishām, from his father, from al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “For a man to carry a rope and gather firewood, then come and put it in the market and sell it, and thereby be made free of need and spend it on himself, is better for him than that he ask the people, whether they give him or refuse him.”
items.ma-1408: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, Hishām narrated to us, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr, from al-Zubayr, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ combined for me his two parents on the day of Uḥud.
items.ma-1409: Abū Usāmah narrated to us, Hishām informed us, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr, he said: On the day of the Trench, I and ʿUmar ibn Abī Salamah were in the stronghold in which were the women of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the stronghold of Ḥassān, and he would lift me and I would lift him, and when he lifted me I recognised my father as he passed on to Banū Qurayẓah, and he was fighting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of the Trench. And he said: “Who will go to Banū Qurayẓah and fight them?” And I said to him when he returned: O my father, I used to recognise you when you passed, going to Banū Qurayẓah. He said: O my son, by Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would indeed combine his two parents for me, ransoming me with them, saying: “May my father and my mother be your ransom.”
items.ma-1410: Yazīd ibn Hārūn narrated to us, Sulaymān—meaning al-Taymī—informed us, from Abū ʿUthmān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir, from al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām: that a man mounted [someone] upon a mare called Ghamrah or Ghamrāʾ, and he said: “Then he found a mare or a colt being sold, and it was attributed to that mare, so it was forbidden.”
items.ma-1411:
Yazīd narrated to us, Ibn Abī Dhiʾb informed us, from Muslim ibn Jundub, from al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām, he said: We used to pray the Friday prayer with the Prophet ﷺ, then depart and hasten to the ājām, and we would find only the extent of the place of our feet.
Yazīd said: Al-ājām: they are al-āṭām.
items.ma-1412: Yazīd ibn Hārūn narrated to us, Hishām informed us, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from Yaʿīsh ibn al-Walīd ibn Hishām. And Abū Muʿāwiyah Shaybān, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from Yaʿīsh ibn al-Walīd ibn Hishām, from al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There has crept to you the disease of the nations before you: envy and hatred; and hatred is the shaver—the shaver of the religion, not the shaver of hair. By the One in whose Yad is the soul of Muḥammad, you will not believe until you love one another. Shall I not inform you of something which, if you do it, you will love one another? Spread salām among yourselves.”
items.ma-1413: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Jāmiʿ ibn Shaddād, from ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr, from his father, he said: I said to al-Zubayr: Why do I not hear you narrate from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as I hear Ibn Masʿūd and so-and-so and so-and-so? He said: Indeed, I have not parted from him since I became Muslim, but I heard from him a word: “Whoever lies about me deliberately, let him take his seat in the Fire.”
items.ma-1414: Abū Saʿīd, the mawlā of Banū Hāshim, narrated to us, Shaddād—meaning Ibn Saʿīd—narrated to us, Ghaylān ibn Jarīr narrated to us, from Muṭarrif, he said: We said to al-Zubayr: O Abū ʿAbd Allāh, what brought you? You lost the caliph until he was killed, then you came to demand [redress] for his blood? Al-Zubayr said: We used to recite it in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abū Bakr, ʿUmar and ʿUthmān: {And beware a trial that will not strike only those among you who have wronged} [al-Anfāl: 25], and we did not think that we were its people until it occurred among us where it occurred.
items.ma-1415: Muḥammad ibn Kunāsah narrated to us, Hishām ibn ʿUrwah narrated to us, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from al-Zubayr, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Change the grey hair, and do not imitate the Jews.”
items.ma-1416: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith, of the people of Makkah, a Makhzūmī, narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Insān narrated to me—he said: and he praised him well—from his father, from ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, from al-Zubayr, he said: We came back with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from Liyyah, until, when we were at al-Sidrah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stopped at the edge of al-Qarn al-Aswad opposite it, and faced Nakhib with his sight—meaning a valley—and stopped until all the people had come together. Then he said: “Indeed the game of Wajj and its thorny trees is a ḥaram, made inviolable for Allah.” And that was before his encamping at al-Ṭāʾif and his besieging Thaqīf.
items.ma-1417: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbbād ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr narrated to me, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr, from al-Zubayr, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say on that day: “Ṭalḥah has made [it] obligatory,” when he did for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ what he did—meaning when Ṭalḥah knelt for him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ climbed upon his back.
items.ma-1418: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd al-Hāshimī narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān—meaning Ibn Abī al-Zinād—informed us, from Hishām, from ʿUrwah, he said: My father al-Zubayr informed me: that on the day of Uḥud a woman came running, until when she was about to look down upon the slain, he said: the Prophet ﷺ disliked that she see them, and said: “The woman! The woman!” Al-Zubayr said: I discerned that she was my mother Ṣafiyyah. He said: So I went out running to her and reached her before she arrived at the slain. He said: She struck me on my chest—and she was a strong woman—and said: Away with you! You have no land. He said: I said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has insisted upon you. He said: So she stopped, and took out two garments she had with her, and said: These are two garments I brought for my brother Ḥamzah, for news of his killing has reached me, so shroud him in them. He said: So we came with the two garments to shroud Ḥamzah in them, and beside him was a man of the Anṣār, slain, who had been done to as had been done to Ḥamzah. He said: And we felt shame and embarrassment that Ḥamzah be shrouded in two garments while the Anṣārī had no shroud, so we said: A garment for Ḥamzah and a garment for the Anṣārī. We estimated them, and one of them was larger than the other, so we drew lots between them, and we shrouded each of them in the garment that fell to him.
items.ma-1419:
Abū al-Yamān narrated to us, Shuʿayb informed us, from al-Zuhrī, he said: ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me: that al-Zubayr used to narrate: that he disputed, before the Prophet ﷺ, with a man of the Anṣār who had been present at Badr, concerning the channels of al-Ḥarrah, from which both of them irrigated, and the Prophet ﷺ said to al-Zubayr: “Irrigate, then send [water] to your neighbour.” The Anṣārī became angry and said: O Messenger of Allah, [is it] because he was the son of your paternal aunt! The face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ changed colour, then he said to al-Zubayr: “Irrigate, then hold back the water until it returns to the wall.” So the Prophet ﷺ then secured fully for al-Zubayr his right; and the Prophet ﷺ had before that advised al-Zubayr with an opinion in which he intended ease for him and for the Anṣārī; but when the Anṣārī angered the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ secured fully for al-Zubayr his right in explicit judgment.
ʿUrwah said: Al-Zubayr said: By Allah, I think this verse was revealed only concerning that: {But no, by your Rabb, they will not believe until they make you judge in what is in dispute among them, then find within themselves no discomfort from what you have judged, and submit in full submission} [al-Nisāʾ: 65].
items.ma-1420: Yazīd ibn ʿAbd Rabbih narrated to us, Baqiyyah ibn al-Walīd narrated to us, Jubayr ibn ʿAmr al-Qurashī narrated to me, Abū Saʿd al-Anṣārī narrated to me, from Abū Yaḥyā, the mawlā of the family of al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām, from al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The lands are the lands of Allah, and the servants are the servants of Allah; so wherever you find good, settle.”
items.ma-1421: Yazīd narrated to us, Baqiyyah ibn al-Walīd narrated to us, Jubayr ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, from Abū Saʿd al-Anṣārī, from Abū Yaḥyā, the mawlā of the family of al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām, from al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while he was at ʿArafah, reciting this verse: {Allah has borne witness that there is no deity except Him, and the angels and those of knowledge, standing in justice. There is no deity except Him, al-ʿAzīz, al-Ḥakīm} [Āl ʿImrān: 18]: “And I, to that, am among the witnesses, O my Rabb.”
items.ma-1422: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAṭāʾ ibn Ibrāhīm, the mawlā of al-Zubayr, narrated to me, from his mother and his grandmother Umm ʿAṭāʾ, the two said: By Allah, it is as though we are looking at al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām when he came to us on a white mule of his and said: O Umm ʿAṭāʾ, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has forbidden the Muslims to eat from the meat of their nusuk beyond three. She said: I said: [May] my father [be your ransom]; so what do we do with what has been given as a gift to us? He said: As for what has been given as a gift to you, then your affair is with it.
items.ma-1423: ʿAttāb ibn Ziyād narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh—meaning Ibn al-Mubārak—narrated to us, Hishām ibn ʿUrwah informed us, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr, he said: On the day of al-Aḥzāb, I and ʿUmar ibn Abī Salamah were placed with the women, and I looked, and behold, I saw al-Zubayr on his horse going back and forth to Banū Qurayẓah, twice or three times. When he returned I said: O my father, I saw you going back and forth. He said: And did you see me, O my son? I said: Yes. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Who will go to Banū Qurayẓah and bring me news of them?” So I went, and when I returned, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ combined his two parents for me and said: “May my father and my mother be your ransom.”
items.ma-1424: ʿAttāb narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUqbah—he is ʿAbd Allāh ibn Lahīʿah ibn ʿUqbah—informed us, Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb narrated to me, from one who heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah ibn Abī Burdah say: I heard Sufyān ibn Wahb al-Khawlānī say: When we conquered Egypt without a treaty, al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām stood and said: O ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, divide it. ʿAmr said: I will not divide it. Al-Zubayr said: By Allah, you will surely divide it as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ divided Khaybar. ʿAmr said: By Allah, I will not divide it until I write to the Commander of the Believers. So he wrote to ʿUmar ﵁, and ʿUmar wrote to him: Leave it as it is, until the offspring of offspring go out on campaign from it.
items.ma-1425: ʿAttāb narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Fulayḥ ibn Muḥammad informed us, from al-Mundhir ibn al-Zubayr, from his father: that the Prophet ﷺ gave al-Zubayr a share, and his mother a share, and his horse two shares.
items.ma-1426: ʿAffān narrated to us, al-Mubārak narrated to us, al-Ḥasan narrated to us, he said: A man came to al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām and said: Shall I not kill ʿAlī for you? He said: No, and how would you kill him when he has troops with him? He said: I will catch up with him and assassinate him. He said: No. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed īmān has shackled assassination; a believer does not assassinate.”
items.ma-1427: Yazīd ibn Hārūn narrated to us, Mubārak ibn Fuḍālah informed us, al-Ḥasan narrated to us, he said: A man came to al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām and said: Shall I not kill ʿAlī for you? He said: And how can you kill him when the people are with him? And he mentioned its meaning.
items.ma-1428: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Jāmiʿ ibn Shaddād, from ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr, from his father, he said: I said to my father al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām: What is the matter that you do not narrate from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? He said: I have not parted from him since I became Muslim, but I heard a word from him; I heard him say: “Whoever lies about me, let him take his seat in the Fire.”
items.ma-1430: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Ḥarb ibn Shaddād narrated to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, that Yaʿīsh ibn al-Walīd narrated to him, that a mawlā of the family of al-Zubayr narrated to him: that al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām narrated to him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There has crept to you the disease of the nations before you: envy and hatred; and hatred is the shaver—I do not say that it shaves hair, but it shaves the religion. By the One in whose Yad is my soul—or: by the One in whose Yad is the soul of Muḥammad—you will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another. Shall I not inform you of what will establish that for you? Spread salām among yourselves.”
items.ma-1431: Abū ʿĀmir narrated to us, ʿAlī ibn al-Mubārak narrated to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from Yaʿīsh ibn al-Walīd, that a mawlā of the family of al-Zubayr narrated to him: that al-Zubayr narrated to him, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “There has crept to you …” and he mentioned it.
items.ma-1432: Ibrāhīm ibn Khālid narrated to us, Rabāḥ narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from Yaʿīsh ibn al-Walīd ibn Hishām, from a mawlā of the family of al-Zubayr: [[that al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām narrated to him,]] (*) that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There has crept to you …” and he mentioned it.
items.ma-1433: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Ayyūb narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan, he said: A man said to al-Zubayr: Shall I not kill ʿAlī for you? He said: How would you kill him? He said: I would assassinate him. He said: No. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Īmān has shackled assassination; a believer does not assassinate.”
items.ma-1434: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, Muḥammad—meaning Ibn ʿAmr—narrated to us, from Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥāṭib, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr, from al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām, he said: When this sūrah was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: {Indeed you will die, and indeed they will die. Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, with your Rabb, will dispute}, al-Zubayr said: O Messenger of Allah, will what was between us in the world be repeated against us, along with the particular sins? He said: “Yes, it will surely be repeated against you until to every possessor of a right his right is rendered.” Al-Zubayr said: By Allah, the matter is indeed severe.
items.ma-1435:
Sufyān narrated to us: ʿAmr said: And I heard ʿIkrimah: {And when We directed to you}, and it was read to Sufyān: from al-Zubayr: {a group of the jinn, listening to the Qurʾān} [al-Aḥqāf: 29], he said: At Nakhlah, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was praying the late ʿIshāʾ: {They were almost upon him in dense layers} [al-Jinn: 19].
Sufyān said: Al-libad: some of them upon others, like the libad, some of it upon others.
items.ma-1436: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Ibn Abī Dhiʾb narrated to us, Muslim ibn Jundub narrated to us, one who heard al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām say narrated to me: We used to pray the Friday prayer with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then hasten, and we would find of the shade only the place of our feet. Or he said: we would not find of the shade the place of our feet.
items.ma-1437: Kathīr ibn Hishām narrated to us, Hishām narrated to us, from Abū al-Zubayr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salimah—or Salamah; Kathīr said: and my memory is Salimah—from ʿAlī, or from al-Zubayr, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to address us and remind us of the days of Allah, until we would recognise that in his face, as though he were the warner of a people to whom the matter would come in the morning; and when he was recently in contact with Jibrīl he would not smile, laughing, until it lifted from him.
items.ma-1438: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Jarīr narrated to us, he said: I heard al-Ḥasan say: Al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām said: This verse was revealed while we were many with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: {And beware a trial that will not strike only those among you who have wronged} [al-Anfāl: 25], and we began to say: What is this trial? And we did not perceive that it would occur where it occurred.
items.ma-1439: ʿAffān narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Wārith narrated to us, Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated to us, he said: I asked Ṭāwūs about a man who threw at the jamrah with six pebbles, and he said: Let him feed a handful of food. He said: Then I met Mujāhid and asked him, and I mentioned to him the statement of Ṭāwūs, and he said: May Allah have mercy on Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān; has the statement of Saʿd ibn Mālik not reached him? He said: We threw at the jamarāt—or the jamrah—in our Ḥajj with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then we sat discussing, and among us were those who said: I threw with six, and among us were those who said: I threw with seven, and among us were those who said: I threw with eight, and among us were those who said: I threw with nine, and they did not see any harm in that.
items.ma-1440: ʿAffān narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, Ayyūb narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ḥimyarī, from three of the sons of Saʿd, from Saʿd: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon him visiting him while he was ill, and he was in Makkah, and he said: O Messenger of Allah, I fear that I will die in the land from which I emigrated, as Saʿd ibn Khawlah died, so supplicate Allah to cure me. He said: “O Allah, cure Saʿd; O Allah, cure Saʿd; O Allah, cure Saʿd.” He said: O Messenger of Allah, I have much wealth and I have no heir except a daughter; may I bequeath all my wealth? He said: “No.” He said: May I bequeath two-thirds of it? He said: “No.” He said: May I bequeath half of it? He said: “No.” He said: May I bequeath a third? He said: “A third—and a third is a lot. Indeed your spending from your wealth is ṣadaqah for you, and your spending on your dependants is ṣadaqah for you, and your spending on your family is ṣadaqah for you; and that you leave your family in livelihood—or he said: in good—is better than that you leave them begging from the people.”
items.ma-1441: Abū Bakr al-Ḥanafī ʿAbd al-Kabīr ibn ʿAbd al-Majīd narrated to us, Bukayr ibn Mismār narrated to us, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd: that his brother ʿUmar went to Saʿd, who was with some sheep of his outside Madīnah. When Saʿd saw him, he said: I seek refuge in Allah from the evil of this rider. When he came to him he said: O my father, are you content to be a Bedouin among your sheep while the people dispute over kingship in Madīnah? So Saʿd struck ʿUmar's chest and said: Be silent; I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Indeed Allah ﷿ Yuḥibbu the servant who is God-fearing, wealthy, and hidden.”
