items.ma-1442: Abū ʿĀmir narrated to us, Fulayḥ narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān—meaning Ibn Maʿmar—he said: ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd narrated to ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, while he was governor over Madīnah: that Saʿd said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever eats seven dates of ʿajwah from between the two lava fields of Madīnah on an empty stomach, nothing will harm him that day until evening.” Fulayḥ said: And I think he said: “And if he eats them when evening comes, nothing will harm him until morning.” ʿUmar said: Look, O ʿĀmir, at what you narrate from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ! He said: I bear witness that I have not lied about Saʿd, and Saʿd has not lied about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-1443: Abū ʿĀmir narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Muḥammad ibn Saʿd, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd: that Saʿd rode to his palace at al-ʿAqīq and found a boy beating down leaves from a tree—or cutting it—and he stripped him. When Saʿd returned, the family of the boy came to him and spoke to him that he return what he had taken from their boy. He said: Allah forbid that I return something that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ granted me as spoil. And he refused to return it to them.
items.ma-1444: Rawḥ—he dictated it to us in Baghdād—narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥumayd narrated to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Muḥammad ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, from his father, from his grandfather Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Part of the happiness of the son of Ādam is his istikhārah of Allah, and part of the happiness of the son of Ādam is his contentment with what Allah decreed; and part of the wretchedness of the son of Ādam is his leaving istikhārah of Allah, and part of the wretchedness of the son of Ādam is his discontent with what Allah ﷿ decreed.”
items.ma-1445: Rawḥ narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥumayd narrated to us, Ismāʿīl ibn Muḥammad ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Three things are of the happiness of the son of Ādam, and three are of the wretchedness of the son of Ādam: of the happiness of the son of Ādam are the righteous woman, the righteous dwelling, and the righteous mount; and of the wretchedness of the son of Ādam are the evil woman, the evil dwelling, and the evil mount.”
items.ma-1446: Abū Saʿīd, the mawlā of Banū Hāshim, narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, Bukayr ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ashajj narrated to us, that he heard Ḥusayn ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrating: that he heard Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “There will be a trial in which the one sitting is better than the one standing, the one standing in it is better than the one walking, and the one walking in it will be better than the one running.” He said: And I think he said: “And the one lying down in it is better than the one sitting.”
items.ma-1447: Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from a nephew of Saʿd, from Saʿd, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Banū Nājiyah: “I am of them, and they are of me.”
items.ma-1448: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, and he mentioned the hadith with a story in it, and the nephew of Saʿd ibn Mālik said: They mentioned Banū Nājiyah in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: “They are a clan from me.” And Saʿd is not mentioned in it.
items.ma-1449: Ḥasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb narrated to us, from Dāwūd ibn ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “If what a fingernail could carry of what is in Paradise were to appear, what is between the horizons of the heavens and the earth would be adorned for it; and if a man from the people of Paradise were to look out and his bracelet appeared, its light would efface the light of the sun, as the sun effaces the light of the stars.”
items.ma-1450: Abū Salamah al-Khuzāʿī narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar informed us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Muḥammad, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd, from Saʿd, he said: Dig a laḥd for me, and stand the bricks upon me upright, as was done for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-1451: Ibn Mahdī narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd, and he mentioned the like of it. And Abū Saʿīd concurred with him on ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd, as al-Khuzāʿī said.
items.ma-1452: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd al-Hāshimī narrated to us, Ismāʿīl—meaning Ibn Jaʿfar—narrated to us, Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah informed me, from Abū al-Naḍr, the mawlā of ʿUmar ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Maʿmar, from Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, that the Prophet ﷺ said concerning wiping over the two khuffs: “There is no harm in that.”
items.ma-1453: Isḥāq ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us, Mālik—meaning Ibn Anas—narrated to me, from Sālim Abū al-Naḍr, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, he said: I heard my father say: I did not hear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say of any living person walking among the people: “He is in Paradise,” except of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām.
items.ma-1454: Hushaym narrated to us, Khālid informed us, from Abū ʿUthmān, he said: When Ziyād was claimed [as a son], I met Abū Bakrah and said: What is this that you have done? I heard Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ say: My ear heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was saying: “Whoever claims a father in Islam other than his father, while knowing that he is other than his father, Paradise is forbidden to him.” Abū Bakrah said: And I heard it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-1455: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, from Wuhayb, from Abū Wāqid al-Laythī, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd, from his father, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “The hand is cut off for the price of a shield.”
items.ma-1456: Rawḥ narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥumayd al-Madanī narrated to us, Ismāʿīl ibn Muḥammad ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered me to call out during the days of Minā: Indeed they are days of eating and drinking, so there is no fasting in them—meaning the days of tashrīq.
items.ma-1457: Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, al-Fuḍayl ibn Sulaymān narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Abī Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq ibn Sālim, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd, from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, he said: What is between the two lava fields of Madīnah is sacred; the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made it sacred, as Ibrāhīm made Makkah sacred. O Allah, make the blessing in it two blessings, and bless them in their ṣāʿ and their mudd.
items.ma-1458: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, ʿĀṣim ibn Bahdalah informed us, from Muṣʿab ibn Saʿd, from his father: that a large bowl was brought to the Prophet ﷺ, and he ate from it, and a remainder was left over. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “A man from the people of Paradise will come from this mountain pass; he will eat this remainder.” Saʿd said: I had left my brother ʿUmayr performing wuḍūʾ. He said: So I said: It is ʿUmayr. He said: Then ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām came and ate it.
items.ma-1459: ʿAffān narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah narrated to us, he said: I heard Abū al-Naḍr narrating from Abū Salamah, from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ a hadith that he attributed to the Prophet ﷺ: concerning wuḍūʾ upon the two khuffs: that there is no harm in it.
items.ma-1460: ʿAffān narrated to us, Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim narrated to us, Yaʿlā ibn Ḥakīm narrated to me, from Sulaymān ibn Abī ʿAbd Allāh, he said: I saw Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ seize a man hunting in the ḥaram of Madīnah, which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made sacred, and he stripped him of his clothes. His mawlās came, and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made this ḥaram sacred, and said: “Whoever you see hunting anything in it, then his spoils are for him.” So I will not return to you a provision that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave me to eat; but if you wish, I will give you its price. And ʿAffān once said: If you wish that I give you its price, I will give it to you.
items.ma-1461: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥuṣayn narrated to me, that he narrated from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ: that he used to pray the late ʿIshāʾ in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then pray witr with one rakʿah, not adding to it. He said: It was said to him: Do you pray witr with one, not adding to it, O Abū Isḥāq? He would say: Yes, I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “The one who does not sleep until he has prayed witr is prudent.”
items.ma-1462:
Ismāʿīl ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, Yūnus ibn Abī Isḥāq al-Hamdānī narrated to us, Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn Saʿd narrated to us, my father Muḥammad narrated to me, from his father Saʿd, he said: I passed by ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān in the mosque and greeted him with salām, and he filled his eyes with me, then did not return the salām to me. So I came to the Commander of the Believers ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb and said: O Commander of the Believers, has something happened in Islam?—twice. He said: No, and what is that? I said: No, except that I passed by ʿUthmān just now in the mosque and greeted him with salām, and he filled his eyes with me, then did not return the salām to me. He said: So ʿUmar sent for ʿUthmān and called him, and said: What prevented you from returning the salām to your brother? ʿUthmān said: I did not do [so]. Saʿd said: I said: Yes, you did. He said: Until he swore and I swore. He said: Then ʿUthmān remembered and said: Yes, and I seek forgiveness of Allah and repent to Him; you passed by me just now while I was speaking to myself of a word that I had heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; no, by Allah, I never remember it except that a covering comes over my sight and my heart.
He said: Saʿd said: And I will inform you of it: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned to us the first supplication, then a Bedouin came and occupied him until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood, and I followed him; and when I feared that he would precede me to his dwelling, I struck the ground with my foot, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned to me and said: “Who is this? Abū Isḥāq?” I said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah. He said: “What then?” I said: No, by Allah, except that you mentioned to us the first supplication, then this Bedouin came and occupied you. He said: “Yes: the supplication of Dhū al-Nūn when he was in the belly of the whale: {There is no deity except You; glory be to You; indeed I was among the wrongdoers} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 87]. For no Muslim ever supplicates his Rabb with it in anything except that He answers him.”
items.ma-1463: Abū Saʿīd, the mawlā of Banū Hāshim, narrated to us, Sulaymān ibn Bilāl narrated to us, al-Juʿayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from ʿĀʾishah bint Saʿd, from her father: that ʿAlī went out with the Prophet ﷺ until he came to Thaniyyat al-Wadāʿ, and ʿAlī was weeping, saying: Are you leaving me behind with those left behind? He said: “Are you not pleased to be to me in the position of Hārūn to Mūsā, except prophethood?”
items.ma-1464:
ʿIṣām ibn Khālid narrated to us, Abū Bakr—meaning Ibn Abī Maryam—narrated to me, from Rāshid ibn Saʿd, from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he used to say: “My ummah will not be incapable with my Rabb that He delay it half a day.”
And I asked Rāshid: Has it reached you what this half a day is? He said: Five hundred years.
items.ma-1465: Abū al-Yamān narrated to us, Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, from Rāshid ibn Saʿd, from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “Indeed I hope that my ummah will not be incapable with my Rabb that He delay them half a day.” It was said to Saʿd: And how much is half a day? He said: Five hundred years.
items.ma-1466: Abū al-Yamān narrated to us, Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, from Rāshid ibn Saʿd, from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about this verse: {He is al-Qādir to send upon you a punishment from above you or from beneath your feet} [al-Anʿām: 65], and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed it will be, and its taʾwīl has not yet come.”
items.ma-1467: ʿAlī ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh informed us, Ibn Lahīʿah informed us, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, from Dāwūd ibn ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “If what a fingernail could carry of what is in Paradise were to appear, what is between the horizons of the heavens and the earth would be adorned for it; and if a man of the people of Paradise were to look out and his bracelets appeared, his light would efface the light of the sun, as the sun effaces the light of the stars.”
items.ma-1468: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd al-Hāshimī narrated to us, Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd informed us, from his father, from his father, from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, he said: I saw, on the right of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and on his left on the day of Uḥud, two men wearing white garments fighting on his behalf with the fiercest fighting; I had not seen them before, nor after.
items.ma-1469: Isḥāq ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us, Ibrāhīm—meaning Ibn Saʿd—narrated to me, from his father, from Muʿādh al-Taymī, he said: I heard Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ say: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “Two prayers after which no prayer is prayed: the Ṣubḥ until the sun rises, and the ʿAṣr until the sun sets.”
items.ma-1470: Yūnus narrated it to us, Ibrāhīm narrated to us, from his father, from a man of Banū Taym called Muʿādh, from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he mentioned the like of it.
items.ma-1471: Yaʿqūb and Saʿd narrated to us; both said: My father narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather—Saʿd said: Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān—he said: I heard Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ say: I saw, on the right of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and on his left on the day of Uḥud, two men wearing white garments fighting on his behalf with the fiercest fighting; I had not seen them before, nor after.
items.ma-1472:
Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ṣāliḥ: Ibn Shihāb said: ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd informed me that Muḥammad ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ informed him that his father Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ said: ʿUmar asked permission to enter upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while women of Quraysh were with him, speaking with him and asking him for more, their voices raised. When he asked permission, they stood up, hurrying to the screen. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ permitted him—meaning: and he entered—while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was laughing. ʿUmar said: May Allah make your tooth laugh, O Messenger of Allah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I was amazed at these women who were with me; when they heard your voice, they hurried to the screen.” ʿUmar said: But you, O Messenger of Allah, were more deserving that they fear you. Then ʿUmar said: O enemies of themselves, do you fear me and not fear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? They said: Yes, you are harsher and sterner than the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “By the One in whose Yad is my soul, Satan has never met you walking along a path except that he took a path other than your path.”
ʿAbd Allāh said: My father said: And Yaʿqūb said: I cannot count how many times I heard him say: Ṣāliḥ narrated to us from Ibn Shihāb.
items.ma-1473: Yaʿqūb and Saʿd narrated to us; both said: My father narrated to us, from Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn Shihāb, Muḥammad ibn Abī Sufyān ibn Jāriyah narrated to me, that Yūsuf ibn al-Ḥakam Abū al-Ḥajjāj informed him that Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever intends the humiliation of Quraysh, Allah ﷿ humiliates him.”
items.ma-1474: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from al-Jaʿd ibn Aws, he said: ʿĀʾishah bint Saʿd narrated to me, she said: Saʿd said: I fell ill with an illness of mine in Makkah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon me visiting me. He said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, I have left wealth, and I have only one daughter; may I bequeath two-thirds of my wealth and leave a third for her? He said: “No.” He said: May I bequeath half and leave half for her? He said: “No.” He said: May I bequeath a third and leave two-thirds for her? He said: “A third—and a third is a lot,” three times. He said: Then he put his hand on my forehead and wiped my face, my chest and my belly, and said: “O Allah, cure Saʿd, and complete for him his emigration.” And it still appears to me that I feel the coolness of his hand upon my liver until this hour.
items.ma-1475: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAjlān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Salamah: that Saʿd heard a man say: Labbayka, Dhā al-Maʿārij. He said: Indeed He is Dhū al-Maʿārij, but we, with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, did not say that.
items.ma-1476: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Saʿīd ibn Ḥassān al-Makhzūmī narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Mulaykah, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Nahīk, from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “He is not of us who does not chant with the Qurʾān.” Wakīʿ said: meaning: he becomes free of need through it.
items.ma-1477: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Usāmah ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Labībah, from Saʿd ibn Mālik, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The best dhikr is the hidden one, and the best provision is what suffices.”
items.ma-1478: ʿAlī ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, from Ibn al-Mubārak, from Usāmah, he said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān informed me that Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Labībah informed him. My father said: And Yaḥyā—meaning al-Qaṭṭān—said: Ibn Labībah also, except that he said: from Usāmah, he said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Labībah narrated to me.
items.ma-1479: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Hishām narrated to us, from his father, from Saʿd: that the Prophet ﷺ entered upon him visiting him while he was ill, and he said: O Messenger of Allah, shall I not bequeath all my wealth? He said: “No.” He said: Then half? He said: “No.” He said: Then a third? He said: “A third—and a third is great, or a lot.”
items.ma-1480: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd, from his father, that the Prophet ﷺ said to him: “Indeed whatever spending you spend on your family, you are rewarded for it, even the morsel that you raise to the mouth of your wife.”
items.ma-1481: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd, from Muṣʿab ibn Saʿd, from his father, he said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, which of the people is most severe in affliction? He said: “The prophets, then the righteous, then the next best and the next best of the people. A man is afflicted according to his religion; if there is firmness in his religion, his affliction is increased, and if there is softness in his religion, it is lightened for him. And affliction continues with the servant until he walks upon the surface of the earth with no sin upon him.”
items.ma-1482: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Misʿar and Sufyān narrated to us, from Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm—Sufyān said: from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd, and Misʿar said: from some of the family of Saʿd—from Saʿd: that the Prophet ﷺ entered upon him visiting him while he was ill in Makkah, and I said: O Messenger of Allah, shall I bequeath all my wealth? He said: “No.” I said: Then half? He said: “No.” I said: Then a third? He said: “A third—and a third is great—or a lot. That you leave your heir wealthy is better than that you leave him poor, begging from the people. And whatever spending you spend on your family, you are rewarded for it, even the morsel that you raise to the mouth of your wife.” He said: And he had no one at that time except a daughter. Then Saʿd mentioned the emigration, and he said: “May Allah have mercy on Ibn ʿAfrāʾ. And perhaps Allah will raise you up so that a people benefit from you and others are harmed by you.”
items.ma-1483: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Ziyād ibn Mikhrāq, he said: I heard Abū ʿAbāyah, from a mawlā of Saʿd: that Saʿd heard a son of his supplicating, saying: O Allah, I ask You for Paradise and its delight and its brocade, and the like of this, and I seek refuge in You from the Fire and its chains and its shackles. He said: You have asked Allah for much good, and sought refuge in Allah from much evil. And I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “There will be a people who transgress in supplication,” and he recited this verse: {Call upon your Rabb in humility and in secret; indeed He lā yuḥibbu the transgressors} [al-Aʿrāf: 55]. And it is enough for you to say: O Allah, I ask You for Paradise and whatever brings one near to it of word or deed, and I seek refuge in You from the Fire and whatever brings one near to it of word or deed.
items.ma-1484: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī and Abū Saʿīd narrated to us; both said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Muḥammad—Abū Saʿīd said: he said: Ismāʿīl ibn Muḥammad narrated to us—from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd, from his father, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was—and Abū Saʿīd said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam—giving the taslīm to his right until the whiteness of his cheek was seen, and to his left until the whiteness of his cheek was seen.
items.ma-1485: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Hammām, from Qatādah, from Yūnus ibn Jubayr, from Muḥammad ibn Saʿd, from his father: that the Prophet ﷺ entered upon him in Makkah while he was ill, and he said: Indeed I have only one daughter; may I bequeath all my wealth? The Prophet ﷺ said: “No.” He said: May I bequeath half of it? The Prophet ﷺ said: “No.” He said: May I bequeath a third of it? He said: “A third—and a third is great.”
items.ma-1486: Bahz narrated to us, Hammām narrated to us, Qatādah narrated to us, from Abū Ghalāb, from Muḥammad ibn Saʿd ibn Mālik, from his father: that the Prophet ﷺ entered upon him … and he mentioned the like of it. And ʿAbd al-Ṣamad said: a lot, meaning: the third.
items.ma-1487: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, the meaning being the same; he said: Sufyān informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-ʿAyzār ibn Ḥurayth, from ʿUmar ibn Saʿd, from his father, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I am amazed at the decree of Allah ﷿ for the believer: if good befalls him, he praises his Rabb and is thankful; and if a calamity befalls him, he praises his Rabb and is patient. The believer is rewarded in everything, even in the morsel he raises to the mouth of his wife.”
items.ma-1488: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Saʿd, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd, from his father, he said: The Prophet ﷺ came to him visiting him while he was in Makkah, and he disliked to die in the land from which he had emigrated. The Prophet ﷺ said: “May Allah have mercy on Saʿd ibn ʿAfrāʾ, may Allah have mercy on Saʿd ibn ʿAfrāʾ.” And he had only one daughter. He said: O Messenger of Allah, shall I bequeath all my wealth? He said: “No.” He said: Then half? He said: “No.” He said: Then a third? He said: “A third—and a third is a lot. Indeed that you leave your heirs wealthy is better than that you leave them dependent, begging from the people with their hands; and indeed whatever spending you spend, it is ṣadaqah, even the morsel that you raise to the mouth of your wife. And perhaps Allah will raise you, so that people benefit from you and others are harmed by you.”
items.ma-1489: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd, he said: Dig a laḥd for me, and set up [the bricks] over me, as was done for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-1490:
ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād—meaning Ibn Salamah—narrated to us, ʿAlī ibn Zayd informed us, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, he said: I said to Saʿd ibn Mālik: I want to ask you about a hadith, and I am in awe of you to ask you about it. He said: Do not do that, O son of my brother; when you know that I have knowledge, ask me about it and do not be in awe of me. He said: I said: The statement of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to ʿAlī when he left him behind in Madīnah in the expedition of Tabūk. Saʿd said: The Prophet ﷺ left ʿAlī behind in Madīnah in the expedition of Tabūk, and he said: O Messenger of Allah, are you leaving me behind among those left behind, among the women and the children? He said: “Are you not pleased to be to me in the position of Hārūn to Mūsā?” He said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah. He said: Then ʿAlī turned away hurriedly, as if I am looking at the dust of his feet rising.
And Ḥammād said: So ʿAlī returned hurriedly.
items.ma-1491: ʿAffān narrated to us, Salīm ibn Ḥayyān narrated to us, ʿIkrimah ibn Khālid narrated to me, Yaḥyā ibn Saʿd narrated to me, from his father, he said: The plague was mentioned in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: “A scourge with which those before you were afflicted. So when it is in a land, do not enter it; and when it is in it while you are in it, do not leave it.”
items.ma-1492: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-ʿAyzār ibn Ḥurayth, from ʿUmar ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, from his father, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I am amazed at the believer: if good befalls him, he praises Allah and is thankful, and if a calamity befalls him, he praises Allah and is patient. So the believer is rewarded in all his affairs, until he is rewarded for the morsel that he raises to the mouth of his wife.”
items.ma-1493: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Rāshid narrated to us, from Makḥūl, from Saʿd ibn Mālik, he said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, a man who is the defender of the people—is his share and the share of another equal? He said: “May your mother be bereaved of you, O son of Umm Saʿd! Are you provided for and given victory except through your weak ones?”
items.ma-1494: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim ibn Bahdalah, he said: I heard Muṣʿab ibn Saʿd narrating from Saʿd, he said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: Which of the people is most severe in affliction? He said: “The prophets, then the next best and the next best. A man is afflicted according to his religion: if he is soft in religion, he is afflicted according to that, and if he is firm in religion, he is afflicted according to that. He said: And afflictions continue with the man until he walks on the earth with no sin upon him.”
items.ma-1495: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, he said: Saʿd ibn Mālik said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ combined for me his two parents on the day of Uḥud.
items.ma-1496: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh, the mawlā of Juhaynah, he said: I heard Muṣʿab ibn Saʿd narrating from Saʿd, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: “Is one of you unable to earn a thousand good deeds in a day?” He said: And who can bear that? He said: “He glorifies a hundred glorifications, so a thousand good deeds are written for him, and a thousand evil deeds are erased from him.”
items.ma-1497: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal, he said: I heard Abū ʿUthmān say: I heard Saʿd—and he was the first to shoot an arrow in the way of Allah—and Abū Bakrah—who had scaled the fortress of al-Ṭāʾif with some people, then came to the Prophet ﷺ, and the two said: We heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “Whoever claims a father other than his father, while knowing that he is other than his father, Paradise is forbidden to him.”
items.ma-1498: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Ismāʿīl, he said: I heard Qays ibn Abī Ḥāzim say: Saʿd said: I have seen myself the seventh of seven with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we had no food except the leaves of the ḥublah, such that one of us would defecate as a sheep defecates, with nothing mixed with it. Then Banū Asad began to reproach me regarding Islam; then indeed I would be a loser, and my effort would go astray.
items.ma-1499: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from ʿĀṣim, Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī narrated to me, he said: I heard Ibn Mālik say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever claims [lineage] to other than his father, while knowing, Paradise is forbidden to him.”
items.ma-1500: Muḥammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥumayd informed us, Ismāʿīl ibn Muḥammad ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ informed me, from his father, from his grandfather, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: “O Saʿd, stand and call out in Minā: Indeed they are days of eating and drinking, and there is no fasting in them.”
items.ma-1501: al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, from Zāʾidah, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, he said: Saʿd said: Concerning me the Messenger of Allah ﷺ laid down the third as a sunnah: he came to me visiting me, and said to me: “Have you made a bequest?” I said: Yes, I have made all my wealth for the poor, the needy and the wayfarer. He said: “Do not do that.” I said: My heirs are wealthy. I said: Two-thirds? He said: “No.” I said: Then half? He said: “No.” I said: A third? He said: “A third—and a third is a lot.”
items.ma-1502: Suwayd ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, Abān narrated to us, Yaḥyā narrated to us, from al-Ḥaḍramī ibn Lāḥiq, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, from Saʿd ibn Mālik, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no hāmah, no contagion, and no ṭiyarah. If it [exists], then it is in the woman, the horse, and the house.”
items.ma-1503: I read to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Mālik. And ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Mālik ibn Anas informed us, from Ibn Shihāb, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Nawfal ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, that he narrated to him: that he heard Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ and al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Qays in the year that Muʿāwiyah ibn Abī Sufyān performed Ḥajj, while the two were mentioning tamattuʿ with the ʿumrah to the Ḥajj. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: None does that except one who is ignorant of the command of Allah. Saʿd said: How evil is what you have said, O son of my brother! Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: Indeed ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb forbade that. Saʿd said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did it, and we did it with him.
items.ma-1504: Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us, ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal narrated to us, from Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī, he said: Saʿd said—and once he said: I heard Saʿd say—: My two ears heard, and my heart retained, from Muḥammad ﷺ: “That whoever claims a father other than his father, while knowing that he is other than his father, Paradise is forbidden to him.” He said: So I met Abū Bakrah and narrated it to him, and he said: And I—my two ears heard it, and my heart retained it, from Muḥammad ﷺ.
items.ma-1505: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm, he said: I heard Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd narrating from Saʿd, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said to ʿAlī: “Are you not pleased to be to me in the position of Hārūn to Mūsā?”
items.ma-1506:
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us. And Ḥajjāj: Shuʿbah narrated to me, from Qatādah, from Yūnus ibn Jubayr, from Muḥammad ibn Saʿd, from Saʿd, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “For the belly of one of you to be filled with pus that corrupts it is better for him than that it be filled with poetry.”
Ḥajjāj said: I heard Yūnus ibn Jubayr.
items.ma-1507: Ḥasan narrated it to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Qatādah, from ʿUmar ibn Saʿd ibn Mālik, from Saʿd, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said: “For the belly of one of you to be filled with pus until it corrupts it is better than that it be filled with poetry.”
items.ma-1508:
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Qatādah, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn Saʿd, from Saʿd, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said about the plague: “When it occurs in a land, do not enter it; and when you are in it, do not flee from it.”
Shuʿbah said: And Hishām Abū Bakr narrated to me that he is ʿIkrimah ibn Khālid.
items.ma-1509: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, he said: I heard Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab say: I said to Saʿd ibn Mālik: You are a person in whom there is sharpness, and I want to ask you. He said: What is it? I said: The hadith of ʿAlī. He said: The Prophet ﷺ said to ʿAlī: “Are you not pleased to be to me in the position of Hārūn to Mūsā?” He said: I am pleased, I am pleased. Then he said: Yes, yes.
items.ma-1510: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū ʿAwn, from Jābir ibn Samurah. And Bahz and ʿAffān narrated to us; both said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, Abū ʿAwn informed me; Bahz said: he said: I heard Jābir ibn Samurah say: ʿUmar said to Saʿd: The people have complained about you in everything, even in the prayer. He said: As for me, I lengthen the first two, and shorten the last two, and I do not fall short in following the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. ʿUmar said: That is the thought about you—or: my thought about you.
items.ma-1511: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Fiṭr narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sharīk, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ruqaym al-Kinānī, he said: We went out to Madīnah at the time of al-Jamal, and Saʿd ibn Mālik met us there and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered the closing of the doors that open onto the mosque, and the leaving of the door of ʿAlī ﵁.
items.ma-1512: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Layth informed us; and Abū al-Naḍr: Layth narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Mulaykah al-Qurashī, then al-Taymī, narrated to me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Nahīk, from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: “He is not of us who does not chant with the Qurʾān.”
items.ma-1513: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Layth informed us, ʿUqayl narrated to me, from Ibn Shihāb, from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade that a man come to his family by night after the ʿIshāʾ prayer.
items.ma-1514: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Layth informed us, ʿUqayl narrated to me, from Ibn Shihāb, Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab informed me that he heard Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ say: ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn wanted to practise tabattul, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade him; and had he permitted that to him, we would have castrated ourselves.
items.ma-1515: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, Mālik ibn Anas narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd, the mawlā of al-Aswad ibn Sufyān, narrated to me, from Abū ʿAyyāsh, from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about fresh dates for dried dates? He said: “Do fresh dates not diminish when they dry?” They said: Yes. So he disliked it.
items.ma-1516: Yaʿlā narrated to us, ʿUthmān ibn Ḥakīm narrated to us, ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ narrated to us, from his father, he said: We came back with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until we passed the mosque of Banū Muʿāwiyah. He entered and prayed two rakʿahs, and we prayed with him, and he conversed intimately with his Rabb ﷿ for a long time. He said: “I asked my Rabb ﷿ for three things: I asked Him that He not destroy my ummah by drowning, and He gave it to me; and I asked Him that He not destroy my ummah by famine, and He gave it to me; and I asked Him that He not set their might among themselves, and He withheld it from me.”
items.ma-1517: Yaʿlā and Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us; Yaḥyā said: he said: A man narrated to me, whom I used to name, but I forgot his name, from ʿUmar ibn Saʿd, he said: I had a need with Abū Saʿd. He said: And Abū Ḥayyān narrated to us, from Mujammiʿ, he said: ʿUmar ibn Saʿd had a need with his father, and he put before his need some words of what the people say, which they connect, which he had not been hearing. When he finished, he said: O my son, have you finished your speech? He said: Yes. He said: You were not farther from your need, nor was I more detached from you, than I have been since I heard this speech of yours. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “There will be a people who eat with their tongues as the cows eat from the earth.”
items.ma-1518: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, from Jābir ibn Samurah, he said: The people of al-Kūfah complained about Saʿd to ʿUmar and said: He does not pray well. He said: So ʿUmar asked him, and he said: I pray with them the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: I stay still long in the first two, and I shorten in the last two. He said: That is the thought about you, O Abū Isḥāq.
items.ma-1519: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿUmar ibn Saʿd, Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ narrated to us, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Fighting a Muslim is kufr, and reviling him is fusūq, and it is not lawful for a Muslim to forsake his brother for more than three days.”
items.ma-1520: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, from his father, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed among the greatest of the Muslims in guilt among the Muslims is a man who asked about something and pressed about it until a prohibition was revealed concerning that thing because of his question.”
items.ma-1521: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUmar ibn Saʿd, or another: that Saʿd ibn Mālik said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever humiliates Quraysh, Allah ﷿ humiliates him.”
items.ma-1522: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, from his father, he said: The Prophet ﷺ gave men, and did not give one man among them anything. Saʿd said: O Prophet of Allah, you gave so-and-so and so-and-so, and you did not give so-and-so anything, though he is a believer. The Prophet ﷺ said: “Or a Muslim”—until Saʿd had repeated it three times, and the Prophet ﷺ was saying: “Or a Muslim.” Then the Prophet ﷺ said: “Indeed I give men, and I leave the one who is dearer to me than they, so I do not give him anything, for fear that they be thrown into the Fire on their faces.”
items.ma-1523: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd, from his father, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered the killing of the gecko, and named it a little transgressor.
items.ma-1524:
ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, from his father, he said: I was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the Ḥajj of the Farewell, and I fell ill with an illness in which I came near death, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ visited me. I said: O Messenger of Allah, I have much wealth, and none inherits from me except a daughter of mine; may I bequeath two-thirds of my wealth? He said: “No.” I said: Half of my wealth? He said: “No.” I said: Then a third of my wealth? He said: “A third—and a third is a lot. Indeed, O Saʿd, that you leave your heirs wealthy is better for you than that you leave them dependent, begging from the people. Indeed, O Saʿd, you will not spend any spending seeking by it Wajh Allāh except that you will be rewarded for it, even the morsel that you put into the mouth of your wife.”
He said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, will I be left behind after my Companions? He said: “Indeed you will not be left behind and do a deed seeking by it Wajh Allāh except that you will increase by it in rank and elevation; and perhaps you will be left behind so that Allah benefits people through you and others are harmed through you. O Allah, carry through for my Companions their emigration, and do not turn them back on their heels; but the wretched one is Saʿd ibn Khawlah”—the Messenger of Allah ﷺ felt pity for him, and he had died in Makkah.
items.ma-1525: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, he said: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab then informed me, from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ rejected tabattul from ʿUthmān, and had he made it lawful, we would have castrated ourselves.
items.ma-1526: Yazīd ibn Hārūn narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq informed us, from Dāwūd ibn ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd ibn Mālik, from his father, from his grandfather, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There was no prophet except that he described the Dajjāl to his ummah, and I will surely describe him with a description that no one before me described: he is one-eyed, and indeed Allah ﷿ is not one-eyed.”
items.ma-1527: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad and ʿAffān narrated to us; both said: Salīm ibn Ḥayyān narrated to us, ʿIkrimah ibn Khālid narrated to us—ʿAffān said: narrated to me—from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿd, from Saʿd: that the plague was mentioned in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: “Indeed it is a scourge with which those before you were afflicted. So when it is in a land, do not enter it; and when you are in a land and it is in it, do not leave it.”
items.ma-1528: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, Fulayḥ narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Maʿmar, he said: ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd narrated to ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, while he was governor over Madīnah: that Saʿd said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever eats seven dates of ʿajwah from between the two lava fields of Madīnah when he rises in the morning, nothing will harm him that day until evening.” Fulayḥ said: And I think he said: “And if he eats them when evening comes, nothing will harm him until morning.” He said: ʿUmar said: O ʿĀmir, look at what you narrate from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. ʿĀmir said: By Allah, I have not lied about Saʿd, and Saʿd has not lied about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-1529: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, Kathīr ibn Zayd al-Aslamī narrated to us, from al-Muṭṭalib, from ʿUmar ibn Saʿd, from his father, that he said: His son ʿĀmir came to him, and he said: O my son, do you order me in the fitnah to be a head? No, by Allah, not until I am given a sword which, if I strike a believer with it, turns away from him, and if I strike a disbeliever with it, kills him. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Indeed Allah ﷿ Yuḥibbu the wealthy, the hidden, the God-fearing.”
items.ma-1530: Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, Misʿar narrated to us, from Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, he said: I saw on the right of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and on his left on the day of Uḥud two men wearing white garments; I had not seen them before, nor after.
items.ma-1531: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-ʿAyzār, from ʿUmar ibn Saʿd, from his father Saʿd, from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: “I am amazed at the Muslim: if good befalls him, he praises Allah and is thankful, and if a calamity befalls him, he seeks reward and is patient. The Muslim is rewarded in everything, even in the morsel that he raises to his mouth.”
items.ma-1532: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from Qatādah and ʿAlī ibn Zayd ibn Judʿān, both said: Ibn al-Musayyib narrated to us, a son of Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ narrated to me a ḥadīth from his father, he said: I entered upon Saʿd and said: [There is] a ḥadīth that was narrated to me from you, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed ʿAlī as his deputy over al-Madīnah? He said: He became angry and said: Who narrated it to you? I disliked to tell him that his son had narrated it to me, lest he become angry with him. Then he said: Indeed, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out on the expedition of Tabūk, he appointed ʿAlī as his deputy over al-Madīnah, and ʿAlī said: O Messenger of Allah, I did not like that you should go out in any direction unless I were with you. So he said: “Are you not pleased to be to me in the position of Hārūn to Mūsā? Except that there is no prophet after me.”
items.ma-1533: Isḥāq ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us, he said: Mālik – meaning Ibn Anas – narrated to me, Abū al-Naḍr narrated to us, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd, he said: I heard my father say: I did not hear the Prophet ﷺ say of any living person walking: “He is in Paradise,” except of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām.
items.ma-1534: Hārūn ibn Maʿrūf narrated to us – ʿAbd Allāh said: And I myself heard it from Hārūn –, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Wahb narrated to us, Makhramah narrated to me, from his father, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, he said: I heard Saʿd, and [other] people from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, say: There were two men, brothers, in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and one of them was better than the other. The one who was the better of the two died, then the other was granted a long life after him of forty nights, then he died. The superiority of the first over the other was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: “Did he not pray?” They said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah, and there was nothing wrong with him. He said: “What lets you know what his prayer has attained for him?” Then he said at that: “The likeness of the prayer is only like a flowing river at the door of a man, abundant, sweet, into which he plunges five times every day. What do you think that leaves of his dirt?”
items.ma-1535: Bahz narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, Qatādah narrated to us, from Yūnus ibn Jubayr, from Muḥammad ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “For the inside of one of you to be filled with pus and blood is better for him than for it to be filled with poetry.”
items.ma-1536: Bahz narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit informed me, he said: I came to al-Madīnah, and it reached us that the plague had occurred in al-Kūfah. He said: I said: Who narrates this ḥadīth? It was said: ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd. He said: And he was absent. So I met Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd, and he narrated to me that he heard Usāmah ibn Zayd narrating to Saʿd that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When the plague occurs in a land, do not enter it, and when it occurs while you are in it, do not leave it.” He said: I said: Did you yourself hear Usāmah? He said: Yes.
items.ma-1537: ʿAlī ibn Baḥr narrated to us, ʿĪsā ibn Yūnus narrated to us, from Zakariyyā, from Abū Isḥāq, from Muḥammad ibn Saʿd ibn Mālik, from his father, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Fighting a Muslim is kufr, and reviling him is fisq.”
items.ma-1538: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Abū Bakr informed us, from ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd, from Muṣʿab ibn Saʿd, from Saʿd ibn Mālik, he said: He said: O Messenger of Allah, Allah has healed me today of the polytheists, so give me this sword. He said: “This sword is not for you and not for me; put it down.” He said: So I put it down, then I went back, [and] I said: Perhaps this sword will be given today to one who has not put himself to the test as I did. He said: Then suddenly a man was calling me from behind me. He said: I said: Has something been revealed about me? He said: “You had asked me for the sword, and it was not mine, and it has now been given to me, so it is yours.” He said: And this verse was revealed: {They ask you about the spoils of war. Say: The spoils of war belong to Allah and the Messenger} [al-Anfāl: 1].
items.ma-1539: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, he said: I found this ḥadīth in my father's book in his own handwriting: ʿAbd al-Mutaʿāl ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb narrated to me, Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Umawī narrated to me. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: And Saʿīd ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, my father narrated to us, al-Mujālid narrated to us, from Ziyād ibn ʿIlāqah, from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, he said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived in al-Madīnah, Juhaynah came to him and said: You have alighted among us, so make a firm covenant for us, so that we may come to you and you give us security. So he made a firm covenant with them, and they accepted Islam. He said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent us out in Rajab, and we were not a hundred, and he commanded us to raid a clan of Banū Kinānah next to Juhaynah. So we raided them, and they were many, so we took refuge with Juhaynah and they protected us, and said: Why do you fight in the sacred month? We said: We only fight those who expelled us from the sacred land in the sacred month. Then some of us said to others: What do you think? Some of us said: We should go to the Prophet of Allah ﷺ and inform him, and a group said: No, rather we should stay here, and I said, among some people with me: No, rather we should go to the caravan of Quraysh and cut it off. So we set out to the caravan, and the fayʾ at that time was: whoever took something, it was his. So we set out to the caravan, and our companions set out to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him of the news, and he stood angry, his face red, and said: “Did you go from me together, and come back scattered? Those before you were destroyed only by division. I will surely send over you a man who is not the best of you, the most patient of you in hunger and thirst.” So he sent over us ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaḥsh al-Asadī, and he was the first commander appointed in Islam.
items.ma-1540: Ḥusayn narrated to us, from Zāʾidah, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, and ʿAbd al-Ṣamad: Zāʾidah narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr narrated to us, from Jābir ibn Samurah, from Nāfiʿ ibn ʿUtbah ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “You will fight the Arabian Peninsula and Allah will open it for you, then you will fight Persia and Allah will open it for you, then you will fight Rome and Allah will open it for you, then you will fight the Dajjāl and Allah will open him for you.” He said: Then Jābir said: The Dajjāl will not come out until Rome is opened.
items.ma-1541: ʿAffān narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr narrated to us, from Jābir ibn Samurah, from Nāfiʿ ibn ʿUtbah ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, that he heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “You will raid the Arabian Peninsula, and Allah will open [it] for you, and you will raid Persia, and Allah will open it for you, and you will raid Rome, and Allah will open it for you, and you will raid the Dajjāl, and Allah will open [him] for you.”
items.ma-1542: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, he said: I heard my father narrating from Muḥammad ibn ʿIkrimah, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Labībah, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ: that the owners of farms in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to rent out their farms for what grew on the irrigation channels of crops, and for what prospered with the water of what was around the well. So they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and disputed over some of that, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade them to rent out in that way, and said: “Rent out for gold and silver.”
items.ma-1543: Ibn Abī ʿAdī narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq. And Yaʿqūb: my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad – Yaʿqūb said: Ibn Abī ʿAtīq – narrated to me, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd, he narrated to him from his father Saʿd, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “When one of you spits phlegm in the mosque, let him hide his phlegm, lest it strike the skin of a believer, or his garment, and harm him.”
items.ma-1544: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, from Mālik, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd, from Zayd ibn ʿAyyāsh, he said: Saʿd was asked about [selling] white barley for hull-less barley, and he disliked it, and said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ being asked about fresh dates for dry dates, and he said: “Does it decrease when it dries?” They said: Yes. He said: “Then no.”
items.ma-1545: Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd, from his father, he conveys it to the Prophet ﷺ: “The greatest of the Muslims among the Muslims in offence is one who asked about a matter that was not forbidden, and it was forbidden to the people because of his asking.”
items.ma-1546:
Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd, from his father, he said: I fell ill in Makkah in the year of the Conquest with a severe illness, from which I was on the verge of death, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to visit me. I said: O Messenger of Allah, I have much wealth, and none inherits from me except my daughter. Shall I give two-thirds of my wealth as ṣadaqah? – and Sufyān said once: Shall I give all my wealth as ṣadaqah? He said: “No.” He said: Shall I give two-thirds of my wealth as ṣadaqah? – He said: “No.” I said: Then half? He said: “No.” I said: A third? He said: “A third, and a third is much. That you leave your heirs wealthy is better than that you leave them in need, begging from people. You will not spend any expenditure except that you will be rewarded for it, even the morsel that you raise to the mouth of your wife.”
I said: O Messenger of Allah, shall I be left behind from my hijrah? He said: “You will not be left behind after me, and then do a deed by which you intend Wajh Allāh, except that you will increase by it in elevation and rank. And perhaps you will be left behind until people benefit from you and others are harmed by you. O Allah, complete for my Companions their hijrah, and do not turn them back on their heels. But the wretched one is Saʿd ibn Khawlah.” He felt pity for him that he had died in Makkah.
items.ma-1547: Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, from Saʿd, that the Prophet ﷺ said to ʿAlī: “You are to me in the position of Hārūn to Mūsā.” It was said to Sufyān: “Except that there is no prophet after me,” he said: He said: Yes.
items.ma-1548: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik, he heard it from Jābir ibn Samurah: The people of al-Kūfah complained about Saʿd to ʿUmar, and said: He does not pray well. He said: The bedouins?! By Allah, I do not fall short with them in the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; in the Ẓuhr and the ʿAṣr [prayers] I linger in the first two [rakʿahs] and shorten the last two. Then I heard ʿUmar say: Such is the thought about you, O Abū Isḥāq.
items.ma-1549: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr, I heard Ibn Abī Mulaykah, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Nahīk, from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “He is not of us who does not yataghanna with the Qurʾān.”
items.ma-1550: Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from Mālik ibn Aws: I heard ʿUmar say to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, Ṭalḥah, al-Zubayr and Saʿd: I adjure you by Allah, by whom the heaven and the earth stand – and once he said: by whose permission they stand – do you know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “We are not inherited from; what we leave is ṣadaqah”? They said: O Allah, yes.
items.ma-1551: Sufyān narrated to us, from al-ʿAlāʾ – meaning Ibn Abī al-ʿAbbās –, from Abū al-Ṭufayl, from Bakr ibn Qirwāsh, from Saʿd – it was said to Sufyān: From the Prophet ﷺ? He said: Yes – he said: “The devil of al-radhah brings him down,” meaning a man from Bajīlah.
items.ma-1552: Sufyān narrated to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Umayyah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd, from Abū ʿAyyāsh, he said: Saʿd was asked about the sale of hull-less barley for barley, or something of this, and he said: The Prophet ﷺ was asked about dry dates for fresh dates, and he said: “Does the fresh date decrease when it dries?” They said: Yes. He said: “Then no.”
items.ma-1553: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal narrated to us, from Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī, he said: I heard Saʿd say: My two ears heard and my heart retained from Muḥammad ﷺ: “That whoever claims [lineage] to other than his father, and he knows that he is other than his father, Paradise is forbidden to him.” He said: Then I met Abū Bakrah and narrated it to him, and he said: And my two ears heard, and my heart retained, from Muḥammad ﷺ.
items.ma-1554: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Hishām al-Dastuwāʾī informed us, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from al-Ḥaḍramī ibn Lāḥiq, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, he said: I asked Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ about ṭiyarah, and he rebuked me and said: Who narrated to you? I disliked to tell him who had narrated to me. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no contagion, no ṭiyarah and no hāmah. If ṭiyarah is in anything, it is in the horse, the woman and the house. And when you hear of the plague in a land, do not go down to it, and if it is in a land while you are in it, do not flee from it.”
items.ma-1555:
Ismāʿīl – meaning Ibn Ibrāhīm – narrated to us, Hishām al-Dastuwāʾī informed us, from ʿĀṣim ibn Bahdalah, from Muṣʿab ibn Saʿd, he said: Saʿd said: O Messenger of Allah, which of the people is most severe in trial? He said: “The prophets, then the next best, then the next best, until the servant is tried according to the measure of that religion of his. If he is firm in religion, he is tried according to that measure – and once he said: his trial is intensified – and if there is softness in his religion, he is tried according to that measure – and once he said: according to his religion – He said: Trials do not cease from the servant until he walks on the earth, meaning, while there is no sin upon him.”
My father said: And once he said: from Saʿd, he said: I said: O Messenger of Allah.
items.ma-1556: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, Abū Isḥāq al-Shaybānī narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd Allāh al-Thaqafī, from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, he said: When it was the day of Badr, my brother ʿUmayr was killed, and I killed Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ and took his sword, which was called Dhū al-Katīfah, and I brought it to the Prophet of Allah ﷺ. He said: “Go and throw it in the qabaḍ.” He said: So I went back, and in me was what none knows except Allah, from the killing of my brother and the taking of my spoil. He said: I had not gone beyond [that] except a little when Sūrat al-Anfāl was revealed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: “Go and take your sword.”
items.ma-1557: Jarīr ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, from Jābir ibn Samurah, he said: The people of al-Kūfah complained about Saʿd to ʿUmar, and said: He does not pray well. ʿUmar mentioned that to him, and he said: As for the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I used to lead them in it, lingering in the first two and shortening the last two. He said: That is the thought about you, O Abū Isḥāq.
items.ma-1558: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from ʿUmar ibn Nubayh, Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Qarrāẓ narrated to me, he said: I heard Saʿd ibn Mālik say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever intends the people of al-Madīnah with a sudden onslaught or with evil, Allah will dissolve him as salt dissolves in water.”
items.ma-1559: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from Usāmah ibn Zayd, Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Labībah narrated to me, from Saʿd ibn Mālik, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “The best remembrance is the hidden one, and the best provision is that which suffices.”
items.ma-1560: ʿAlī ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, from Ibn al-Mubārak, from Usāmah ibn Zayd, he said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān informed me that Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Labībah informed him, and he mentioned it.
items.ma-1561: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from Mūsā al-Juhanī, Muṣʿab ibn Saʿd narrated to me, from his father: that a bedouin came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: Teach me words that I may say. He said: “Say: There is no deity except Allah alone, He has no partner; Allah is the Greatest, in greatness; and praise belongs to Allah abundantly; and glory be to Allah, Rabb of the worlds; and there is no power and no strength except with Allah, al-ʿAzīz al-Ḥakīm,” five. He said: These are for my Rabb, so what is for me? He said: “Say: O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, provide for me, guide me, and grant me well-being.”
items.ma-1562: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, Yaḥyā – meaning Ibn Saʿīd al-Anṣārī – narrated to us, he said: I heard Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib say: I heard Saʿd say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ combined for me his two parents on the day of Uḥud.
items.ma-1563:
Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Mūsā – meaning al-Juhanī –, Muṣʿab ibn Saʿd narrated to me, my father narrated to me, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Is one of you unable to earn a thousand good deeds every day?” A man from those sitting with him said: How can one of us earn a thousand good deeds? He said: “He glorifies a hundred glorifications; a thousand good deeds are written for him, or a thousand sins are removed from him.”
My father said: And Ibn Numayr also said “or are removed”, and Yaʿlā also: “or are removed.”
items.ma-1564: Yaḥyā narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, Muṣʿab ibn Thābit narrated to me, from Ismāʿīl ibn Muḥammad ibn Saʿd, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd, from his father Saʿd ibn Mālik, he said: The Prophet ﷺ used to give the salām to his right and to his left, until the whiteness of his cheeks could be seen.
items.ma-1565: Yūnus ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qays, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, from his father Saʿd, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever says when he hears the muʾadhdhin: And I bear witness that there is no deity except Allah, alone, having no partner, and that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger; I am pleased with Allah as Rabb, with Muḥammad as Messenger, and with Islam as religion, his sin is forgiven for him.” Qutaybah narrated it to us, and said: Layth narrated it to us: from al-Ḥukaym ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qays.
items.ma-1566: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Qays narrated to us, he said: I heard Saʿd ibn Mālik say: I am the first of the Arabs to shoot an arrow in the path of Allah, and I have seen us raiding with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we had no food to eat except the leaves of the ḥublah and this acacia, until one of us would drop as the sheep drops, with nothing mixed in it. Then Banū Asad have come to rebuke me about the religion; I would have failed then, and my deed would have gone astray.
items.ma-1567:
Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, Simāk ibn Ḥarb narrated to me, from Muṣʿab ibn Saʿd, he said: Four verses were revealed about my father. He said: My father said: I obtained a sword. I said: O Messenger of Allah, grant it to me as an extra share. He said: “Put it down.” I said: O Messenger of Allah: grant it to me as an extra share; am I to be made like one who has no avail? He said: “Put it back from where you took it.” So there was revealed: {They ask you about the spoils of war} – he said: And it is thus in the recitation of Ibn Masʿūd – {Say: The spoils of war}. And my mother said: Does Allah not command you to maintain ties of kinship and kindness to parents? By Allah, I will not eat food and I will not drink drink until you disbelieve in Muḥammad. So she would not eat until they would pry open her mouth with a stick and pour the drink into it – Shuʿbah said: and I think he said: and the food – so there was revealed: {And We enjoined man concerning his parents; his mother bore him in weakness upon weakness}, and he recited until he reached: {for what you used to do} [Luqmān: 14 - 15]. And the Prophet ﷺ entered upon me while I was ill. I said: O Messenger of Allah, shall I make a bequest of all my wealth? He forbade me. I said: Half? He said: “No.” I said: A third? He was silent, so the people took to it.
And a man of the Anṣār made food, and they ate and drank and became intoxicated from khamr, and that was before it was prohibited. So we gathered with him, and they boasted, and the Anṣār said: The Anṣār are better, and the Muhājirūn said: The Muhājirūn are better. Then a man swung at him with the jawbone of a camel and split his nose, so Saʿd's nose was split. So there was revealed: {O you who believe, khamr and maysir [are] only} up to His saying: {Will you then desist?} [al-Māʾidah: 90 - 91].
items.ma-1568: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, Sulaymān – meaning al-Taymī – informed us, Ghunaym narrated to me, he said: I asked Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ about the mutʿah. He said: We did it, and this one was a disbeliever in the ʿUrush; meaning Muʿāwiyah.
items.ma-1569: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from Qatādah, from Yūnus ibn Jubayr, from Muḥammad ibn Saʿd, from his father, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “For the inside of a man to be filled with pus is better than for it to be filled with poetry.”
items.ma-1570: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Ismāʿīl, from al-Zubayr ibn ʿAdī, from Muṣʿab ibn Saʿd, he said: I prayed with Saʿd, and I [did] thus with my hands – Yaḥyā described the tatbīq – and he struck my hands and said: We used to do this, then we were commanded to raise [them] to the knees.
items.ma-1571: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Numayr narrated to us, Hāshim narrated to us, from ʿĀʾishah bint Saʿd, from Saʿd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever takes in the morning seven dates of ʿajwah, neither poison nor sorcery will harm him that day.”
items.ma-1572:
Makkī narrated to us, Hāshim narrated to us, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, from Saʿd, and he mentioned the ḥadīth, the like of it.
ʿAbd Allāh said: And my father said: Abū Badr narrated it to us, from Hāshim, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd.
items.ma-1573: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from ʿUthmān – meaning Ibn Ḥakīm –, ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd informed me, from his father, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I declare forbidden what is between the two lava tracts of al-Madīnah: that its thorny trees be cut or its game be killed.” And he said: “Al-Madīnah is better for them, if they knew. No one leaves it out of aversion to it except that Allah replaces in it one who is better than him, and no one remains steadfast through its hardship and its difficulty except that I will be a witness for him, or an intercessor, on the Day of Resurrection.”
items.ma-1574: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Numayr narrated to us, from ʿUthmān, he said: ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd informed me from his father: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came one day from al-ʿĀliyah, until when he passed by the mosque of Banū Muʿāwiyah he entered, and prayed two rakʿahs in it, and we prayed with him, and he supplicated his Rabb for a long time, then turned to us and said: “I asked my Rabb for three, and He gave me two and withheld one from me: I asked my Rabb that He not destroy my ummah by a year, and He gave it to me; and I asked Him that He not destroy my ummah by drowning, and He gave it to me; and I asked Him that He not make their might among themselves, and He withheld it from me.”
items.ma-1575: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-ʿAyzār ibn Ḥurayth al-ʿAbdī, from ʿUmar ibn Saʿd, from his father, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I marvel at the believer: if good befalls him he praises Allah and gives thanks, and if an affliction befalls him, he anticipates reward and is patient. The believer is rewarded in everything, even in the morsel that he raises to his mouth.”
items.ma-1576: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Ibn Abī Khālid narrated to us, from al-Zubayr ibn ʿAdī, from Muṣʿab ibn Saʿd, he said: When I bowed, I would place my hands between my knees. He said: My father Saʿd ibn Mālik saw me and forbade me, and said: We used to do it, then we were forbidden from it.
items.ma-1577: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, from Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd, from Saʿd ibn Mālik, Khuzaymah ibn Thābit, and Usāmah ibn Zayd, they said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “This plague is rijz, or a remnant of a punishment with which a people before you were punished. So when it occurs in a land while you are in it, do not go out from it in flight from it, and when you hear of it in a land, do not enter upon it.”
items.ma-1578: Yazīd narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq informed us, from Dāwūd ibn ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd ibn Mālik, from his father, from his grandfather, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I will surely describe the Dajjāl with a description that none before me described: he is one-eyed, and Allah ﷿ is not one-eyed.”
items.ma-1579: Yazīd narrated to us, Ibn Abī Dhiʾb informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd ibn Mālik, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ: that a group came to him and asked him, and he gave them, except a man among them. Saʿd said: So I said: O Messenger of Allah, you gave them and left so-and-so, and by Allah, I see him as a believer. The Prophet ﷺ said: “Or a Muslim.” Then Saʿd repeated that to him three times: a believer, and the Prophet ﷺ replied to him: “Or a Muslim.” Then the Prophet ﷺ said on the third: “By Allah, I give a man a gift while another is dearer to me than him, fearing that Allah may cast him on his face in the Fire.”
items.ma-1580: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, my father narrated to me, he said: Abū Nuʿaym said: I met Sufyān in Makkah, and the first one who asked me about him said: How is Shujāʿ? meaning Abū Badr.
items.ma-1581: Yazīd narrated to us, Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd and Hāshim ibn al-Qāsim informed us, Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd narrated to us, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Kaysān – Hāshim said in his ḥadīth: he said: Ṣāliḥ ibn Kaysān narrated to me, and Yazīd said: from Ṣāliḥ – from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Muḥammad ibn Saʿd, from his father, he said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb entered upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and with him were women of Quraysh asking him, and asking for much, raising their voices. When they heard the voice of ʿUmar, they cowered and fell silent, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed. ʿUmar said: O enemies of yourselves, do you fear me and not fear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? They said: You are harsher than the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and sterner. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “O ʿUmar, Shayṭān never meets you travelling a path except that he travels a path other than your path.”
items.ma-1582: Yazīd narrated to us, Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd informed us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿIkrimah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Labībah, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, from Saʿd ibn Mālik, he said: We used to rent out land in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for what was on the irrigation channels of crops, and for what prospered with the water of it. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade us that, and permitted us – or gave a concession – to rent it out for gold and silver.
items.ma-1583: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Muṣʿab ibn Saʿd, from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ left ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib behind on the expedition of Tabūk, and he said: O Messenger of Allah, are you leaving me behind with the women and the children? He said: “Are you not pleased to be to me in the position of Hārūn to Mūsā? Except that there is no prophet after me.”
items.ma-1584: Abū al-Naḍr narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: Ziyād ibn Mikhrāq informed me, he said: I heard Qays ibn ʿAbāyah narrate from a mawlā of Saʿd. And Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Ziyād ibn Mikhrāq, he said: I heard Qays ibn ʿAbāyah al-Qaysī narrate from a mawlā of Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, from a son of Saʿd: that he was praying, and he was saying in his supplication: O Allah, I ask You for Paradise, and I ask You for its bliss and its splendour, and for such and such, and for such and such, and for such and such, and for such and such, and I seek refuge with You from the Fire and its chains and its shackles, and from such and such, and from such and such. He said: Saʿd was silent toward him, and when he had prayed, Saʿd said to him: You have sought refuge from a great evil and asked for a great bliss – or he said: a long one, Shuʿbah was in doubt –. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There will be a people who transgress in supplication,” and he recited: {Call upon your Rabb in humility and in secret; indeed He does not Yuḥibbu the transgressors} [al-Aʿrāf: 55] – Shuʿbah said: I do not know whether his saying: {Call upon your Rabb in humility and in secret}, was from the saying of Saʿd or the saying of the Prophet ﷺ. And Saʿd said to him: Say: O Allah, I ask You for Paradise, and whatever brings [one] near to it of word or deed, and I seek refuge with You from the Fire, and whatever brings [one] near to it of word or deed.
items.ma-1585: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, from Muṣʿab, from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ: that he used to command these five, and narrate them from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: “O Allah, I seek refuge with You from miserliness, and I seek refuge with You from cowardice, and I seek refuge with You from being returned to the vilest of life, and I seek refuge with You from the fitnah of the world, and I seek refuge with You from the punishment of the grave.”
items.ma-1586: Abū Kāmil narrated to us, Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd narrated to us, Ṣāliḥ ibn Kaysān narrated to us, from Ibn Shihāb, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Sufyān ibn al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Jāriyah, from Yūsuf ibn al-Ḥakam Abū al-Ḥajjāj, from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever humiliates Quraysh, Allah ﷿ will humiliate him.”
items.ma-1587: And Abū Kāmil narrated to us on another occasion: Ṣāliḥ ibn Kaysān narrated to me, from Ibn Shihāb, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Sufyān ibn al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Jāriyah, from Muḥammad ibn Saʿd, from his father Saʿd, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever wants the humiliation of Quraysh, Allah will humiliate him.”
items.ma-1588: Abū Kāmil narrated to us, Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd narrated to us, Ibn Shihāb narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, he said: I heard Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ rejected tabattul for ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn, and had he permitted him in it, we would have castrated ourselves.
items.ma-1589: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Muḥammad ibn Saʿd ibn Mālik, from his father, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “It is not lawful for a Muslim to forsake his brother beyond three.”
items.ma-1590: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Muṣʿab ibn Saʿd, from his father, he said: I swore by al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā, and my companions said: You have said something foul. So I came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: The covenant was near, and I swore by al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Say: There is no deity except Allah alone,” three times, “then spit lightly to your left three times, and seek refuge, and do not repeat.”
items.ma-1591: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān Muʾammal ibn Ismāʿīl and ʿAffān narrated to us, in meaning, both said: Ḥammād narrated to us, ʿĀṣim narrated to us, from Muṣʿab ibn Saʿd, from his father: that the Prophet ﷺ was brought a bowl of tharīd, and he ate, and a remainder was left of it, and he said: “There will enter from this mountain pass a man of the people of Paradise, who will eat this remainder.” Saʿd said: And I had left my brother ʿUmayr ibn Abī Waqqāṣ preparing to come to the Prophet ﷺ, and I hoped that it would be him, but ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām came and ate it.
items.ma-1592: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, Abān narrated to us, ʿĀṣim narrated to us, and he mentioned its meaning, except that he said: So I passed by ʿUwaymir ibn Mālik.
items.ma-1593: ʿUthmān ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, Usāmah – meaning Ibn Zayd – narrated to us, Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Qarrāẓ narrated to us, that he heard Saʿd ibn Mālik and Abū Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “O Allah, bless the people of al-Madīnah in their city, and bless them in their ṣāʿ, and bless them in their mudd. O Allah, indeed Ibrāhīm is Your servant and Your khalīl, and I am Your servant and Your Messenger, and Ibrāhīm asked You for the people of Makkah, and I ask You for the people of al-Madīnah, as Ibrāhīm asked You for the people of Makkah, and the like of it with it. Indeed al-Madīnah is interlaced with angels; at every pass of it are two angels guarding it; neither the plague nor the Dajjāl enters it; whoever intends it with evil, Allah will dissolve him as salt dissolves in water.”
items.ma-1594: Muḥammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Saʿd, from his father Saʿd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us striking one of his hands upon the other, saying: “The month is thus and thus,” then he withdrew his finger on the third.
items.ma-1595: Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, Zāʾidah narrated to us, from Ismāʿīl, from Muḥammad ibn Saʿd, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “The month is thus and thus” – ten, and ten, and nine once.
items.ma-1596: Al-Ṭālaqānī narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubārak narrated to us, from Ismāʿīl, from Muḥammad ibn Saʿd, from his father, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The month is thus and thus and thus,” and thus – meaning twenty-nine.
items.ma-1597: Surayj ibn al-Nuʿmān narrated to us, ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz – meaning al-Darāwardī – narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The Hour will not be established until a people come forth who eat with their tongues, as the cows eat with their tongues.”
items.ma-1598: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Ḥasan narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm ibn al-Muhājir, from Abū Bakr – meaning Ibn Ḥafṣ – and he mentioned a story. Saʿd said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “How excellent is the death, that a man die in defence of his right.”
items.ma-1599: Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, Jarīr – meaning Ibn Ḥāzim – narrated to us, from his paternal uncle Jarīr – meaning Ibn Zayd –, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, from his father, he said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, shall I make a bequest of all my wealth? He said: “No.” I said: Then two-thirds of it? He said: “No.” I said: Then half of it? He said: “No.” I said: Then a third? He said: “A third, and a third is much. That one of you leave his family in good [circumstances] is better for him than that he leave them in need, dependent on the hands of the people.”
items.ma-1600: Abū Aḥmad al-Zubayrī narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh – meaning Ibn Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit – narrated to us, from Ḥamzah ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from his father, from Saʿd, he said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out on the expedition of Tabūk, he left ʿAlī behind, and he said to him: Are you leaving me behind? He said to him: “Are you not pleased to be to me in the position of Hārūn to Mūsā? Except that there is no prophet after me.”
items.ma-1601: Abū Saʿīd, the mawlā of Banū Hāshim, narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Ismāʿīl ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd, that Saʿd said in his illness: When I die, dig a laḥd for me, and do as was done for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-1602: Manṣūr ibn Salamah al-Khuzāʿī narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar informed us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Muḥammad, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd, from Saʿd, he said: Dig a laḥd for me, and set up [bricks] over me, as was done for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-1603: Surayj ibn al-Nuʿmān narrated to us, Abū Shihāb narrated to us, from al-Ḥajjāj, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, from Saʿd ibn Mālik, he said: We performed ṭawāf with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; some of us circled seven, some of us circled eight, and some of us more than that. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no blame.”
items.ma-1604: Hārūn ibn Maʿrūf narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Wahb informed us, Abū Ṣakhr informed me – Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad said: And I myself heard it from Hārūn – that Abū Ḥāzim narrated to him, from a son of Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, he said: I heard my father say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saying: “Indeed īmān began as a stranger, and it will return as it began, so Ṭūbā to the strangers on that day, when the people are corrupted. And by Him in Whose Yad is the soul of Abū al-Qāsim, īmān will surely withdraw between these two mosques as the snake withdraws into its hole.”
items.ma-1605: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān – meaning Ibn Abī al-Zinād – informed us, from Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Qarrāẓ, from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “A prayer in this mosque of mine is better than a thousand prayers in any other than it, except al-Masjid al-Ḥarām.”
