items.ma-1606: ʿAffān narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Ziyād narrated to us, ʿUthmān ibn Ḥakīm informed us, ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd narrated to me, from his father, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I declare forbidden what is between the two lava tracts of al-Madīnah, as Ibrāhīm declared his ḥaram forbidden; its thorny trees are not to be cut, its game is not to be killed, and no one leaves it out of aversion to it except that Allah replaces it with one better than him, and al-Madīnah is better for them, if they knew; and no one intends them with evil except that Allah dissolves him as lead dissolves in fire, or as salt dissolves in water.”
items.ma-1607: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrated to us, ʿĀṣim ibn Bahdalah narrated to us, Muṣʿab ibn Saʿd narrated to me, from his father, he said: I said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: Which of the people is most severe in trial? He said: So he said: “The prophets, then the next best, then the next best. A man is tried according to his religion. If his religion is firm, his trial is intensified, and if there is softness in his religion, he is tried according to his religion. And trial does not cease to be with the servant until it leaves him walking on the earth with no sin upon him.”
items.ma-1608:
Qutaybah ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, Ḥātim ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, from Bukayr ibn Mismār, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd, from his father, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saying to him – and he had left him behind on one of his expeditions – and ʿAlī said: O Messenger of Allah, are you leaving me behind with the women and the children? He said: “O ʿAlī, are you not pleased to be to me in the position of Hārūn to Mūsā? Except that there is no prophethood after me.”
And I heard him say on the day of Khaybar: “I will surely give the banner to a man who loves Allah and His Messenger, and Yuḥibbuhu Allāh wa-Rasūluh.” So we stretched ourselves toward it, and he said: “Call ʿAlī for me.” So he was brought, sore-eyed, and he spat in his eye and handed the banner to him, and Allah opened upon him.
And when this verse was revealed: {Let us call our sons and your sons} [Āl ʿImrān: 61], the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called ʿAlī, Fāṭimah, Ḥasan and Ḥusayn, Riḍwān Allāh ʿalayhim, and said: “O Allah, these are my family.”
items.ma-1609: Qutaybah ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, Layth ibn Saʿd narrated to us, from ʿAyyāsh ibn ʿAbbās, from Bukayr ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Busr ibn Saʿīd, that Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ said at the time of the fitnah of ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān: I bear witness that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There will be a fitnah in which the one sitting is better than the one standing, and the one standing is better than the one walking, and the one walking is better than the one hastening.” He said: Do you see, if he enters upon me in my house and stretches out his hand to me to kill me? He said: “Be like the son of Ādam.”
items.ma-1610: ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥah al-Taymī, of the people of al-Madīnah, narrated to me, Abū Suhayl Nāfiʿ ibn Mālik narrated to me, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to al-ʿAbbās: “This is al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, the most generous of Quraysh in hand and the most connecting of them.”
items.ma-1611:
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Numayr and Yaʿlā narrated to us, both said: Mūsā – meaning al-Juhanī – narrated to us, from Muṣʿab ibn Saʿd, from his father, he said: A bedouin came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Prophet of Allah, teach me words that I may say. He said: “Say: There is no deity except Allah alone, having no partner; Allah is the Greatest, in greatness; and praise belongs to Allah abundantly; glory be to Allah, Rabb of the worlds; there is no power and no strength except with Allah, al-ʿAzīz al-Ḥakīm.” He said: These are for my Rabb ﷿, so what is for me? He said: Say: “O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, guide me, and provide for me.”
Ibn Numayr said: Mūsā said: As for “grant me well-being”, I surmise [it], and I do not know.
items.ma-1612: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Numayr narrated to us, Mūsā narrated to us, from Muṣʿab ibn Saʿd, my father narrated to me, he said: We were sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: “Is one of you unable to earn a thousand good deeds every day?” He said: So one of those sitting with him asked him: O Prophet of Allah, how can one of us earn a thousand good deeds? He said: “He glorifies a hundred glorifications, so a thousand good deeds are written for him, or a thousand sins are removed from him.”
items.ma-1613: Yaʿlā ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, Mūsā narrated to us, from Muṣʿab ibn Saʿd, from his father, he said: We were sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: “Is one of you unable to earn a thousand good deeds every day?” So one of those sitting with him asked him: How can one of us earn a thousand good deeds every day, O Messenger of Allah? He said: “He glorifies a hundred glorifications, so a thousand good deeds are written for him, or a thousand sins are removed from him.”
items.ma-1614:
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Simāk, from Muṣʿab ibn Saʿd, from his father, he said: Four verses were revealed about me: On the day of Badr I obtained a sword, and he came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, grant it to me as an extra share. He said: “Put it down.” Then he stood and said: O Messenger of Allah, grant it to me as an extra share. He said: “Put it down.” Then he stood and said: O Messenger of Allah, grant it to me as an extra share; am I to be made like one who has no avail? The Prophet ﷺ said: “Put it back from where you took it.” So this verse was revealed: {They ask you about the spoils of war. Say: The spoils of war belong to Allah and the Messenger}. He said: And a man of the Anṣār made food and invited us, and we drank khamr until we became intoxicated. He said: Then the Anṣār and Quraysh boasted, and the Anṣār said: We are better than you, and Quraysh said: We are better than you. So a man of the Anṣār took the jawbone of a camel and struck Saʿd's nose with it and split it. He said: So Saʿd's nose was split. He said: So this verse was revealed: {O you who believe, khamr and maysir and the stone altars and the divining arrows are only an abomination from the work of Shayṭān, so avoid it, that you may succeed}.
He said: And the mother of Saʿd said: Has Allah not commanded them to be dutiful? By Allah, I will not eat food and I will not drink drink until I die or you disbelieve in Muḥammad. He said: So when they wanted to feed her, they would pry open her mouth with a stick, then pour [it] into her mouth. He said: So this verse was revealed: {And We enjoined man to treat his parents with goodness}.
He said: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon Saʿd while he was ill, visiting him, and he said: O Messenger of Allah, shall I make a bequest of all my wealth? He said: “No.” He said: Then two-thirds of it? He said: “No.” He said: Then a third of it? He said: He was silent.
items.ma-1615: Suwayd ibn ʿAmr al-Kalbī narrated to us, Abān narrated to us, Yaḥyā narrated to us, from al-Ḥaḍramī ibn Lāḥiq, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, from Saʿd ibn Mālik, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When the plague is in a land, do not go down to it, and when it is in a land while you are in it, do not flee from it.”
items.ma-1616: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb al-Thaqafī narrated to us, from Khālid, from ʿIkrimah, from Saʿd ibn Mālik, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on the day of Uḥud: “Shoot him; may my father and my mother be a ransom for you.”
items.ma-1617: Yazīd ibn Hārūn narrated to us, al-Ḥajjāj ibn Arṭāh informed us, from Yaḥyā ibn ʿUbayd al-Bahrānī, from Muḥammad ibn Saʿd; he said: And he used to perform wuḍūʾ at the corner, and he came out to us one day from the open ground, and performed wuḍūʾ, and wiped over his khuffs, and we were amazed and said: What is this? He said: My father narrated to me: that he saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do the like of what I did.
items.ma-1618: Yazīd ibn Hārūn narrated to us, Ismāʿīl informed us, from Qays, he said: I heard Saʿd ibn Mālik say: By Allah, I am the first of the Arabs to shoot an arrow in the path of Allah; we used to raid with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we had no food to eat except the leaves of the ḥublah and this acacia, until one of us would drop as the sheep drops, with nothing mixed in it. Then Banū Asad have come to rebuke me about the religion; I would have failed then, and my deed would have gone astray.
items.ma-1619: Yazīd narrated to us, Abū Maʿshar informed us, from Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd, from his father, he said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ give the salām to his right and to his left.
items.ma-1620: Rawḥ narrated to us, Ibn ʿAwn narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Aswad, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd, from his father, he said: When it was the day of the Trench, and a man was shielding himself with a shield, he began to say with the shield thus, and he put it above his nose, then he would say thus, lowering it afterwards. He said: So I reached for my quiver and took out from it an arrow stained with blood, and placed it in the middle of the bow, and when he said thus, lowering the shield, I shot, and I have not forgotten the fall of the arrow on such and such [part] of the shield. He said: And he fell, and he said with his leg, and the Prophet of Allah ﷺ laughed – I think he said: until his molars appeared – He said: I said: Why? He said: At the action of the man.
items.ma-1621: Rawḥ narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, he said: I heard Muṣʿab ibn Saʿd narrating from his father Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ: that he used to command this supplication, and narrate it from the Prophet ﷺ: “O Allah, I seek refuge with You from miserliness, and I seek refuge with You from cowardice, and I seek refuge with You from being returned to the vilest of life, and I seek refuge with You from the fitnah of the world, and I seek refuge with You from the punishment of the grave.”
items.ma-1622: Ḥujayn ibn al-Muthannā and Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, both said: Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq – Abū Saʿīd said: he said: Abū Isḥāq narrated to us – from Muṣʿab ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, from his father: that he swore by al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā, and his companions said to him: You have said something foul. So he came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: The covenant was recent, and I swore by al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā. The Prophet ﷺ said to him: “Say: There is no deity except Allah alone,” three times, “and spit to your left three times, and seek refuge with Allah from Shayṭān, and do not repeat.”
items.ma-1623: ʿUthmān ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, Usāmah narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Labībah: that Saʿd ibn Mālik said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “The best remembrance is the hidden one, and the best provision is that which suffices.”
items.ma-1624: Abū Dāwūd Sulaymān narrated to us, Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd narrated to us, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Kaysān, Ibn Shihāb narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Muḥammad ibn Saʿd, from his father, he said: ʿUmar asked permission to enter upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and with him were girls whose voices had risen above his voice, and he gave him permission, so they hurried and went away. Then ʿUmar entered while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was laughing, and ʿUmar said: May Allah make your tooth laugh, O Messenger of Allah; may my father and my mother be a ransom for you. He said: “I marvelled at girls who were with me; when they heard your sound they hurried and went away.” Then he turned to them and said: O enemies of themselves, by Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is the one you were more entitled to fear than me. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Leave them, O ʿUmar, for by Allah, never has Shayṭān met you on a path except that he took a path other than your path.”
items.ma-1625: Muʿtamir ibn Sulaymān narrated to us, he said: I heard ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, from ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth, from Saʿīd ibn Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl, that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: “The truffle is from the manna, and its water is a cure for the eye.”
items.ma-1626: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, from ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth, from Saʿīd ibn Zayd, from the Prophet ﷺ: “The truffle is from the manna, and its water is a cure for the eye.”
items.ma-1627: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, my father narrated to me, ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth; he said: My father narrated to me, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said: “The truffle is from the salwā, and its water is a cure for the eye.”
items.ma-1628: Sufyān narrated to us, he said: This we memorised from al-Zuhrī, from Ṭalḥah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAwf, from Saʿīd ibn Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever is killed defending his property is a shahīd, and whoever wrongs [another] of the land by a span, he is encircled with it from seven earths.”
items.ma-1629: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from Ṣadaqah ibn al-Muthannā, Riyāḥ ibn al-Ḥārith narrated to me: that al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah was in the Greater Mosque, and with him were the people of al-Kūfah, on his right and on his left, and a man called Saʿīd ibn Zayd came to him, and al-Mughīrah greeted him and seated him at his feet on the couch. Then a man of the people of al-Kūfah came and faced al-Mughīrah, and reviled and reviled. He said: Whom is this one reviling, O Mughīrah? He said: He reviles ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib. He said: O Mughīr ibn Shuʿb, O Mughīr ibn Shuʿb – three times – shall I hear the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ being reviled in your presence, and you do not denounce it and do not change it? Then I bear witness regarding the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, to what my two ears heard and my heart retained from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, for I would not narrate a lie from him that he would ask me about when I meet him: that he said: “Abū Bakr is in Paradise, and ʿUmar is in Paradise, and ʿAlī is in Paradise, and ʿUthmān is in Paradise, and Ṭalḥah is in Paradise, and al-Zubayr is in Paradise, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān is in Paradise, and Saʿd ibn Mālik is in Paradise,” and the ninth of the believers is in Paradise; if I wished to name him, I would name him. He said: The people of the mosque clamoured, adjuring him: O Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who is the ninth? He said: You have adjured me by Allah, and Allah is Great: I am the ninth of the believers, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is the tenth. Then he followed that with an oath, he said: By Allah, a scene that a man witnesses, in which his face becomes dusty with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, is better than the deed of any of you, even if he were granted the lifespan of Nūḥ ﵇.
items.ma-1630: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Ḥuṣayn and Manṣūr, from Hilāl ibn Yisāf, from Saʿīd ibn Zayd – and Wakīʿ said once: Manṣūr said, from Saʿīd ibn Zayd, and said once: Ḥuṣayn, from Ibn Ẓālim, from Saʿīd ibn Zayd – that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Be still, Ḥirāʾ, for upon you there is only a prophet, or a ṣiddīq, or a shahīd.” He said: And upon it were the Prophet ﷺ, Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, ʿAlī, Ṭalḥah, al-Zubayr, Saʿd, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, and Saʿīd ibn Zayd, ﵃.
items.ma-1631: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥurr ibn al-Ṣayyāḥ, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Akhnas, he said: Al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah gave us a khuṭbah, and spoke ill of ʿAlī ﵁, so Saʿīd ibn Zayd stood and said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “The Prophet is in Paradise, and Abū Bakr is in Paradise, and ʿUmar is in Paradise, and ʿUthmān is in Paradise, and ʿAlī is in Paradise, and Ṭalḥah is in Paradise, and al-Zubayr is in Paradise, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf is in Paradise, and Saʿd is in Paradise,” and if I wished, I would name the tenth.
items.ma-1632: ʿUmar ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, from ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth, from Saʿīd ibn Zayd, he said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “The truffle is from the manna, and its water is a cure for the eye.”
items.ma-1633: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Hishām, and Ibn Numayr: Hishām narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from Saʿīd ibn Zayd ibn ʿAmr, from the Prophet ﷺ – Ibn Numayr said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever takes a span of the land wrongfully will be encircled with it on the Day of Resurrection, to seven earths.” Ibn Numayr said: “From seven earths.”
items.ma-1634: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, from ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth, from Saʿīd ibn Zayd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us, and in his hand was a truffle, and he said: “Do you know what this is? This is from the manna, and its water is a cure for the eye.”
items.ma-1635: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, he said: I heard ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth say: I heard Saʿīd ibn Zayd say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “The truffle is from the manna, and its water is a cure for the eye.”
items.ma-1636:
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtaybah informed me, from al-Ḥasan al-ʿUranī, from ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth, from Saʿīd ibn Zayd, from the Prophet ﷺ …
Shuʿbah said: When al-Ḥakam narrated it to me, I did not deny it from the ḥadīth of ʿAbd al-Malik.
items.ma-1637: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us. And Ḥajjāj: Shuʿbah narrated to me, from al-Ḥurr ibn Ṣayyāḥ, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Akhnas: that al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah gave a khuṭbah, and spoke ill of ʿAlī ﵁. He said: So Saʿīd ibn Zayd stood and said: I bear witness that I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “The Messenger of Allah is in Paradise, and Abū Bakr is in Paradise, and ʿUmar is in Paradise, and ʿAlī is in Paradise, and ʿUthmān is in Paradise, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān is in Paradise, and Ṭalḥah is in Paradise, and al-Zubayr is in Paradise, and Saʿd is in Paradise,” then he said: If you wish, I will inform you of the tenth. Then he mentioned himself.
items.ma-1638: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Ḥuṣayn, from Hilāl ibn Yisāf, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ẓālim, he said: Al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah gave a khuṭbah, and spoke ill of ʿAlī, so Saʿīd ibn Zayd came out and said: Do you not marvel at this one reviling ʿAlī?! I bear witness regarding the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that we were on Ḥirāʾ, or Uḥud, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Stand firm, Ḥirāʾ – or Uḥud – for upon you there is only a ṣiddīq or a shahīd.” Then the Prophet ﷺ named the ten, and he named Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, ʿAlī, Ṭalḥah, al-Zubayr, Saʿd, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, and Saʿīd named himself.
items.ma-1639:
ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from Ṭalḥah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAwf, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sahl, from Saʿīd ibn Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl, that he heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “Whoever steals a span of the land will be encircled with it from seven earths.”
Maʿmar said: And it reached me from al-Zuhrī – and I did not hear it from him – that he added in this ḥadīth: “And whoever is killed defending his property is a shahīd.”
items.ma-1640: Yazīd ibn Hārūn narrated to us, Ibn Abī Dhiʾb informed us, from al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Abū Salamah that Marwān said: Go and reconcile between these two: Saʿīd ibn Zayd and Arwā. Saʿīd said: Do you think I took anything of her right? I bear witness that I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever takes a span of the land without right will be encircled with it from seven earths; and whoever allies himself with the mawlā of a people without their permission, upon him is the curse of Allah; and whoever takes away the property of a Muslim man by an oath, may Allah not bless him in it.”
items.ma-1641: Abū al-Yamān narrated to us, Shuʿayb narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, Ṭalḥah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAwf narrated to me, that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr ibn Sahl informed him: that Saʿīd ibn Zayd said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “Whoever wrongs [another] of the land by a span, he will be encircled with it from seven earths.”
items.ma-1642: Yazīd narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from Ṭalḥah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAwf, he said: Arwā bint Uways came to me with a group of Quraysh, among them ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr ibn Sahl, and said: Saʿīd ibn Zayd has taken from my land into his land what is not his, and I would like you to come to him and speak to him. He said: So we rode to him, and he was on his land at al-ʿAqīq, and when he saw us, he said: I know what brought you, and I will narrate to you what I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; I heard him say: “Whoever takes of the land what is not his will be encircled with it to the seventh of the earths on the Day of Resurrection, and whoever is killed defending his property is a shahīd.”
items.ma-1643: Yazīd ibn ʿAbd Rabbih narrated to us, Baqiyyah ibn al-Walīd narrated to us, al-Zubaydī narrated to me, from al-Zuhrī, from Ṭalḥah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAwf, that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr ibn Sahl informed him: that Saʿīd ibn Zayd said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “Whoever wrongs [another] of the land in anything, he will be encircled with it from seven earths.”
items.ma-1644: ʿAlī ibn ʿĀṣim narrated to us, he said: Ḥuṣayn informed us, from Hilāl ibn Yisāf, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ẓālim al-Māzinī, he said: When Muʿāwiyah left al-Kūfah, he appointed al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah. He said: So he set up speakers who would speak against ʿAlī. He said: And I was beside Saʿīd ibn Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl. He said: He became angry, and stood, and took me by the hand and I followed him, and he said: Do you not see this man, who wrongs himself, who commands the cursing of a man of the people of Paradise? I bear witness regarding the nine that they are in Paradise, and if I bore witness regarding the tenth I would not be sinning. He said: I said: And what is that? He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Stand firm, Ḥirāʾ, for upon you there is only a prophet, or a ṣiddīq, or a shahīd.” He said: I said: Who are they? He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, ʿAlī, al-Zubayr, Ṭalḥah, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, and Saʿd ibn Mālik. He said: Then he fell silent. He said: I said: And who is the tenth? He said: He said: I.
items.ma-1645: Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, Zāʾidah narrated to us, Ḥuṣayn ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Hilāl ibn Yisāf, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ẓālim al-Tamīmī, from Saʿīd ibn Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl, he said: I bear witness that ʿAlī is of the people of Paradise. I said: And what is that? He said: He is among the nine, and if I wished to name the tenth, I would name him. He said: Ḥirāʾ shook, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Stand firm, Ḥirāʾ, for upon you there is only a prophet, or a ṣiddīq, or a shahīd.” He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿAlī, ʿUthmān, Ṭalḥah, al-Zubayr, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, Saʿd, and I – meaning Saʿīd himself.
items.ma-1646: Ibrāhīm ibn Abī al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, Abū Uways narrated to us, he said: Al-Zuhrī said: Ṭalḥah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAwf informed me, that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr ibn Sahl informed him, that Saʿīd ibn Zayd said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever wrongs [another] of the land in anything, he will be encircled with it in seven earths.”
items.ma-1647: Ḥammād ibn Usāmah narrated to us, Misʿar informed me, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Maysarah, from Hilāl ibn Yisāf, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ẓālim, from Saʿīd ibn Zayd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned fitnahs like portions of the dark night – I think he said: “People may go in them with the swiftest going.” He said: It was said: Are all of them destroyed, or some of them? He said: “Sufficient for them – or: by sufficiency for them – is killing.”
items.ma-1648: Yazīd narrated to us, al-Masʿūdī narrated to us, from Nufayl ibn Hishām ibn Saʿīd ibn Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl, from his father, from his grandfather, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in Makkah, he and Zayd ibn Ḥārithah, and Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl passed by them, and they invited him to a spread of food of theirs, and he said: O son of my brother, I do not eat of what is slaughtered on the stone altars. He said: Then the Prophet ﷺ was not seen after that eating anything of what was slaughtered on the stone altars. He said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, my father was as you have seen and as it has reached you, and had he reached you he would have believed in you and followed you, so ask forgiveness for him. He said: “Yes, I will ask forgiveness for him, for he will be raised on the Day of Resurrection as an ummah by himself.”
items.ma-1649: Yazīd narrated to us, Ibn Abī Dhiʾb informed us, from al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Abū Salamah, he said: Marwān said to us: Go and reconcile between these two: Saʿīd ibn Zayd and Arwā bint Uways. So we came to Saʿīd ibn Zayd and he said: Do you think I have diminished anything of her right? I bear witness, I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever takes a span of the land without right will be encircled with it from seven earths; and whoever allies himself with a people without their permission, upon him is the curse of Allah; and whoever takes away the property of his brother by his oath, may Allah not bless him in it.”
items.ma-1650: Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth, he said: I came to al-Madīnah and divided [the inheritance] with my brother, and Saʿīd ibn Zayd said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no blessing in the price of land or a house that is not put into land or a house.”
items.ma-1651: Abū al-Yamān narrated to us, Shuʿayb informed us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Ḥusayn, he said: It reached me that Luqmān used to say: O my son, do not learn knowledge in order to boast with it before the scholars, or to dispute with it with the foolish, and to show off with it in the gatherings … and he mentioned it. And he said: Nawfal ibn Musāḥiq narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Zayd, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “Among the greatest of ribā is the extension [of oneself] over the honour of a Muslim without right, and indeed this raḥim is a branch from al-Raḥmān, so whoever severs it, Allah forbids Paradise to him.”
items.ma-1652: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd al-Hāshimī narrated to us, Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd narrated to us, from his father, from Abū ʿUbaydah ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir, from Ṭalḥah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAwf, from Saʿīd ibn Zayd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever is killed defending his property is a shahīd, and whoever is killed defending his family is a shahīd, and whoever is killed defending his religion is a shahīd, and whoever is killed defending his blood is a shahīd.”
items.ma-1653: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from his father, from Abū ʿUbaydah ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAmmār, from Ṭalḥah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAwf, from Saʿīd ibn Zayd, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he mentioned the like of it.
items.ma-1654: Al-Faḍl ibn Dukayn narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm ibn Muhājir, one who heard ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth narrating narrated to me, narrating from Saʿīd ibn Zayd, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “O assembly of the Arabs, praise Allah, who has lifted from you the tithes.”
items.ma-1655: Bishr ibn al-Mufaḍḍal narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Isḥāq, from al-Zuhrī, from Muḥammad ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim, from his father, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “I witnessed the pact of al-Muṭayyabīn with my paternal uncles while I was a boy, and I would not love to have red camels and to break it.” Al-Zuhrī said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Islam did not meet any pact except that it increased it in strength, and there is no pact in Islam.” And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had brought together Quraysh and the Anṣār.
items.ma-1656: Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq narrated to me, from Makḥūl, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that ʿUmar said to him: O boy, have you heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, or from any of his Companions: when a man doubts in his prayer, what does he do? He said: While he was like that, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf came, and said: What are you two about? ʿUmar said: I asked this boy: Has he heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, or any of his Companions: when a man doubts in his prayer, what does he do? ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “When one of you doubts in his prayer, and does not know whether he has prayed one or two, let him make it one; and when he does not know whether he has prayed two or three, let him make it two; and when he does not know whether he has prayed three or four, let him make it three; then let him prostrate two prostrations when he has finished his prayer, while he is sitting, before he gives the salām.”
items.ma-1657:
Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr, he heard Bajālah say: I was a scribe for Jazʾ ibn Muʿāwiyah, the paternal uncle of al-Aḥnaf ibn Qays, and the letter of ʿUmar came to us a year before his death: Kill every sorcerer – and Sufyān sometimes said: and sorceress – and separate every one with a maḥram relation among the Majūs, and forbid them from the zamzamah. So we killed three sorcerers, and we began to separate between a man and his ḥarīmah in the Book of Allah. And Jazʾ made much food, and laid the sword across his thigh, and invited the Majūs, and they threw down the load of a mule or two mules of silver, and ate without zamzamah. And ʿUmar had not taken – and Sufyān sometimes said: accepted – the jizyah from the Majūs, until ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf bore witness that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took it from the Majūs of Hajar.
And my father said: Sufyān said: Bajālah performed Ḥajj with Muṣʿab in the year seventy.
items.ma-1658: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from al-Zuhrī, from Mālik ibn Aws: I heard ʿUmar say to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, Ṭalḥah, al-Zubayr and Saʿd: I adjure you by Allah, by whom the heaven and the earth stand – and once he said: by whose permission the heaven and the earth stand – do you know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “We are not inherited from; what we leave is ṣadaqah”? They said: O Allah, yes.
items.ma-1659: Yazīd ibn Hārūn narrated to us, Hishām al-Dastuwāʾī informed us, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qāriẓ, that his father narrated to him: that he entered upon ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, who was ill, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said to him: A raḥim has connected you. Indeed the Prophet ﷺ said: “Allah ﷿ said: I am al-Raḥmān. I created the raḥim, and I split for it from My name; whoever connects it, I will connect him, and whoever severs it, I will cut him off, and I will sever him – or he said: whoever cuts it off, I will cut him off.”
items.ma-1660: Abū Saʿīd, the mawlā of Banū Hāshim, narrated to us, al-Qāsim ibn al-Faḍl narrated to us, al-Naḍr ibn Shaybān narrated to us, he said: I met Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and said: Narrate to me something you heard from your father, which he heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, about the month of Ramaḍān. He said: Yes, my father narrated to me, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said: “Indeed Allah ﷿ made obligatory the fasting of Ramaḍān, and I have made its standing a sunnah, so whoever fasts it and stands in it out of īmān and iḥtisāb, he comes out of his sins as on the day his mother bore him.”
items.ma-1661: Yaḥyā ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Jaʿfar, that Ibn Qāriẓ informed him from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When a woman prays her five [prayers], and fasts her month, and guards her private part, and obeys her husband, it is said to her: Enter Paradise from whichever of the gates of Paradise you wish.”
items.ma-1662: Abū Salamah Manṣūr ibn Salamah al-Khuzāʿī narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, from Yazīd ibn al-Hād, from ʿAmr ibn Abī ʿAmr, from Abū al-Ḥuwayrith, from Muḥammad ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out, and I followed him until he entered date palms, and prostrated, and prolonged the prostration until I feared – or I dreaded – that Allah had taken him [in death] or seized him. He said: So I came to look, and he raised his head and said: “What is the matter with you, O ʿAbd al-Raḥmān?” He said: So I mentioned that to him. He said: And he said: “Jibrīl ﵇ said to me: Shall I not give you glad tidings? Indeed Allah ﷿ says to you: Whoever sends ṣalāh upon you, I send ṣalāh upon him, and whoever gives salām to you, I give salām to him.”
items.ma-1663: Yūnus narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, from Yazīd, from ʿAmr, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān Abū al-Ḥuwayrith, from Muḥammad ibn Jubayr, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, he said: I entered the mosque, and I saw the Messenger of Allah صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ going out of the mosque, and I followed him … and he mentioned the ḥadīth.
items.ma-1664: Abū Saʿīd, the mawlā of Banū Hāshim, narrated to us, Sulaymān ibn Bilāl narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn Abī ʿAmr narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out and headed toward his ṣadaqah, and entered, and faced the qiblah, and fell down prostrating, and prolonged the prostration, until I thought that Allah ﷿ had taken his soul in it. So I drew near to him, then sat, and he raised his head and said: “Who is this?” I said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. He said: “What is your matter?” I said: O Messenger of Allah, you prostrated a prostration in which I feared that Allah ﷿ had taken your soul. He said: “Indeed Jibrīl ﵇ came to me and gave me glad tidings, and said: Indeed Allah ﷿ says: Whoever sends ṣalāh upon you, I send ṣalāh upon him, and whoever gives salām to you, I give salām to him. So I prostrated to Allah ﷿ in thanks.”
items.ma-1665: Haytham ibn Khārijah narrated to us – Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: And I myself heard it from al-Haytham ibn Khārijah –, Rishdīn narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Walīd, that he heard Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrating from his father: that he was with the Prophet ﷺ on a journey, and the Prophet ﷺ went off for his need, and the time of prayer reached them, so they established the prayer, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān went forward before them, then the Prophet ﷺ came, and prayed with the people, behind him, one rakʿah, and when he gave the salām, he said: “You have done right – or: You have done well.”
items.ma-1666: Rawḥ narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥafṣah narrated to us, al-Zuhrī narrated to us, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “When the epidemic is in a land and you are not in it, do not enter it, and when it is in a land and you are in it, do not leave it.”
items.ma-1667: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, from Yazīd ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qusayṭ, from Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf: that some people of the Arabs came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at al-Madīnah and accepted Islam, and an epidemic of al-Madīnah afflicted them: its fever, so they were overturned, and they left al-Madīnah, and a group of his Companions – meaning the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ – met them and said to them: What is the matter with you that you returned? They said: The epidemic of al-Madīnah afflicted us, and we found al-Madīnah unsuitable. They said: Do you not have an example in the Messenger of Allah? Some of them said: They have become hypocrites, and some of them said: They have not become hypocrites, they are Muslims. So Allah ﷿ revealed: {Then what is the matter with you that you are two parties concerning the hypocrites, while Allah has overturned them for what they earned} the verse [al-Nisāʾ: 88].
items.ma-1668: Hāshim ibn al-Qāsim narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir ibn Rabīʿah, he said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb ﵁ heard the voice of Ibn al-Mughtarif – or Ibn al-Gharif – the camel-driver, in the middle of the night, while we were going to Makkah, so ʿUmar urged his mount on until he joined the people, and he was with ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. When the dawn broke, ʿUmar said: Enough now, be silent now, the dawn has broken, remember Allah. He said: Then he noticed on ʿAbd al-Raḥmān two khuffs, and said: Two khuffs?! He said: I wore them with one better than you, or with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. ʿUmar said: I insist that you take them off, for I fear that the people will look at you and follow you.
items.ma-1669: He said: And Isḥāq ibn ʿĪsā narrated it to us, Sharīk narrated to us, and he mentioned it with its isnād and said: I wore them with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-1670: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, Hishām ibn ʿUrwah narrated to us, from ʿUrwah, that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ granted me and ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb land of such and such. So al-Zubayr went to the family of ʿUmar and bought his share from them, then he came to ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān and said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf claims that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ granted him and ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb land of such and such, and I have bought the share of the family of ʿUmar. ʿUthmān said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān is acceptable in testimony, for him and against him.
items.ma-1671: Al-Ḥakam ibn Nāfiʿ narrated to us, Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh narrated to us, from Ḍamḍam ibn Zurʿah, from Shurayḥ ibn ʿUbayd, he refers it to Mālik ibn Yukhāmir, from Ibn al-Saʿdī, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Hijrah does not cease as long as the enemy is fought.” Muʿāwiyah, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Hijrah is two qualities: one of them is that you forsake evil deeds, and the other is that you migrate to Allah and His Messenger; and hijrah does not cease as long as repentance is accepted, and repentance does not cease to be accepted until the sun rises from the west, and when it rises, every heart is sealed with what is in it, and the people are relieved of the deed.”
items.ma-1672: Abū al-Mughīrah narrated to us, Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz narrated to us, Sulaymān ibn Mūsā narrated to me, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, he said: When the Majūsī left the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I asked him, and he informed me that the Prophet ﷺ gave him a choice between the jizyah and being killed, and he chose the jizyah.
items.ma-1673: Abū Salamah Yūsuf ibn Yaʿqūb al-Mājishūn narrated to us, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, from his father, from his grandfather ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, that he said: I was standing on the day of Badr in the row, I looked to my right and to my left, and behold, I was between two boys of the Anṣār, young in age, and I wished that I were between stronger men than they. One of them nudged me and said: O uncle, do you know Abū Jahl? He said: I said: Yes, and what do you want with him, O son of my brother? He said: It has reached me that he reviled the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and by Him in Whose Yad is my soul, if I see him, my figure will not leave his figure until the quicker of us dies. He said: Then the other nudged me and said to me the like of it. He said: I marvelled at that. He said: And I had not lingered when I looked at Abū Jahl, moving about among the people, and I said to them: Do you not see? This is your companion about whom you ask. So they hurried to him, and he faced them, and they struck him until they killed him, then they turned back to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and informed him, and he said: “Which of you killed him?” Each one of them said: I killed him. He said: “Have you wiped your swords?” They said: No. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked at the two swords and said: “Both of you killed him,” and he ruled his spoil for Muʿādh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ, and they were: Muʿādh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ and Muʿādh ibn ʿAfrāʾ.
items.ma-1674: ʿAffān narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from ʿUmar ibn Abī Salamah, from his father, he said: The storyteller of the people of Palestine narrated to me, he said: I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Three – and by Him in Whose Yad is the soul of Muḥammad, I was indeed one who swears upon them: wealth does not decrease from ṣadaqah, so give ṣadaqah; and a servant does not pardon a wrong, seeking by it Wajh Allāh, except that Allah raises him by it in honour – and Abū Saʿīd, the mawlā of Banū Hāshim, said: except that Allah increases him by it in honour on the Day of Resurrection – and a servant does not open a door of asking except that Allah opens upon him a door of poverty.”
items.ma-1675: Qutaybah ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Muḥammad al-Darāwardī narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥumayd, from his father, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Abū Bakr is in Paradise, and ʿUmar is in Paradise, and ʿAlī is in Paradise, and ʿUthmān is in Paradise, and Ṭalḥah is in Paradise, and al-Zubayr is in Paradise, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf is in Paradise, and Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ is in Paradise, and Saʿīd ibn Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl is in Paradise, and Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ is in Paradise.”
items.ma-1676: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Ibn Isḥāq – meaning ʿAbd al-Raḥmān – narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from Muḥammad ibn Jubayr, from his father, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I witnessed, as a boy with my paternal uncles, the pact of al-Muṭayyabīn, and I would not love to have red camels and to break it.”
items.ma-1677:
Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, Makḥūl narrated to me, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When one of you prays and doubts in his prayer, then if he doubts between one and two, let him make them one; and if he doubts between two and three, let him make them two; and if he doubts between three and four, let him make them three, so that the uncertainty is in the addition; then let him prostrate two prostrations before he gives the salām, then he gives the salām.”
Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq said: And Ḥusayn ibn ʿAbd Allāh said to me: Did he give you an isnād for it? I said: No. He said: But he narrated to me that Kurayb, the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās, narrated to him from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I sat with ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and he said: O Ibn ʿAbbās, when a man is confused in his prayer, and does not know whether he has added or decreased? I said: By Allah, O Commander of the Believers, I do not know; I have not heard anything about that. ʿUmar said: By Allah, I do not know. He said: While we were thus, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf came and said: What is this that you two are discussing? ʿUmar said to him: We mentioned the man who doubts in his prayer, what he should do. He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say … this ḥadīth.
items.ma-1678: Ḥajjāj and Yazīd narrated to us, in meaning, both said: Ibn Abī Dhiʾb informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from Sālim, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir ibn Rabīʿah: that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf informed ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, while he was travelling on the road to al-Shām, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “This sickness is that with which the nations before you were punished, so when you hear of it in a land, do not enter it upon it, and when it occurs in a land while you are in it, do not go out in flight from it.” He said: So ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb returned from al-Shām.
items.ma-1679: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Nawfal, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, he said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb went out intending al-Shām … and he mentioned the ḥadīth. He said: And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf was absent, and he came and said: I have knowledge of this: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “When you hear of it in a land, do not come upon it, and when it occurs in a land while you are in it, do not go out in flight from it.”
items.ma-1680: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to me, that Raddād al-Laythī informed him, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Allah ﷿ said: I am al-Raḥmān. I created the raḥim, and I split for it from My name a name, so whoever connects it, I connect him, and whoever severs it, I sever him.”
items.ma-1681: Bishr ibn Shuʿayb ibn Abī Ḥamzah narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from al-Zuhrī, Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to me, that Abū al-Raddād al-Laythī informed him, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Allah ﷿ said: I am al-Raḥmān, and I created the raḥim, and I derived for it from My name; so whoever connects it, Allah connects him, and whoever severs it, I sever him.”
items.ma-1682: Isḥāq ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us, Mālik informed me, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir ibn Rabīʿah, that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb went out to al-Shām, and when he came to Sargh, it reached him that the epidemic had occurred in al-Shām, so ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf informed him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When you hear of it in a land, do not come upon it, and when it occurs in a land while you are in it, do not go out in flight from it.” So ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb returned from Sargh.
items.ma-1683: Isḥāq ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us, Mālik informed me, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Nawfal, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās: that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb went out to al-Shām, until when he was at Sargh, the commanders of the armies met him: Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ and his companions, and they informed him that the epidemic had occurred in al-Shām … and he mentioned the ḥadīth. He said: Then ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf came, who had been absent on some need of his, and said: I have knowledge of this; I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “When it is in a land while you are in it, do not go out in flight from it, and when you hear of it in a land, do not come upon it.” He said: So ʿUmar praised Allah, then turned back.
items.ma-1684: Abū al-ʿAlāʾ al-Ḥasan ibn Sawwār narrated to us, Hishām ibn Saʿd narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “When you hear of it in a land and you are not in it, do not enter it, and when it occurs while you are in it, do not go out from it in flight.”
items.ma-1685: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj informed us, ʿAmr ibn Dīnār informed me, from Bajālah al-Tamīmī, he said: ʿUmar did not intend to take the jizyah from the Majūs, until ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf bore witness that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took it from the Majūs of Hajar.
items.ma-1686: Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from Abū Salamah, he said: Abū al-Raddād fell ill, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf visited him, and Abū al-Raddād said: The best of them and the most connecting of them; I have not known Abū Muḥammad [otherwise]. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Allah ﷿ said: I am Allah, and I am al-Raḥmān. I created the raḥim, and I split for it from My name; whoever connects it, I connect him, and whoever severs it, I sever him.”
items.ma-1687: Yazīd ibn Hārūn narrated to us, Hishām informed us, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qāriẓ, that his father narrated to him: that he entered upon ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf while he was ill, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said to him: A raḥim has connected you. Indeed the Prophet ﷺ said: “Allah said: I am al-Raḥmān, and I created the raḥim, and I split for it from My name; whoever connects it, I will connect him, and whoever cuts it off, I will cut him off – or he said: whoever severs it, I will sever him.”
items.ma-1688: Surayj ibn al-Nuʿmān narrated to us, Nūḥ ibn Qays narrated to us, from Naṣr ibn ʿAlī al-Jahḍamī, from al-Naḍr ibn Shaybān al-Ḥuddānī, from Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, he said: I said to him: Will you not narrate to me a ḥadīth from your father that your father heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? He said: Ramaḍān approached, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed Ramaḍān is a month whose fasting Allah ﷿ made obligatory, and I have made its standing a sunnah for the Muslims, so whoever fasts it out of īmān and iḥtisāb comes out of sins as on the day his mother bore him.”
items.ma-1689: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: I found this ḥadīth in my father's book in his own handwriting: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd narrated to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Muslim, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that he was discussing with ʿUmar the matter of the prayer, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf came up to them and said: Shall I not narrate to you a ḥadīth that I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? They said: Yes. He said: I bear witness that I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever prays a prayer, doubting regarding the decrease, let him pray until he doubts regarding the addition.”
items.ma-1690: Ziyād ibn al-Rabīʿ Abū Khidāsh narrated to us, Wāṣil, the mawlā of Abū ʿUyaynah, narrated to us, from Bashshār ibn Abī Sayf al-Jarmī, [from al-Walīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Jurashī], from ʿIyāḍ ibn Ghuṭayf, he said: We entered upon Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ visiting him in an illness that had afflicted him, and his wife Tuḥayfah was sitting at his head. We said: How did Abū ʿUbaydah spend the night? She said: By Allah, he spent the night in reward. Abū ʿUbaydah said: I did not spend the night in reward. And he was facing the wall with his face, and he turned his face to the people and said: Will you not ask me about what I said? They said: What you said did not please us, so that we should ask you about it. He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever spends a surplus expenditure in the path of Allah, then it is by seven hundred; and whoever spends on himself and his family, or visits a sick person, or removes harm, then the good deed is by ten times its like; and fasting is a shield as long as one does not tear it; and whoever Allah afflicts with an affliction in his body, it is for him a ḥiṭṭah.”
items.ma-1691: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, Ibrāhīm ibn Maymūn narrated to us, Saʿd ibn Samurah ibn Jundub narrated to us, from his father, from Abū ʿUbaydah, he said: The last thing the Prophet ﷺ spoke was: “Expel the Jews of the people of al-Ḥijāz, and the people of Najrān, from the Arabian Peninsula, and know that the worst of people are those who took the graves of their prophets as mosques.”
items.ma-1692: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Khālid, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaqīq, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Surāqah, from Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ, from the Prophet ﷺ: that he mentioned the Dajjāl, and described him with a description that I do not remember. They said: O Messenger of Allah, how will our hearts be that day? Like today? He said: “Or better.”
items.ma-1693: ʿAffān and ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, both said: Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, Khālid al-Ḥadhdhāʾ informed us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaqīq, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Surāqah, from Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “There was no prophet after Nūḥ except that he warned his people of the Dajjāl, and I warn you of him.” He said: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ described him to us, and said: “Perhaps some of those who saw me or heard my words will reach him.” They said: O Messenger of Allah, how will our hearts be that day? Like they are today? He said: “Or better.”
items.ma-1694: Abū Aḥmad al-Zubayrī narrated to us, Ibrāhīm ibn Maymūn narrated to us, from Saʿd ibn Samurah, from Samurah ibn Jundub, from Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ, he said: The last thing the Prophet of Allah ﷺ spoke was that: “Expel the Jews of al-Ḥijāz from the Arabian Peninsula, and know that the worst of people are those who take the graves as mosques.”
items.ma-1695: Ismāʿīl ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from al-Ḥajjāj ibn Arṭāh, from al-Walīd ibn Abī Mālik, from al-Qāsim, from Abū Umāmah, he said: A man of the Muslims granted protection to a man, while Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ was over the army, and Khālid ibn al-Walīd and ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ said: Do not grant him protection. Abū ʿUbaydah said: We grant him protection; I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “One of them grants protection on behalf of the Muslims.”
items.ma-1696: Abū al-Mughīrah narrated to us, Ṣafwān ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, Abū Ḥisbah Muslim ibn Akyas, the mawlā of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir, narrated to us, from Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ, he said: He mentioned one who entered upon him and found him weeping, and he said: What makes you weep, O Abū ʿUbaydah? He said: We weep because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one day mentioned what Allah would open for the Muslims, and bestow upon them as fayʾ, until he mentioned al-Shām, and said: “If your appointed term is deferred, O Abū ʿUbaydah, three servants are sufficient for you: a servant who serves you, and a servant who travels with you, and a servant who serves your family and returns to them; and three mounts are sufficient for you: a mount for your saddle, and a mount for your baggage, and a mount for your boy.” Then here I am, looking at my house filled with slaves, and looking at my stable filled with beasts and horses, so how will I meet the Messenger of Allah ﷺ after this? And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had enjoined us: “Indeed the dearest of you to me, and the nearest of you to me, is the one who meets me in the like of the state in which he parted from me.”
items.ma-1697:
Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, Abān ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to me, from Shahr ibn Ḥawshab al-Ashʿarī, from his stepfather: a man of his people who had succeeded his father with his mother, who had witnessed the plague of ʿAmawās, he said: When the pain flared up, Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ stood among the people giving a khuṭbah and said: O people, this pain is the mercy of your Rabb, the supplication of your Prophet, and the death of the righteous before you, and indeed Abū ʿUbaydah asks Allah to apportion to him his share of it.
He said: Then he was stricken and died, ﵀, and Muʿādh ibn Jabal was appointed over the people, and he stood after him giving a khuṭbah and said: O people, this pain is the mercy of your Rabb, the supplication of your Prophet, and the death of the righteous before you, and indeed Muʿādh asks Allah to apportion to the family of Muʿādh their share of it. He said: Then his son ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Muʿādh was stricken and died, then he stood and supplicated his Rabb for himself, and he was stricken in his palm, and I saw him looking at it, then kissing the back of his hand, then saying: I would not love to have anything of the world in exchange for what is in you. When he died, ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ was appointed over the people, and he stood among us giving a khuṭbah and said: O people, this pain, when it occurs, only flares up like the flaring of fire, so betake yourselves to the mountains from it. He said: Abū Wāthilah al-Hudhalī said to him: You have lied! By Allah, I accompanied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and you are worse than this donkey of mine! He said: By Allah, I will not answer you in what you say, and by Allah, we will not stay in it. Then he went out, and the people went out, and they dispersed from it, and Allah repelled it from them. He said: That reached ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, from the opinion of ʿAmr, and by Allah he did not dislike it.
Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal said: Abān ibn Ṣāliḥ is the grandfather of Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān Mushkudānah.
items.ma-1698: Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿAdī narrated to us, from Dāwūd, from ʿĀmir, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent the army of Dhāt al-Salāsil, and appointed Abū ʿUbaydah over the Muhājirūn, and appointed ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ over the bedouins, and said to them: Obey each other. He said: And they were commanded to raid Bakr, so ʿAmr went and raided Quḍāʿah, because Bakr were his maternal uncles. So al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah went to Abū ʿUbaydah and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed you over us, and the son of so-and-so has taken charge of the affair of the people, and you have no command with him. Abū ʿUbaydah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to obey each other, so I obey the Messenger of Allah ﷺ even if ʿAmr disobeys him.
items.ma-1699: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Ibrāhīm ibn Maymūn, the mawlā of the family of Samurah, narrated to me, from Isḥāq ibn Saʿd ibn Samurah, from his father, from Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ, he said: Indeed the last thing the Prophet ﷺ spoke, he said: “Expel the Jews of the people of al-Ḥijāz and the people of Najrān from the Arabian Peninsula.”
items.ma-1700: Yazīd ibn Hārūn narrated to us, Hishām informed us, from Wāṣil, from al-Walīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿIyāḍ ibn Ghuṭayf, he said: We entered upon Abū ʿUbaydah visiting him, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever spends a surplus expenditure in the path of Allah, then it is by seven hundred. And whoever spends on himself, or on his family, or visits a sick person, or removes harm from a road, it is a good deed by ten times its like; and fasting is a shield as long as one does not tear it; and whoever Allah afflicts with an affliction in his body, it is for him a ḥiṭṭah.”
items.ma-1701: Yazīd narrated to us, Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim informed us, Bashshār ibn Abī Sayf narrated to us, from al-Walīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿIyāḍ ibn Ghuṭayf, he said: We entered upon Abū ʿUbaydah … and he mentioned the ḥadīth.
items.ma-1702: Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿAdī narrated to us, from Sulaymān – meaning al-Taymī –, from Abū ʿUthmān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr, he said: Abū Bakr ﵁ came with a guest of his – or with guests of his – he said: and he spent the evening with the Prophet ﷺ. He said: When he spent the evening, my mother said to him: You have been kept from your guest – or your guests – since the night began. He said: Did you not give them supper? She said: No. She said: I offered that to him – or to them – and they refused – or he refused. He said: Abū Bakr became angry, and swore that he would not eat of it, and the guest – or the guests – swore that they would not eat of it until he ate of it. So Abū Bakr said: If this was from Shayṭān. He said: Then he called for the food, and ate, and they ate. He said: They did not raise a morsel except that it grew from beneath it more than it. He said: O sister of Banū Firās, what is this? He said: She said: O delight of the eye, it is now more than it was before we ate. So they ate, and he sent it to the Prophet ﷺ, and he mentioned that he ate of it.
items.ma-1703: ʿĀrim narrated to us, Muʿtamir ibn Sulaymān narrated to us, from his father, from Abū ʿUthmān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr, that he said: We were with the Prophet ﷺ, a hundred and thirty, and the Prophet ﷺ said: “Is there food with any of you?” And with one man there was a ṣāʿ of food, or about that, and it was kneaded, then a polytheist man, dishevelled and tall, came driving sheep, and the Prophet ﷺ said: “A sale or a gift?” – or he said: “or a present?” He said: No, rather a sale. So he bought a sheep from him, and it was prepared, and the Prophet of Allah ﷺ commanded that the blackness of the belly be roasted. He said: By Allah, there was none of the hundred and thirty except that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ cut a piece for him from the blackness of its belly; if he was present, he gave it to him, and if he was absent, he set it aside for him. He said: And he made two bowls of it. He said: So we all ate and were satisfied, and there was a surplus in the two bowls, and we put it on the camel – or as he said.
items.ma-1704: ʿĀrim and ʿAffān narrated to us, both said: Muʿtamir ibn Sulaymān narrated to us; ʿAffān said in his ḥadīth: He said: I heard my father, Abū ʿUthmān narrated to us, that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr narrated to him: that the People of the Ṣuffah were poor people, and that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ once said: “Whoever has food for two, let him go with a third – and ʿAffān said: with three – and whoever has food for four, let him go with a fifth, a sixth,” or as he said, and that Abū Bakr came with three, and the Prophet ﷺ went with ten, and Abū Bakr with three – ʿAffān said: with a sixth –.
items.ma-1705: Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us, from ʿAmr – meaning Ibn Dīnār – ʿAmr ibn Aws al-Thaqafī informed him, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr informed me, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded me to mount ʿĀʾishah behind me to al-Tanʿīm and have her perform ʿumrah.
items.ma-1706: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bakr al-Sahmī narrated to us, Hishām ibn Ḥassān narrated to us, from al-Qāsim ibn Mihrān, from Mūsā ibn ʿUbayd, from Maymūn ibn Mihrān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed my Rabb gave me seventy thousand of my ummah who will enter Paradise without reckoning.” ʿUmar said: O Messenger of Allah, would you not ask Him for more? He said: “I asked Him for more, and He gave me with every man seventy thousand.” ʿUmar said: Would you not ask for more? He said: “I asked Him for more, and He gave me with every man seventy thousand.” ʿUmar said: Would you not ask for more? He said: “I asked Him for more, and He gave me thus.” And ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bakr spread his hands apart, and ʿAbd Allāh said: and he stretched out his two arms, and ʿAbd Allāh scooped. And Hishām said: And this is from Allah; its number is not known.
items.ma-1707: Yazīd narrated to us, Ṣadaqah ibn Mūsā informed us, from Abū ʿImrān al-Jawnī, from Qays ibn Zayd, from the judge of the two cities, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed Allah ﷿ will call the one with a debt on the Day of Resurrection, and stand him bayna yadayhi, and say: O My servant, in what did you spend away the property of the people? He will say: O Rabb, You know that I did not ruin it; it went in a drowning, or a burning, or a theft, or a loss. Then Allah ﷿ will call for something and place it in his balance, so his good deeds will outweigh.”
items.ma-1708: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, Ṣadaqah narrated to us, Abū ʿImrān narrated to us, Qays ibn Zayd narrated to me, from the judge of the two cities, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Allah will call the one with a debt on the Day of Resurrection, until he is made to stand bayna yadayhi, and it is said: O son of Ādam, in what did you take this debt, and in what did you lose the rights of the people? He says: O Rabb, You know that I took it, and I did not eat, and did not drink, and did not wear, and did not lose it, but there came upon my hands either a burning, or a theft, or a loss. Then Allah ﷿ says: My servant has spoken truly; I am the most entitled of those who settle on your behalf today. Then Allah will call for something and place it in the pan of his balance, so his good deeds outweigh his evil deeds, and he enters Paradise by the favour of His mercy.”
items.ma-1709: ʿAlī ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh – meaning Ibn al-Mubārak – informed us, Zakariyyā ibn Isḥāq informed us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, that his father narrated to him that one who heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr say informed him: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Saddle this she-camel, then take your sister behind you, and when you both descend from the hill of al-Tanʿīm, then make ihlāl and proceed.” And that was the night of the ṣadar.
items.ma-1710: Dāwūd ibn Mihrān al-Dabbāgh narrated to us, Dāwūd – meaning al-ʿAṭṭār – narrated to us, from Ibn Khuthaym, from Yūsuf ibn Māhak, from Ḥafṣah, daughter of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, from her father, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān: “Take your sister behind you – meaning ʿĀʾishah – and have her perform ʿumrah from al-Tanʿīm; and when you descend with her from the hill, command her to enter iḥrām, for it is an accepted ʿumrah.”
items.ma-1711: ʿĀrim narrated to us, Muʿtamir ibn Sulaymān narrated to us, from his father, from Abū ʿUthmān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr, that he said: We were with the Prophet ﷺ, a hundred and thirty, and the Prophet ﷺ said: “Is there food with any of you?” And with one man there was a ṣāʿ of food, or about that, and it was kneaded, then a polytheist man, dishevelled and tall, came driving sheep, and the Prophet ﷺ said: “A sale or a gift?” – or he said: “or a grant?” He said: No, rather a sale. So he bought a sheep from him, and it was prepared, and the Prophet of Allah ﷺ commanded that the blackness of the belly be roasted. He said: By Allah, there was none of the hundred and thirty except that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ cut a piece for him from the blackness of its belly; if he was present, he gave it to him, and if he was absent, he set it aside for him. He said: And he made two bowls of it. He said: So we all ate and were satisfied, and there was a surplus in the two bowls, and we loaded it onto a camel. Or as he said.
items.ma-1712: ʿĀrim narrated to us, Muʿtamir ibn Sulaymān narrated to us, from his father, Abū ʿUthmān narrated to us, that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr narrated to him: that the People of the Ṣuffah were poor people, and that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ once said: “Whoever has food for two, let him go with a third; whoever has food for four, let him go with a fifth, a sixth,” or as he said, and that Abū Bakr came with three, and the Prophet of Allah ﷺ went with ten, and Abū Bakr with three. He said: And it was I, my father and my mother – and I do not know whether he said: and my wife – and a servant shared between our house and the house of Abū Bakr, and Abū Bakr dined with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then remained until the ʿIshāʾ prayer was prayed, then returned, and remained until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ dozed, and he came after what Allah willed of the night had passed, and his wife said to him: What kept you from your guests – or she said: your guest? He said: Did you not give them supper? She said: They refused until you came; they offered it to them and they overcame them. He said: So I went and hid. He said: And he said: O ʿAntar – or: O Ghunthar. So he abused and reviled, and said: Eat, no pleasure to you, and said: By Allah, I will never eat it. He said: And the guest swore that he would not eat it until Abū Bakr ate it. He said: Abū Bakr said: This is from Shayṭān. He said: Then he called for the food and ate. He said: By Allah, we did not take a morsel except that it grew from beneath it more than it. He said: Until they were satisfied, and it became more than it had been before that, and Abū Bakr looked at it and behold it was as it was, or more, and said to his wife: O sister of Banū Firās, what is this? She said: No, by the delight of my eye, it is now more than before, three times over. So Abū Bakr ate of it, and said: That was only from Shayṭān – meaning his oath – then he ate a morsel of it, then carried it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and it remained with him until morning. He said: And there was a pact between us and a people, and the term passed, so we appointed twelve men, with each man were people – Allah knows how many with each man – except that he sent with them, and they all ate of it, or as he said.
items.ma-1713: ʿAffān narrated to us, Muʿtamir ibn Sulaymān narrated to us, he said: I heard my father say: Abū ʿUthmān narrated to us, that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr narrated to him: that the People of the Ṣuffah were poor people, and that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever has food for two, let him go with three; and whoever has food for four, let him go with a fifth, a sixth.” Or as he said, and that Abū Bakr came with three, and the Prophet of Allah ﷺ went with ten. He said: And it was I, my father and my mother – and I do not know whether he said: my wife – and a servant shared between our house and the house of Abū Bakr رَضِيَ اللهُ تَعَالَى عَنْهُ.
items.ma-1714: ʿAlī ibn Baḥr narrated to us, ʿĪsā ibn Yūnus narrated to us, ʿUthmān ibn Ḥakīm narrated to us, Khālid ibn Salamah narrated to us, that ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān invited Mūsā ibn Ṭalḥah when he held a wedding for his son, and said: O Abū ʿĪsā, how has it reached you about the ṣalāh upon the Prophet ﷺ? Mūsā said: I asked Zayd ibn Khārijah about the ṣalāh upon the Prophet ﷺ, and Zayd said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ myself: How is the ṣalāh upon you? He said: “Send ṣalāh and strive, then say: O Allah, bless Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, as You blessed the family of Ibrāhīm; indeed You are al-Ḥamīd, al-Majīd.”
items.ma-1715: ʿAlī ibn Baḥr narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, from Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbbād, from his father ʿAbbād ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr, he said: Al-Ḥārith ibn Khuzamah came with these two verses from the end of Barāʾah: {There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves} to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and he said: Who is with you on this? He said: I do not know, by Allah, except that I bear witness that I heard them from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and retained them, and memorised them. ʿUmar said: And I bear witness that I heard them from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then he said: If they were three verses, I would have made them a separate sūrah, so look to a sūrah of the Qurʾān and place them in it. So I placed them at the end of Barāʾah.
items.ma-1716: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd – meaning Abū Dāwūd al-Ṭayālisī – narrated to us, Abū ʿĀmir al-Khazzāz narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan, from Saʿd, the mawlā of Abū Bakr, he said: I presented dates before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they began to pair [them], and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Do not pair.”
items.ma-1717: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd narrated to us, Abū ʿĀmir narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan, from Saʿd, the mawlā of Abū Bakr – and he used to serve the Prophet ﷺ, and his service pleased the Prophet ﷺ – and he said: “O Abū Bakr, free Saʿd.” He said: O Messenger of Allah, we have no servant other than him. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Free Saʿd; men are coming to you, men are coming to you.” Abū Dāwūd said: Meaning captives.
items.ma-1718: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Yūnus ibn Abī Isḥāq narrated to us, from Burayd ibn Abī Maryam al-Salūlī, from Abū al-Ḥawrāʾ, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught me words to say in the qunūt of the witr: “O Allah, guide me among those You have guided, and grant me well-being among those You have granted well-being, and take charge of me among those whose charge You have taken, and bless me in what You have given, and protect me from the evil of what You have decreed, for You decree and nothing is decreed against You; indeed he whom You befriend is not humbled. Blessed are You, our Rabb, and Exalted.”
items.ma-1719: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sharīk, from Abū Isḥāq, from Hubayrah: Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ﵁ gave us a khuṭbah, and said: A man parted from you yesterday whom the earlier ones did not precede in knowledge, and the later ones will not reach; the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to send him with the banner, Jibrīl on his right and Mīkāʾīl on his left; he would not turn back until it was opened for him.
items.ma-1720: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Isrāʾīl, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAmr ibn Ḥubshī, he said: Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī gave us a khuṭbah after the killing of ʿAlī ﵄, and said: A man parted from you yesterday whom the earlier ones did not precede in knowledge, nor did the later ones reach; the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to send him and give him the banner, and he would not turn back until it was opened for him; and he left neither yellow nor white, except seven hundred dirhams of his stipend that he was setting aside for a servant for his family.
items.ma-1721: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Burayd ibn Abī Maryam, from Abū al-Ḥawrāʾ, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught him to say in the witr … and he mentioned the like of the ḥadīth of Yūnus.
items.ma-1722: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād informed us, from al-Ḥajjāj ibn Arṭāh, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī: that a funeral passed by them, and the people stood and he did not stand, and al-Ḥasan said: What have you done? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood only out of being harmed by the odour of the Jew.
items.ma-1723:
Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, Burayd ibn Abī Maryam narrated to me, from Abū al-Ḥawrāʾ al-Saʿdī, he said: I said to al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī: What do you remember of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? He said: I remember that I took a date from the dates of ṣadaqah and put it in my mouth, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pulled it out with its saliva and threw it among the dates, and a man said to him: What would it matter if he ate this date? He said: “Indeed we do not eat ṣadaqah.”
He said: And he used to say: “Leave what makes you doubt for what does not make you doubt, for truthfulness is tranquillity, and falsehood is doubt.”
He said: And he used to teach us this supplication: “O Allah, guide me among those You have guided, and grant me well-being among those You have granted well-being, and take charge of me among those whose charge You have taken, and bless me in what You have given, and protect me from the evil of what You have decreed, for You decree and nothing is decreed against You; indeed he whom You befriend is not humbled.”, and sometimes he said: “Blessed are You, our Rabb, and Exalted.”
items.ma-1724: Muḥammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, Thābit ibn ʿUmārah narrated to us, Rabīʿah ibn Shaybān narrated to us, that he said to al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ﵁: What do you remember of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? He said: He brought me into the room of ṣadaqah, and I took a date from it and put it in my mouth, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Throw it out, for it is not lawful for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, nor for anyone of his household.”
items.ma-1725: Abū Aḥmad – he is al-Zubayrī – narrated to us, al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, Burayd ibn Abī Maryam narrated to us, from Abū al-Ḥawrāʾ, he said: We were with Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, and he was asked: What did you comprehend of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? – or: about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? He said: I was walking with him, and he passed by a threshing floor of dates of ṣadaqah, and I took a date and put it in my mouth, and he took it with my saliva, and some of the people said: What would it matter if you left it? He said: “Indeed we, the family of Muḥammad, ṣadaqah is not lawful for us.” He said: And I comprehended from him the five prayers.
items.ma-1726: ʿAffān narrated to us, Yazīd – meaning Ibn Ibrāhīm – and he is al-Tustarī – narrated to us, Muḥammad narrated to us, he said: I was informed that a funeral passed by al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī and Ibn ʿAbbās ﵃, and al-Ḥasan stood and Ibn ʿAbbās sat, and al-Ḥasan said to Ibn ʿAbbās: Have you not seen that a funeral passed by the Prophet ﷺ and he stood? Ibn ʿAbbās said: Yes, and he sat. And al-Ḥasan did not deny what Ibn ʿAbbās said, ﵄.
items.ma-1727:
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: I heard Burayd ibn Abī Maryam narrating from Abū al-Ḥawrāʾ, he said: I said to al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī: “What do you remember of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?” He said: “I remember of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that I took a date from the dates of the ṣadaqah and put it in my mouth.” He said: “So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ removed it with its saliva and put it among the dates. Then it was said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what would it have mattered to you about this date, for this boy?' He said: 'Indeed we, the family of Muḥammad, ṣadaqah is not lawful for us.'”
He said: And he used to say: “Leave what makes you doubt for what does not make you doubt, for truthfulness is tranquillity, and falsehood is doubt.”
He said: And he used to teach us this supplication: “O Allah, guide me among those whom You have guided, grant me well-being among those whom You have granted well-being, befriend me among those whom You have befriended, bless for me what You have given, and protect me from the evil of what You have decreed. Indeed You decree, and nothing is decreed against You. Indeed, he whom You have befriended is not humiliated.” Shuʿbah said: And I think he also said this: “Tabārakta, our Rabb, wa-taʿālayta.” Shuʿbah said: And someone who heard this from him had narrated to me. Then Shuʿbah narrated this ḥadīth at his going out to al-Mahdī after the death of his father, and he had no doubt about: “Tabārakta wa-taʿālayta.” So I said to Shuʿbah: “You doubt it?” He said: “There is no doubt in it.”
items.ma-1728: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn: that a funeral procession passed by Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, so one of them stood and the other sat. The one who stood said: “Do you not know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood?” He said: “Yes, and he sat.”
items.ma-1729: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb al-Thaqafī narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from Muḥammad: that al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī and Ibn ʿAbbās saw a funeral procession, so one of them stood and the other sat. The one who stood said: “Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ not stand?” And the one who sat said: “Yes, and he sat.”
items.ma-1730: Wakīʿ and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, they said: Sufyān narrated to us, from Muṣʿab ibn Muḥammad, from Yaʿlā ibn Abī Yaḥyā, from Fāṭimah bint Ḥusayn, from her father — ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī — he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The one who asks has a right, even if he comes on a horse.”
items.ma-1731: Wakīʿ informed us, Thābit ibn ʿUmārah narrated to us, from Rabīʿah ibn Shaybān, he said: I said to al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī ﵁: “What do you remember from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?” He said: “I climbed up to an upper room and took a date and rolled it around in my mouth, so the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Throw it out, for indeed ṣadaqah is not lawful for us.'”
items.ma-1732: Ibn Numayr and Yaʿlā narrated to us, they said: Ḥajjāj — meaning Ibn Dīnār al-Wāsiṭī — narrated to us, from Shuʿayb ibn Khālid, from Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed, part of the excellence of a man's Islam is little speech about what does not concern him.”
items.ma-1733: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, Ibn Jurayj informed us, he said: I heard Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī claiming, from Ḥusayn and Ibn ʿAbbās, or from one of them, that he said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only stood because of the funeral procession of a Jew that was passed by him, and he said: 'Its smell harmed me.'”
items.ma-1734: Yazīd and ʿAbbād ibn ʿAbbād narrated to us, they said: Hishām ibn Abī Hishām informed us — ʿAbbād said: Ibn Ziyād — from his mother, from Fāṭimah daughter of al-Ḥusayn, from her father al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “There is no Muslim man or Muslim woman who is afflicted by a calamity and then remembers it, even if its time was long ago — ʿAbbād said: its time was old — and so renews on that account an istirjāʿ, except that Allah renews [it] for him at that time, and gives him the like of its reward on the day he was afflicted by it.”
items.ma-1735: Yazīd narrated to us, Sharīk ibn ʿAbd Allāh informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Burayd ibn Abī Maryam, from Abū al-Ḥawrāʾ, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī, he said: My grandfather taught me — or he said: the Prophet ﷺ — words that I say in the witr … and he mentioned the ḥadīth.
