items.ma-1736: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿAmr and Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, they said: Sulaymān ibn Bilāl narrated to us, from ʿUmārah ibn Ghaziyyah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAlī ibn Ḥusayn, from his father ʿAlī ibn Ḥusayn, from his father: that the Prophet ﷺ said: “The miserly one is he in whose presence I am mentioned and who then does not send blessings upon me.” Abū Saʿīd said: “and he did not send blessings upon me,” ﷺ abundantly.
items.ma-1737: Mūsā ibn Dāwūd narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥusayn, from his father ﵁, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Part of the excellence of a man's Islam is his leaving what does not concern him.”
items.ma-1738: al-Ḥakam ibn Nāfiʿ narrated to us, Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh narrated to us, from Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAqīl, he said: ʿAqīl ibn Abī Ṭālib married, and he came out to us, so we said: “With harmony and sons!” He said: “Stop! Do not say that, for the Prophet ﷺ forbade us from that, and he said: 'Say: May Allah bless you, and bless for you in her.'”
items.ma-1739: Ismāʿīl — and he is Ibn ʿUlayyah — narrated to us, Yūnus informed us, from al-Ḥasan: that ʿAqīl ibn Abī Ṭālib ﵁ married a woman from Banū Jusham, and the people entered upon him and said: “With harmony and sons!” He said: “Do not say that.” They said: “Then what shall we say, O Abū Yazīd?” He said: “Say: May Allah bless you, and bless upon you. Thus we used to be commanded.”
items.ma-1741: Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, he said: I saw the Prophet ﷺ eating cucumber with fresh dates.
items.ma-1742: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Ḥabīb ibn al-Shahīd informed us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Mulaykah, he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar said to Ibn al-Zubayr: “Do you remember when we met the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I and you and Ibn ʿAbbās?” He said: “Yes.” He said: “So he carried us and left you?” And Ismāʿīl said on one occasion: “Do you remember when we met the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I and you and Ibn ʿAbbās?” So he said: “Yes, he carried us and left you.”
items.ma-1743: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, ʿĀṣim narrated to us, from Muwarriq al-ʿIjlī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, he said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came back from a journey, he would be met with the boys of his household. He said: And once he came back from a journey, he said: I was sent ahead to him, he said: so he carried me in front of him. He said: Then one of the two sons of Fāṭimah was brought, either Ḥasan or Ḥusayn, and he seated him behind him. He said: So we entered al-Madīnah, three on one riding animal.
items.ma-1744: Yaḥyā narrated to us, Misʿar narrated to us, a shaykh from Fahm narrated to me — he said: and I think he was named Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, he said: and I think he was a Ḥijāzī — that he heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar narrating to Ibn al-Zubayr, when a camel for slaughter, or a camel, had been slaughtered for the people, that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while the people were serving the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the meat, saying: “The best of meat is the meat of the back.”
items.ma-1745: Yazīd narrated to us, Mahdī ibn Maymūn informed us, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Yaʿqūb, from al-Ḥasan ibn Saʿd, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar. And Bahz and ʿAffān narrated to us, they said: Mahdī narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Abī Yaʿqūb narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan ibn Saʿd, the mawlā of al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, he said: One day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ seated me behind him, and he confided to me a ḥadīth that I will not tell to anyone. And the most beloved thing the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would take cover behind for his need was a mound or a cluster of palm trees. One day he entered a garden of the gardens of the Anṣār, and there was a camel that came to him, groaned, and its eyes shed tears — Bahz and ʿAffān said: When it saw the Prophet ﷺ it yearned and its eyes shed tears — so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wiped its back and the area behind its ears, and it became calm. He said: “Who is the owner of the camel?” A young man of the Anṣār came and said: “It is mine, O Messenger of Allah.” He said: “Do you not fear Allah regarding this animal that Allah has given you to own? Indeed it complained to me that you starve it and overwork it.”
items.ma-1747: Rawḥ narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Musāfiʿ informed me that Muṣʿab ibn Shaybah informed him, from ʿUqbah ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥārith — and Ḥajjāj said: ʿUtbah ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥārith — from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Whoever doubts in his prayer, let him prostrate two prostrations while he is sitting.”
items.ma-1748: Isḥāq ibn ʿĪsā and Yaḥyā ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, they said: Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, from Abū al-Aswad, he said: I heard ʿUbayd Ibn Umm Kilāb narrating from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar — Yaḥyā ibn Isḥāq said: he said: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar. One of the two said: Dhū al-Janāḥayn — that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he sneezed, would praise Allah, and it would be said to him: “May Allah have mercy on you.” Then he would say: “May Allah guide you and set right your condition.”
items.ma-1749: Naṣr ibn Bāb narrated to us, from Ḥajjāj, from Qatādah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, that he said: Indeed, the last time I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in one of his hands were some fresh dates and in the other a cucumber, and he was eating from this one and biting from that one, and he said: “Indeed the best of the sheep is the meat of the back.”
items.ma-1750:
Wahb ibn Jarīr narrated to us, my father narrated to us, he said: I heard Muḥammad ibn Abī Yaʿqūb narrating from al-Ḥasan ibn Saʿd, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent an army and appointed Zayd ibn Ḥārithah over them, [saying]: “If Zayd is killed or martyred, then your commander is Jaʿfar, and if he is killed or martyred, then your commander is ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥah.” They met the enemy, and Zayd took the banner and fought until he was killed. Then Jaʿfar took the banner and fought until he was killed. Then ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥah took it and fought until he was killed. Then Khālid ibn al-Walīd took the banner, and Allah gave him the conquest. And news of them came to the Prophet ﷺ, so he went out to the people, praised Allah and extolled Him, and said: “Indeed your brothers met the enemy, and Zayd took the banner and fought until he was killed — or martyred. Then Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib took the banner after him and fought until he was killed — or martyred. Then ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥah took the banner and fought until he was killed — or martyred. Then a sword from among the swords of Allah, Khālid ibn al-Walīd, took the banner, and Allah gave him the conquest.” Then he gave time, then he gave the family of Jaʿfar time — three [days] — before he came to them. Then he came to them and said: “Do not weep for my brother after today. Call to me the two sons of my brother.” He said: So we were brought as though we were chicks. He said: “Call the barber to me.” So the barber was brought, and he shaved our heads. Then he said: “As for Muḥammad, he resembles our uncle Abū Ṭālib, and as for ʿAbd Allāh, he resembles my physical form and my character.” Then he took my hand and raised it, and said: “O Allah, succeed Jaʿfar among his family, and bless ʿAbd Allāh in the bargain of his right hand.” He said it three times.
He said: Then our mother came and mentioned our orphanhood to him, and she began to tufriḥ to him. He said: “Are you afraid of poverty for them, while I am their guardian in this world and the Hereafter?!”
items.ma-1751: Sufyān narrated to us, Jaʿfar ibn Khālid narrated to us, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, he said: When the news of Jaʿfar's death came, when he was killed, the Prophet ﷺ said: “Make food for the family of Jaʿfar, for a matter has come to them that occupies them — or: what occupies them has come to them.”
items.ma-1752: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Musāfiʿ informed me that Muṣʿab ibn Shaybah informed him, from ʿUtbah ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥārith, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever doubts in his prayer, let him prostrate two prostrations after he gives the salām.”
items.ma-1753: ʿAlī ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh informed us, Ibn Jurayj informed us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Musāfiʿ narrated to me, from ʿUqbah ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥārith … and he mentioned the like of it with its chain.
items.ma-1754: Wahb ibn Jarīr narrated to us, my father narrated to us, he said: I heard Muḥammad ibn Abī Yaʿqūb narrating from al-Ḥasan ibn Saʿd, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ rode his mule and seated me behind him. And when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to relieve himself, the most beloved thing he would relieve himself at was a mound that he could take cover behind, or a cluster of palm trees. He entered a garden belonging to a man of the Anṣār, and there was a water-drawing camel of his in it. When it saw the Prophet ﷺ, it yearned and its eyes shed tears. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ dismounted and wiped the area behind its ears and its back, and it became calm. He said: “Who is the owner of this camel?” A young man of the Anṣār came and said: “I am.” He said: “Do you not fear Allah regarding this animal that Allah has given you to own? Indeed it complained of you to me, and claimed that you starve it and overwork it.” Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went into the garden, relieved himself, then performed wuḍūʾ, then came, with the water dripping from his beard onto his chest, and he confided something to me that I will not tell to anyone. So we pressed him that he narrate it to us, and he said: “I will not divulge the secret of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until I meet Allah.”
items.ma-1755: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Rāfiʿ, the mawlā of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar used to wear his ring on his right [hand], and he claimed that the Prophet ﷺ used to wear his ring on his right [hand].
items.ma-1756: Hāshim ibn al-Qāsim narrated to us, al-Masʿūdī narrated to us, a shaykh who came to us from the Ḥijāz narrated to us, he said: I was present with ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar at al-Muzdalifah, and Ibn al-Zubayr was cutting the meat for ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “The best of meat is the meat of the back.”
items.ma-1757:
Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Malik narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Ḥakīm, from al-Qāsim, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “It is not fitting for a prophet to say: I am better than Yūnus ibn Mattā.”
Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: And Hārūn ibn Maʿrūf narrated it to us, the like of it.
items.ma-1758: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, he said: Hishām ibn ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to me, from his father ʿUrwah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I was commanded to give Khadījah the glad tidings of a house of reed, in which there is no clamour and no toil.”
items.ma-1759: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Misʿar narrated to us, from a shaykh from Fahm, he said: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar say: Meat was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the people began to serve him the meat. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed the best of meat is the meat of the back.”
items.ma-1760:
Rawḥ narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, Jaʿfar ibn Khālid ibn Sārah informed me that his father informed him that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar said: If you had seen me and Qutham and ʿUbayd Allāh, the two sons of ʿAbbās, while we were boys playing, when the Prophet ﷺ passed by on a riding animal and said: “Lift this one up to me.” He said: So he carried me in front of him. And he said to Qutham: “Lift this one up to me.” And he put him behind him. And ʿUbayd Allāh was more beloved to ʿAbbās than Qutham, yet he was not ashamed before his uncle that he carried Qutham and left him. He said: Then he wiped over my head three times, and each time he wiped he said: “O Allah, succeed Jaʿfar among his children.”
He said: I said to ʿAbd Allāh: “What became of Qutham?” He said: “He was martyred.” He said: I said: “Allah knows the good best, and His Messenger [knows] the good.” He said: “Yes indeed.”
items.ma-1761: Rawḥ narrated to us, he said: Ibn Jurayj said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Musāfiʿ informed me that Muṣʿab ibn Shaybah informed him, from ʿUqbah ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥārith, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever doubts in his prayer, let him prostrate two prostrations after he gives the salām.”
items.ma-1762: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Rāfiʿ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar: that he married his daughter to al-Ḥajjāj ibn Yūsuf, and said to her: “When he goes in to you, say: There is no deity except Allah, al-Ḥalīm, al-Karīm. Glory be to Allah, Rabb of the Mighty ʿArsh. All praise is for Allah, Rabb of the worlds.” And he claimed that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when a matter distressed him, would say this. Ḥammād said: I think he said: “and he did not reach her.”
items.ma-1763: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith, from al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, that he said: “O Messenger of Allah, your uncle Abū Ṭālib used to protect you and do [for you].” He said: “Indeed he is in a shallow of the Fire, and had it not been for me, he would have been in the lowest depth.”
items.ma-1764: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Muḥammad, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd, from al-ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When a man prostrates, seven limbs prostrate with him: his face, his palms, his knees, and his feet.”
items.ma-1765: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, from Yazīd ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Hād, from Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd, from al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, from the Prophet ﷺ, with the like of it.
items.ma-1766: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bakr narrated to us, Ḥātim — meaning Ibn Abī Ṣaghīrah — narrated to us, some of the Banū al-Muṭṭalib narrated to me, he said: ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās came to us during one of those seasons. He said: I heard him say: My father ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās narrated to me, from his father al-ʿAbbās, that he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: “O Messenger of Allah, I am your uncle. My age has advanced and my appointed term has drawn near. So teach me something by which Allah will benefit me.” He said: “O ʿAbbās, you are my uncle, and I cannot avail you anything against Allah. But ask your Rabb for pardon and well-being in this world and the Hereafter.” He said it three times. Then he came to him at the turn of the year and said the like of that to him.
items.ma-1767: Rawḥ narrated to us, Abū Yūnus al-Qushayrī Ḥātim ibn Abī Ṣaghīrah narrated to us, a man from the descendants of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib narrated to me, he said: ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās came to us, and the Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib were present with him. He said: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās narrating from his father ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, he said: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: “O Messenger of Allah, I am your uncle, my age has advanced …” and he mentioned its meaning.
items.ma-1768: ʿAffān narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Nawfal, from ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, he said: I said: “O Messenger of Allah, have you benefited Abū Ṭālib in anything? For he used to protect you and become angry for you.” He said: “Yes. He is in a shallow of the Fire, and had it not been for that, he would have been in the lowest depth of the Fire.”
items.ma-1769: Yaḥyā ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, Ibn Lahīʿah informed us, from Yazīd ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Hād, from Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd, from al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When the son of Ādam prostrates, seven limbs prostrate with him: his face, his palms, his knees, and his feet.”
items.ma-1770: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Yaḥyā ibn al-ʿAlāʾ informed us, from his paternal uncle Shuʿayb ibn Khālid, Simāk ibn Ḥarb narrated to me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmayrah, from ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, he said: We were sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at al-Baṭḥāʾ, and a cloud passed. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Do you know what this is?” He said: We said: “The clouds.” He said: “And the muzn.” We said: “And the muzn.” He said: “And the ʿanān.” He said: We were silent. He said: “Do you know how much there is between the heaven and the earth?” He said: We said: “Allah and His Messenger know best.” He said: “Between them is a journey of five hundred years, and from each heaven to the next heaven is a journey of five hundred years, and the thickness of each heaven is a journey of five hundred years. And above the seventh heaven is a sea, between its bottom and its top is like what is between the heaven and the earth. Then above that are eight mountain goats, between their knees and their hooves is like what is between the heaven and the earth. Then above that is the ʿArsh, between its bottom and its top is like what is between the heaven and the earth. And Allah, Tabāraka wa-Taʿālā, is Fawq that, and nothing of the deeds of the children of Ādam is hidden from Him.”
items.ma-1771: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us: Muḥammad ibn al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Bazzār and Muḥammad ibn Bakkār narrated to us, they said: al-Walīd ibn Abī Thawr narrated to us, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmayrah, from al-Aḥnaf ibn Qays, from al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, from the Prophet ﷺ, similar to it.
items.ma-1772: Yazīd — he is Ibn Hārūn — narrated to us, Ismāʿīl — meaning Ibn Abī Khālid — informed us, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith, from al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, he said: I said: “O Messenger of Allah, when some of Quraysh meet one another, they meet them with beautiful cheerfulness, and when they meet us, they meet us with faces that we do not recognise.” He said: So the Prophet ﷺ became very angry, and said: “By Him in Whose Yad is my soul, faith will not enter a man's heart until he loves you for the sake of Allah and His Messenger.”
items.ma-1773: Jarīr narrated it to us, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith, from ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib ibn Rabīʿah, he said: Al-ʿAbbās entered upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: “We go out and see Quraysh conversing …” and he mentioned the ḥadīth.
items.ma-1774: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from Sufyān, ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr narrated to me, ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith narrated to us, al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, he said: I said to the Prophet ﷺ: “What have you availed your uncle? For he used to protect you and become angry for you.” He said: “He is in a shallow, and had it not been for me, he would have been in the lowest depth of the Fire.”
items.ma-1775: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, Kathīr ibn ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib informed me, from his father al-ʿAbbās, he said: I was present with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Ḥunayn. He said: I saw the Prophet ﷺ, and there was no one with him except me and Abū Sufyān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib. We kept close to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and did not leave him, while he was on a grey mule — and perhaps Maʿmar said: a white one — that Farwah ibn Nuʿāmah al-Judhāmī had gifted to him. When the Muslims and the disbelievers met, the Muslims turned back, retreating, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began to spur his mule toward the disbelievers. Al-ʿAbbās said: And I was holding the bridle of the mule of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, restraining it, while he did not fall short in hastening toward the polytheists, and Abū Sufyān ibn al-Ḥārith was holding the stirrup of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “O ʿAbbās, call: O Companions of the acacia tree!” He said: And I was a loud-voiced man, so I said at the top of my voice: “Where are the Companions of the acacia tree?” He said: By Allah, their turning back when they heard my voice was like the turning back of cows to their young, and they said: “At your service! At your service! At your service!” And the Muslims advanced, and they and the disbelievers fought one another. The Anṣār called out, saying: “O company of the Anṣār!” Then the callers limited it to the Banū al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj, and they called: “O Banū al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj!” He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked, while he was on his mule, like one stretching up on it toward their fighting, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “This is when the waṭīs has become hot.” He said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took some pebbles and threw them at the faces of the disbelievers, then said: “They are routed, by the Rabb of the Kaʿbah! They are routed, by the Rabb of the Kaʿbah!” He said: I went to look, and the fighting was in its same state as far as I could see. He said: By Allah, it was no more than that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ threw his pebbles at them, and I kept seeing their sharpness blunted and their affair receding, until Allah routed them. He said: And it is as though I am looking at the Prophet ﷺ spurring his mule behind them.
items.ma-1776: Sufyān narrated to us, he said: I heard al-Zuhrī once or twice, and I did not memorise it, from Kathīr ibn ʿAbbās, he said: ʿAbbās was, and Abū Sufyān with him — meaning the Prophet ﷺ. He said: So he addressed them and said: “Now the waṭīs has become hot.” And he said: “Call: O Companions of Sūrat al-Baqarah.”
items.ma-1777: Jarīr ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd Abū ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith, from ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib ibn Rabīʿah, he said: Al-ʿAbbās entered upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: “O Messenger of Allah, we go out and see Quraysh conversing, and when they see us they fall silent.” So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ became angry, and a vein between his eyes swelled. Then he said: “By Allah, faith will not enter the heart of a man until he loves you for the sake of Allah and for my kinship.”
items.ma-1778: Muḥammad ibn Idrīs — meaning al-Shāfiʿī — narrated to us, ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, from Yazīd — meaning Ibn al-Hād — from Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd, from ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “He has tasted the taste of faith who is pleased with Allah as Rabb, with Islam as religion, and with Muḥammad as Messenger.”
items.ma-1779: Qutaybah ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, Layth ibn Saʿd narrated to us, from Ibn al-Hād, from Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm ibn al-Ḥārith, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd, from al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “He has tasted the taste of faith who is pleased with Allah as Rabb, with Islam as religion, and with Muḥammad as Prophet.”
items.ma-1780: Qutaybah ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, Bakr ibn Muḍar al-Qurashī narrated to us, from Ibn al-Hād, from Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm ibn al-Ḥārith, from ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd, from al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “When the servant prostrates, seven limbs prostrate with him: his face, his palms, his knees, and his feet.”
items.ma-1781:
Abū al-Yamān narrated to us, Shuʿayb informed us, from al-Zuhrī, Mālik ibn Aws ibn al-Ḥadathān al-Naṣrī informed me that ʿUmar summoned him … and he mentioned the ḥadīth. He said: While I was with him, his doorkeeper Yarfaʾ came and said: “Do you want [to receive] ʿUthmān, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, al-Zubayr and Saʿd, who are asking permission?” He said: “Yes.” So he admitted them. He stayed a little while, then came to him and said: “Do you want [to receive] ʿAlī and ʿAbbās, who are asking permission?” He said: “Yes.” So he gave permission to the two, and when the two entered, ʿAbbās said: “O Commander of the Believers, judge between me and this one; [he said it] regarding ʿAlī” — and the two were disputing over the select properties that Allah gave as fayʾ to His Messenger from the properties of Banū al-Naḍīr. The group said: “O Commander of the Believers, judge between the two and relieve one of them of the other.” ʿUmar said: “Take it easy! I adjure you by Allah, by Whose permission the heaven and the earth stand, do you know that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'We are not inherited from; what we leave is ṣadaqah' — meaning himself?” They said: “He did say that.” Then ʿUmar turned to ʿAlī and ʿAbbās and said: “I adjure you two by Allah, do you know that the Prophet ﷺ said that?” They said: “Yes.”
He said: “Then I will tell you about this matter. Allah ﷿ had singled out His Messenger in this fayʾ with something He gave to no one other than him, for He said: {And what Allah gave as fayʾ to His Messenger from them, so you did not spur} to {Qadīr} [al-Ḥashr: 6]. So this was exclusively for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then, by Allah, he did not seize it to the exclusion of you, nor did he reserve it for himself over you; he gave it to you and distributed it among you, until this property remained of it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would spend on his family their expenses for the year from this property, then take what remained and put it in the place of the property of Allah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ acted thus throughout his life. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died, and Abū Bakr said: 'I am the walī of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ,' and Abū Bakr took possession of it and acted regarding it as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had acted.”
items.ma-1782:
Yaʿqūb narrated to us, the son of the brother of Ibn Shihāb narrated to us, from his paternal uncle Muḥammad ibn Muslim, he said: Mālik ibn Aws ibn al-Ḥadathān al-Naṣrī informed me … and he mentioned the ḥadīth. He said: While I was sitting with him, his doorkeeper Yarfaʾ came to him and said to ʿUmar: “Do you want [to receive] ʿUthmān, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, Saʿd and al-Zubayr, who are asking permission?” He said: “Yes, give them permission.” He said: So they entered, greeted, and sat. He said: Then Yarfaʾ stayed a little while and said to ʿUmar: “Do you want [to receive] ʿAlī and ʿAbbās?” He said: “Yes.” So he gave permission to the two, and when the two entered upon him, they sat. ʿAbbās said: “O Commander of the Believers, judge between me and ʿAlī.” The group, ʿUthmān and his companions, said: “Judge between the two, and relieve one of them of the other.” ʿUmar said: “Take it easy! I adjure you by Allah, by Whose permission the heaven and the earth stand, do you know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'We are not inherited from; what we leave is ṣadaqah' — the Messenger of Allah ﷺ meaning himself by that?” The group said: “He did say that.” Then ʿUmar turned to ʿAlī and ʿAbbās and said: “I adjure you two by Allah, do you know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did say that?” The two said: “He did say that.”
Then ʿUmar said: “Then I will tell you about this matter. Allah ﷿ had singled out His Messenger in this fayʾ with something He gave to no one other than him, for Allah said: {And what Allah gave as fayʾ to His Messenger from them, so you did not spur} — the verse. So this verse was exclusively for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then, by Allah, he did not seize it, nor did he reserve it for himself over you; he gave it to you and distributed it among you, until this property remained of it. And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would spend on his family their expenses for the year from this property, then take what remained of it and put it in the place of the property of Allah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ acted thus throughout his life. I adjure you by Allah, do you know that?” They said: “Yes.” He said to ʿAlī and ʿAbbās: “I adjure you two by Allah, do you know that?” The two said: “Yes.” “Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died, and Abū Bakr said: 'I am the walī of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.' So Abū Bakr ﵁ took possession of it and acted regarding it as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had acted regarding it. And you at that time” — and he turned to ʿAlī and ʿAbbās — “claim that Abū Bakr [was] such-and-such in it, while Allah knows that he was truthful in it, righteous, rightly guided, following the truth.”
items.ma-1783: Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, from Zāʾidah, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith, from al-ʿAbbās, he said: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: “O Messenger of Allah, teach me something with which I may supplicate.” He said: “Ask Allah for pardon and well-being.” He said: Then I came to him another time and said: “O Messenger of Allah, teach me something with which I may supplicate.” He said: So he said: “O ʿAbbās, O uncle of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, ask Allah for well-being in this world and the Hereafter.”
items.ma-1784: Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī al-Safar narrated to me, from Ibn Shuraḥbīl, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from al-ʿAbbās, he said: I entered upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while his wives were with him, and they screened themselves from me, except Maymūnah. He said: “No one who witnessed the ladd shall remain in the house except that the ladd is administered to him, except that my right hand did not reach al-ʿAbbās.” Then he said: “Command Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” ʿĀʾishah said to Ḥafṣah: “Say to him: Indeed Abū Bakr is a man who, when he stands in your place, weeps.” He said: “Command Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” So he stood and prayed, and the Prophet ﷺ found some lightness, and he came. Abū Bakr ﵁ drew back, and wished to move back, but he sat beside him, then he recited.
items.ma-1785: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Qays narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī al-Safar narrated to us, from Arqam ibn Shuraḥbīl, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said during his illness: “Command Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” So Abū Bakr went out and said the takbīr, and the Prophet ﷺ found some relief, and he went out, supported between two men. When Abū Bakr saw him, he drew back, and the Prophet ﷺ gestured to him: “[Stay in] your place.” Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat beside Abū Bakr, and he recited from the place in the sūrah that Abū Bakr ﵁ had reached.
items.ma-1786: ʿUbayd ibn Abī Qurrah narrated to us, Layth ibn Saʿd narrated to us, from Abū Qabīl, from Abū Maysarah, from al-ʿAbbās, he said: I was with the Prophet ﷺ one night, and he said: “Look, do you see any star in the heaven?” He said: I said: “Yes.” He said: “What do you see?” He said: I said: “I see the Pleiades.” He said: “Indeed, this ummah will be governed, by the number of them, from your loins, two of them in a fitnah.”
items.ma-1787: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, Yaḥyā ibn al-Ashʿath narrated to me, from Ismāʿīl ibn Iyās ibn ʿAfīf al-Kindī, from his father, from his grandfather, he said: I was a man who was a merchant, and I came for the Ḥajj, and I went to al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib to buy some merchandise from him, and he was a man who was a merchant. By Allah, I was with him at Minā when a man came out of a tent near him, and looked at the sun, and when he saw it had declined — meaning he stood to pray. He said: Then a woman came out of that tent from which the man had come out, and stood behind him praying. Then a boy came out of that tent, when he was nearing puberty, and stood with him praying. He said: I said to al-ʿAbbās: “Who is this, O ʿAbbās?” He said: “This is Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, the son of my brother.” He said: I said: “Who is this woman?” He said: “This is his wife Khadījah daughter of Khuwaylid.” He said: I said: “Who is this youth?” He said: “This is ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, the son of his paternal uncle.” He said: I said: “And what is this that he is doing?” He said: “He is praying. And he claims that he is a prophet, and none has followed him in his affair except his wife and the son of his paternal uncle, this youth. And he claims that the treasures of Kisrā and Qayṣar will be opened to him.” He said: ʿAfīf — and he is the son of the paternal uncle of al-Ashʿath ibn Qays — used to say — and he accepted Islam after that and his Islam became good —: “Would that Allah had granted me Islam on that day, so that I would be the third with ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib ﵁.”
items.ma-1788: Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Nawfal, from al-Muṭṭalib ibn Abī Wadāʿah, he said: Al-ʿAbbās said: Some of what the people were saying reached him ﷺ. He said: So he ascended the minbar and said: “Who am I?” They said: “You are the Messenger of Allah.” He said: “I am Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib. Indeed Allah created the creation and placed me in the best of His creation, and made them two groups and placed me in the best group, and created the tribes and placed me in the best tribe, and made them houses and placed me in the best of them as a house. So I am the best of you as a house, and the best of you as a self.”
items.ma-1789: ʿAffān narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Nawfal, from ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, he said: “O Messenger of Allah, have you benefited Abū Ṭālib in anything? For he used to protect you and become angry for you.” He said: “Yes. He is in a shallow of the Fire; were it not for that, he would be in the lowest depth of the Fire.”
items.ma-1790: Asbāṭ ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, Hishām ibn Saʿd narrated to us, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, the brother of ʿAbd Allāh, he said: Al-ʿAbbās had a spout over the path of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. ʿUmar put on his clothes on the day of Jumuʿah, and two chicks had been slaughtered for al-ʿAbbās. When he came level with the spout, water mixed with the blood of the two chicks was poured, and it struck ʿUmar, and in it was the blood of the two chicks. So ʿUmar ordered that it be pulled out. Then ʿUmar returned, cast off his clothes, put on clothes other than his clothes, then came and led the people in prayer. Al-ʿAbbās came to him and said: “By Allah, it is the place where the Prophet ﷺ placed it.” ʿUmar said to al-ʿAbbās: “And I adjure you resolutely to climb onto my back, until you place it in the place where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ placed it.” So al-ʿAbbās ﵁ did that.
items.ma-1791: ʿAbbād ibn ʿAbbād narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās: that he was riding behind the Prophet ﷺ from Jamʿ, and he did not cease making the talbiyah until he cast [pebbles at] the Jamrah.
items.ma-1792: It was read to Sufyān: I heard Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥarmalah, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from al-Faḍl: that the Prophet ﷺ made the talbiyah until he cast [pebbles at] the Jamrah.
items.ma-1793: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, ʿAṭāʾ informed me, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ seated al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās behind him from Jamʿ. ʿAṭāʾ said: Ibn ʿAbbās informed me that al-Faḍl informed him that the Prophet ﷺ did not cease making the talbiyah until he cast [pebbles at] the Jamrah.
items.ma-1794:
Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, Abū al-Zubayr informed me, Abū Maʿbad informed me, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās reporting from al-Faḍl, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, on the evening of ʿArafah, the morning of Jamʿ, to the people when we set off: “[Keep to] tranquillity!” while he was restraining his she-camel, until, when he entered Minā, when he descended into Muḥassir, he said: “[Take] the pebbles of khadhf with which the Jamrah is pelted.” And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was pointing with his hand as a person flicks.
Rawḥ and al-Bursānī said: “on the evening of ʿArafah, and the morning of Jamʿ,” and the two said: “when they set off.”
items.ma-1795: Yūnus ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood in the Kaʿbah, glorified Allah, said the takbīr, supplicated Allah ﷿ and sought forgiveness, and did not bow and did not prostrate.
items.ma-1796: Ḥujayn and Yūnus narrated to us, they said: Layth ibn Saʿd narrated to us, from Abū al-Zubayr, from Abū Maʿbad, the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, from al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās — and he was riding behind the Prophet ﷺ —: that he said on the evening of ʿArafah and the morning of Jamʿ, to the people when they set off: “[Keep to] tranquillity!” while he was restraining his she-camel, until, when he entered Muḥassir — and it is part of Minā — he said: “[Take] the pebbles of khadhf with which the Jamrah is pelted.” And he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not cease making the talbiyah until he cast [pebbles at] the Jamrah.
items.ma-1797: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, he said: Ibn Jurayj said: Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar ibn ʿAlī informed me, from ʿAbbās ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, from al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ visited ʿAbbās in a desert place of ours, and we had a little bitch and a she-donkey grazing. The Prophet ﷺ prayed the ʿAṣr prayer, and the two were in front of him, and they were not moved back and not driven off.
items.ma-1798: ʿAffān narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Khuthaym narrated to us, from Abū al-Ṭufayl, from al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās: that he was riding behind the Prophet ﷺ from Jamʿ to Minā, and he did not cease making the talbiyah until he cast [pebbles at] the Jamrah.
items.ma-1799: ʿAlī ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mubārak informed us, Layth ibn Saʿd informed us, ʿAbd Rabbihi ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from ʿImrān ibn Abī Anas, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Nāfiʿ Ibn al-ʿAmyāʾ, from Rabīʿah ibn al-Ḥārith, from al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The prayer is two by two. You recite the tashahhud at every two rakʿahs, and you show humility, and show reverence, and show lowliness, then you tuqniʿ your hands — he said: you raise them to your Rabb — facing your face with their insides, saying: O Rabb, O Rabb. And whoever does not do that —“ and he said a severe word about it.
items.ma-1800: Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥakīm al-ʿAdanī narrated to us, al-Ḥakam — meaning Ibn Abān — narrated to me, I heard ʿIkrimah say: Al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set off, and I was with him, and we reached the mountain pass, he dismounted and performed wuḍūʾ, then we rode until we came to al-Muzdalifah.
items.ma-1801: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated to me, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ, and from Mujāhid ibn Jabr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās: My brother al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās narrated to me, and he was with him when he entered it: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not pray in the Kaʿbah, but when he entered it he fell prostrating between the two pillars, then sat supplicating.
items.ma-1802:
Hushaym narrated to us, Ibn Abī Laylā informed us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās informed me: that he was riding behind the Prophet ﷺ when he set off from Jamʿ. He said: So he set off with tranquillity upon him. He said: And he made the talbiyah until he cast [pebbles at] the Jamrah of al-ʿAqabah.
And he said on one occasion: Ibn Abī Laylā informed us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās informed us, he said: I witnessed the two ifāḍahs with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he set off with tranquillity upon him while restraining his camel. He said: And he made the talbiyah until he cast [pebbles at] the Jamrah of al-ʿAqabah.
items.ma-1803: ʿAbdah ibn Sulaymān narrated to us, Ibn Abī Laylā narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās — and he was riding behind the Prophet ﷺ when he set off from ʿArafah — he said: He saw the people hurrying, so he ordered his caller, who called out: “Righteousness is not in the hurrying of horses and camels, so [keep to] tranquillity.”
items.ma-1804: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, the son of the brother of Ibn Shihāb narrated to us, from his paternal uncle, he said: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām informed me, he said: ʿĀʾishah and Umm Salamah, the two wives of the Prophet ﷺ, said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to wake up in the morning from his family in a state of janābah, then he would bathe before praying the Fajr prayer, then he would fast that day.” He said: I mentioned that to Abū Hurayrah, and he said: “I do not know; al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās ﵁ informed me of that.”
items.ma-1805: Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, Jarīr narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtaybah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from his brother al-Faḍl, he said: I was riding behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from Jamʿ to Minā, and while he was travelling, a Bedouin presented himself to him, with a beautiful daughter of his riding behind him, and he was travelling alongside him. He said: I was looking at her, and the Prophet ﷺ looked at me and turned my face away from her face. Then I looked again, and he turned my face away from her face, until he did that three times, and I did not stop. And he did not cease making the talbiyah until he cast [pebbles at] the Jamrah of al-ʿAqabah.
items.ma-1806: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, Qays informed us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made the talbiyah on the Day of Sacrifice until he cast [pebbles at] the Jamrah of al-ʿAqabah.
items.ma-1807: Rawḥ narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿĀmir al-Aḥwal, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from al-Faḍl: that he was riding behind the Prophet ﷺ, and he used to make the talbiyah until he cast [pebbles at] the Jamrah.
items.ma-1808: Rawḥ narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, ʿAlī ibn Zayd narrated to us, he said: I heard Yūsuf ibn Māhak, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I was riding behind the Prophet ﷺ, and he made the talbiyah in the Ḥajj until he cast [pebbles at] the Jamrah on the Day of Sacrifice.
items.ma-1809: Hāshim ibn al-Qāsim narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿĀmir al-Aḥwal and Jābir al-Juʿfī and Ibn ʿAṭāʾ, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās: that he was riding behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he made the talbiyah until he cast [pebbles at] the Jamrah on the Day of Sacrifice.
items.ma-1810: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Jābir and ʿĀmir al-Aḥwal and Ibn ʿAṭāʾ, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās was riding behind the Prophet ﷺ, and he used to make the talbiyah on the Day of Sacrifice until he cast [pebbles at] the Jamrah.
items.ma-1811: ʿAffān narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, Mushāsh informed me, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded the weak ones of Banū Hāshim — he commanded them to hasten from Jamʿ by night.
items.ma-1812: Hushaym narrated to us, Yaḥyā ibn Abī Isḥāq narrated to us, from Sulaymān ibn Yasār, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, or from al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās: that a man asked the Prophet ﷺ and said: “O Messenger of Allah, Islam reached my father while he is a very old man who cannot stay firm on his mount. Shall I perform Ḥajj on his behalf?” He said: “Do you see, if a debt were upon him and you paid it on his behalf, would it suffice him?” He said: “Yes.” He said: “Then perform Ḥajj on behalf of your father.”
items.ma-1813: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Isḥāq, he said: I heard Sulaymān ibn Yasār: Al-Faḍl narrated to us, he said: I was riding behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and a man asked him and said: “Indeed my father, or my mother, is a very old person who cannot perform Ḥajj …” and he mentioned the ḥadīth.
items.ma-1814: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to me, from al-Aḥwal and Jābir al-Juʿfī and Ibn ʿAṭāʾ, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from al-Faḍl: that he was riding behind the Prophet ﷺ, and he made the talbiyah until he cast [pebbles at] the Jamrah on the Day of Sacrifice.
items.ma-1815: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad narrated to us — ʿAbd Allāh said: and I heard it myself from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad — Ḥafṣ narrated to us, from Jaʿfar, from his father, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥusayn, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ did not cease making the talbiyah until he cast [pebbles at] the Jamrah of al-ʿAqabah, and he cast seven pebbles at it, saying the takbīr with each pebble.
items.ma-1816: Yaʿlā and Muḥammad, the two sons of ʿUbayd, narrated to us, they said: ʿAbd al-Malik narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, from al-Faḍl, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set off from ʿArafāt, with Usāmah ibn Zayd riding behind him. The she-camel swerved with him while he was standing at ʿArafāt before he set off, and he was raising his hands, they not going past his head. When he set off, he proceeded at his easy pace until he came to Jamʿ. Then he set off from Jamʿ with al-Faḍl riding behind him. Al-Faḍl said: The Prophet ﷺ did not cease making the talbiyah until he cast [pebbles at] the Jamrah.
items.ma-1817: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj informed us, Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar ibn ʿAlī narrated to me, from al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ visited ʿAbbās while we were in a desert place of ours, and he stood to pray — he said: I think he said: the ʿAṣr prayer — and in front of him was a little bitch of ours and a donkey grazing, with nothing between him and the two that came between him and them.
items.ma-1818: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from Sulaymān ibn Yasār, from Ibn ʿAbbās: Al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās narrated to me, he said: A woman from Khathʿam came and said: “O Messenger of Allah, the obligation of Allah ﷿ in the Ḥajj has reached my father, and he is a very old man who cannot stay firm on his mount.” He said: “Then perform Ḥajj on behalf of your father.”
items.ma-1819: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn Dīnār informed me that Ibn ʿAbbās used to report that al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās informed him: that he entered the House with the Prophet ﷺ, and that the Prophet ﷺ did not pray in the House when he entered it, but when he went out and dismounted, he prayed two rakʿahs at the door of the House.
items.ma-1820: Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā — meaning Ibn Abī Zāʾidah — narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Malik narrated to me, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ seated Usāmah ibn Zayd behind him from ʿArafah until he came to Jamʿ, and seated al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās behind him from Jamʿ until he came to Minā. Ibn ʿAbbās said: And al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās informed me: that the Prophet ﷺ did not cease making the talbiyah until he cast [pebbles at] the Jamrah.
items.ma-1821: Rawḥ narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us. And Ibn Bakr said: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, Abū al-Zubayr informed me that Abū Maʿbad, the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās, informed him, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, from al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: that he said on the evening of ʿArafah and the morning of Jamʿ, to the people when they set off: “[Keep to] tranquillity!” while he was restraining his she-camel, until, when he entered Minā, when he descended into Muḥassir, he said: “[Take] the pebbles of khadhf with which the Jamrah is pelted.” And the Prophet ﷺ was pointing with his hand as a person flicks.
items.ma-1822: Rawḥ narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, Ibn Shihāb said: Sulaymān ibn Yasār narrated to me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, from al-Faḍl: that a woman from Khathʿam said: “O Messenger of Allah, the obligation of Allah in the Ḥajj has reached my father, and he is a very old man who cannot sit upright on the back of his camel.” He said: “Then perform Ḥajj on his behalf.”
items.ma-1823: Ḥujayn ibn al-Muthannā and Abū Aḥmad — meaning al-Zubayrī — in meaning, they said: Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās — Abū Aḥmad said: Al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās narrated to me — he said: I was riding behind the Prophet ﷺ when he set off from al-Muzdalifah, and a Bedouin was travelling alongside him, with a beautiful daughter of his riding behind him. Al-Faḍl said: I began to look at her, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took hold of my face, turning me away from her. And he did not cease making the talbiyah until he cast [pebbles at] the Jamrah of al-ʿAqabah.
items.ma-1824: Ḥammād ibn Khālid narrated to us, he said: Ibn ʿUlāthah narrated to us, from Maslamah al-Juhanī, he said: I heard him narrating, from al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one day, and a gazelle sprang up and leaned to its side, so I embraced it, and I said: “O Messenger of Allah, did you take an ill omen?” He said: “Ill omen is only that which sends you on or turns you back.”
items.ma-1825: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ made the talbiyah until he cast [pebbles at] the Jamrah of al-ʿAqabah.
items.ma-1826: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Ibn ʿAwn informed us, from Rajāʾ ibn Ḥaywah, he said: Yaʿlā ibn ʿUqbah built in Ramaḍān, and woke up in the morning in a state of janābah. He met Abū Hurayrah and asked him, and he said: “Break your fast.” He said: “Should I not fast this day and have it suffice in place of another day?” He said: “Break your fast.” So he went to Marwān and told him, and he sent Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith to the Mother of the Believers and he asked her, and she said: “He used to wake up in the morning among us in a state of janābah, without a dream, then be fasting in the morning.” So he returned to Marwān and told him, and he said: “Meet Abū Hurayrah with it.” He said: “My neighbour, my neighbour.” He said: “I adjure you to meet him with it.” He said: So he met him and told him, and he said: “I did not hear it from the Prophet ﷺ; al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās only informed me of it.” He said: Afterward I met Rajāʾ and said: “The ḥadīth of Yaʿlā — who narrated it to you?” He said: “To me he narrated it.”
items.ma-1827:
Muḥammad — he is Ibn Jaʿfar — and Rawḥ narrated to us, they said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from Yūsuf, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from al-Faḍl: that he was riding behind the Prophet ﷺ on the Day of Sacrifice, and he used to make the talbiyah until he cast [pebbles at] the Jamrah. Rawḥ said: in the Ḥajj.
Rawḥ — meaning in his ḥadīth — said: ʿAlī ibn Zayd narrated to us, he said: I heard Yūsuf ibn Māhak. Both of them said: Ibn Māhak.
items.ma-1828: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Saʿīd narrated to us, Kathīr ibn Shinẓīr narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, from al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās: that he was riding behind the Prophet ﷺ on the Day of Sacrifice, and a girl was behind her father, so I began to look at her, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began to turn my face away from her. And from Jamʿ to Minā the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not cease making the talbiyah until he cast [pebbles at] the Jamrah on the Day of Sacrifice.
items.ma-1829:
Bahz narrated to us, Hammām narrated to us, Qatādah narrated to us, ʿAzrah narrated to me, from al-Shaʿbī, that al-Faḍl narrated to him: that he was riding behind the Prophet ﷺ from ʿArafah, and his mount did not raise its leg galloping until he reached Jamʿ.
He said: And al-Shaʿbī narrated to me that Usāmah narrated to him: that he was riding behind the Prophet ﷺ from Jamʿ, and his mount did not raise its leg galloping until he cast [pebbles at] the Jamrah.
items.ma-1830: Abū Kāmil narrated to us, Ḥammād — meaning Ibn Salamah — narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ stood in the Kaʿbah, glorified Allah and said the takbīr, and supplicated Allah and sought His forgiveness, and did not bow and did not prostrate.
items.ma-1831: Marwān ibn Shujāʿ narrated to us, from Khuṣayf, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ seated Usāmah behind him from ʿArafāt to Jamʿ, and seated al-Faḍl behind him from Jamʿ to Minā, and he informed him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not cease making the talbiyah until he cast [pebbles at] the Jamrah.
items.ma-1832: Kathīr ibn Hishām informed us, he said: Furāt narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Karīm narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās: that he was riding behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he did not cease making the talbiyah until he cast [pebbles at] the Jamrah of al-ʿAqabah.
items.ma-1833: Abū Aḥmad al-Zubayrī Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Fuḍayl ibn ʿAmr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, or from al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās, or from one of them from his companion, he said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever wants to perform Ḥajj, let him hasten, for a stray animal may go astray, a sick person may fall ill, and a need may arise.”
items.ma-1834: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Abū Isrāʾīl al-ʿAbsī narrated to us, from Fuḍayl ibn ʿAmr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from al-Faḍl, or one of them from the other, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever wants the Ḥajj, let him hasten, for a sick person may fall ill, a stray animal may go astray, and a need may present itself.”
items.ma-1835: Ismāʿīl ibn ʿUmar Abū al-Mundhir narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū ʿAlī al-Zarrād, he said: Jaʿfar ibn Tammām ibn ʿAbbās narrated to me, from his father, he said: They came to the Prophet ﷺ — or he was come to — and he said: “What is the matter that I see you coming to me with yellow teeth? Use the siwāk! Were it not that I would burden my ummah, I would have made the siwāk obligatory upon them as I made wuḍūʾ obligatory upon them.”
items.ma-1836: Jarīr narrated to us, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to line up ʿAbd Allāh, ʿUbayd Allāh and Kuthayyir, the sons of al-ʿAbbās, then say: “Whoever reaches me first, he will have such and such.” He said: So they would race to him and fall upon his back and chest, and he would kiss them and embrace them.
items.ma-1837:
Hushaym narrated to us, Yaḥyā ibn Abī Isḥāq informed us, from Sulaymān ibn Yasār, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn al-ʿAbbās, he said: Al-Ghumayṣāʾ — or al-Rumayṣāʾ — came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ complaining about her husband, and claiming that he could not reach her, and it was nothing but little. Then her husband came and claimed that she was lying, but that she wanted to return to her first husband. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “That is not for you until a man other than him tastes your little honey.”
Abū ʿAlī al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Mudhhib the preacher informed us, he said: Abū Bakr Aḥmad ibn Jaʿfar ibn Ḥamdān ibn Mālik informed us, by reading to him: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Ḥanbal narrated to us: My father narrated to me from his book:
items.ma-1838: Hushaym narrated to us, ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal and Mughīrah informed us, from al-Shaʿbī, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ drank from Zamzam while standing.
items.ma-1839: Hushaym narrated to us, Ajlaḥ informed us, from Yazīd ibn al-Aṣamm, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a man said to the Prophet ﷺ: “What Allah wills and you will.” The Prophet ﷺ said to him: “Have you made me an equal with Allah? Rather, what Allah alone wills.”
items.ma-1840: Hushaym narrated to us, from Khālid, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: The Prophet ﷺ wiped my head and supplicated for me for wisdom.
items.ma-1841: Hushaym narrated to us, Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ circumambulated the House while on his camel, and touched the Stone with a hooked staff that he had. He said: And he came to al-Siqāyah and said: “Give me to drink.” They said: “Indeed the people dip into this, but we will bring you [some] from the house.” He said: “I have no need of it. Give me to drink from what the people drink from.”
items.ma-1842: Hushaym narrated to us, from Abū Bishr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The report is not like witnessing.”
items.ma-1843: Hushaym narrated to us, Abū Bishr informed us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I spent a night at the home of my maternal aunt Maymūnah bint al-Ḥārith, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was with her on her night. He stood to pray during the night, and I stood on his left to pray his prayer. He said: So he took hold of a forelock I had, or of my head, until he placed me on his right.
items.ma-1844: Hushaym narrated to us, Khālid informed us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: When Barīrah was given the choice, I saw her husband following her in the lanes of al-Madīnah, with his tears running down his beard. Al-ʿAbbās was spoken to, so that he would speak to the Prophet ﷺ about him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Barīrah: “He is your husband.” She said: “Are you commanding me [to take] him, O Messenger of Allah?” He said: “I am only an intercessor.” He said: So he gave her the choice, and she chose herself. And he was a slave of the family of al-Mughīrah, called Mughīth.
items.ma-1845: Hushaym narrated to us, from Abū Bishr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ was asked about the offspring of the polytheists, and he said: “Allah knows best what they would have been doing.”
items.ma-1846: Hushaym narrated to us, ʿAlī ibn Zayd informed us, from Yūsuf ibn Mihrān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ was taken at the age of sixty-five.
items.ma-1847: Hushaym narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn Dīnār informed us, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The food that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade to be sold until it is taken possession of. Ibn ʿAbbās said: And I consider everything [to be] like it.
items.ma-1848: Hushaym narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn Dīnār informed us, from Jābir ibn Zayd, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ delivered a sermon and said: “When the muḥrim does not find an izār, let him wear trousers, and when he does not find sandals, let him wear the khuffayn.”
items.ma-1849: Hushaym narrated to us, he said: Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād informed us, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had cupping done while he was in iḥrām and fasting.
items.ma-1850: Hushaym narrated to us, Abū Bishr informed us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a man was with the Prophet ﷺ, and his she-camel broke his neck while he was in iḥrām, and he died. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Wash him with water and lote, shroud him in his two garments, do not touch him with perfume, and do not cover his head, for he will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection making the talbiyah.”
items.ma-1851: Hushaym narrated to us, ʿAwf informed us, from Ziyād ibn Ḥuṣayn, from Abū al-ʿĀliyah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me on the morning of Jamʿ: “Come, pick up [pebbles] for me.” So I picked up some pebbles for him, and they were pebbles of khadhf. When he placed them in his hand, he said: “Yes, with the like of these. And beware of exaggeration in the religion, for those before you were destroyed only by exaggeration in the religion.”
items.ma-1852: Hushaym narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Ibn Sīrīn, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ travelled from al-Madīnah fearing none but Allah ﷿, and prayed two rakʿahs, two rakʿahs, until he returned.
items.ma-1853: Hushaym narrated to us, Abū Bishr informed us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: This verse was revealed while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in hiding in Makkah: {And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent in it}. He said: And when the Prophet ﷺ prayed with his Companions, he would raise his voice with the Qurʾān, and when the polytheists heard that, they reviled the Qurʾān, and reviled the one who sent it down and the one who brought it. He said: So Allah ﷿ said to His Prophet: {And do not be loud in your prayer} — that is: in your recitation — so that the polytheists hear and revile the Qurʾān; {nor be silent in it} — from your Companions, so that you do not let them hear the Qurʾān until they take it from you; {and seek between that a way} [al-Isrāʾ: 110].
items.ma-1854: Hushaym narrated to us, Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind informed us, from Abū al-ʿĀliyah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by the valley of al-Azraq and said: “Which valley is this?” They said: “This is the valley of al-Azraq.” He said: “It is as though I see Mūsā ﵇ descending from the mountain pass, with a loud cry to Allah ﷿ in the talbiyah.” Until he came to the mountain pass of Harshā, and said: “Which mountain pass is this?” They said: “The mountain pass of Harshā.” He said: “It is as though I see Yūnus ibn Mattā on a red, curly-haired she-camel, wearing a woollen jubbah, the halter-rope of his she-camel being khulbah — Hushaym said: meaning palm fibre — and he is making the talbiyah.”
items.ma-1855: Hushaym narrated to us, our companions informed us, among them Shuʿbah, from Qatādah, from Abū Ḥassān, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ marked his sacrificial camel on the right side, then wiped the blood off it, and garlanded it with two sandals.
items.ma-1856: Hushaym narrated to us, Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād informed us, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that al-Ṣaʿb ibn Jaththāmah al-Asadī gifted the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the leg of a wild donkey while he was in iḥrām, and he returned it, and said: “We are in iḥrām.”
items.ma-1857: Hushaym narrated to us, Manṣūr informed us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ was asked about one who shaved before he slaughtered, and the like of that, and he kept saying: “No blame, no blame.”
items.ma-1858: Hushaym narrated to us, Khālid informed us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ was asked about one who put forward something of his rites before something else, and he kept saying: “No blame.”
items.ma-1859: Hushaym narrated to us, Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād informed us, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “O Allah, forgive those who shave.” A man said: “And those who shorten?” He said: “O Allah, forgive those who shave.” The man said: “And those who shorten?” Then he said, the third or the fourth time: “And those who shorten.”
items.ma-1860: Hushaym narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ set off from ʿArafāt with Usāmah riding behind him, and set off from Jamʿ with al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās riding behind him. He said: And he made the talbiyah until he cast [pebbles at] the Jamrah of al-ʿAqabah.
items.ma-1861: Hushaym narrated to us, from Abū Bishr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a woman travelled by sea, and vowed that if Allah ﵎ saved her she would fast a month. Allah ﷿ saved her, but she did not fast until she died. Then a relative of hers came to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned that to him, and he said: “Fast.”
items.ma-1862: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ṭufāwī narrated to us, Ayyūb narrated to us, from Qatādah, from Mūsā ibn Salamah, he said: We were with Ibn ʿAbbās in Makkah, and I said: “When we are with you we pray four, and when we return to our camps we pray two.” He said: “That is the sunnah of Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ.”
items.ma-1863: Isḥāq — meaning Ibn Yūsuf — narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade that a living thing be taken as a target.
items.ma-1864: Isḥāq — meaning Ibn Yūsuf — narrated to us, from Sharīk, from Khuṣayf, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The sun was eclipsed, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood with his Companions, and recited a long sūrah, then bowed, then raised his head and recited, then bowed, and prostrated two prostrations. Then he stood and recited and bowed, then prostrated two prostrations: four rakʿahs and four prostrations in two rakʿahs.
items.ma-1865: Isḥāq narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Muslim al-Baṭīn, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: When the Prophet ﷺ was expelled from Makkah, Abū Bakr said: “They have expelled their Prophet! Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we are returning. They will surely be destroyed.” Then it was revealed: {Permission is given to those who are being fought, because they have been wronged, and indeed Allah, over their victory, is indeed Qadīr} [al-Ḥajj: 39]. He said: So he knew that there would be fighting. Ibn ʿAbbās said: It is the first verse that was revealed regarding fighting.
items.ma-1866: ʿAbbād ibn ʿAbbād narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever fashions an image will be punished on the Day of Resurrection until he blows into it, and he is not one who blows. And whoever feigns dreaming will be punished on the Day of Resurrection until he ties two barley grains, and he is not one who ties. And whoever listens to the speech of a people who flee from him with it, punishment will be poured into his ears on the Day of Resurrection.”
items.ma-1867: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd al-Ghaṭafānī, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “If one of them, when he comes to his wife, says: In the name of Allah, O Allah, keep Satan away from me, and keep Satan away from what You provide us — then if a child is decreed between the two of them in that, Satan will never harm that child.”
items.ma-1868: Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to me, Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kathīr, from Abū al-Minhāl, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to al-Madīnah while the people were paying in advance for dates, for one year and two years — or he said: two years and three years — and he said: “Whoever pays in advance for dates, let him pay in advance for a known measure and a known weight.”
items.ma-1869:
Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Abū al-Tayyāḥ informed us, from Mūsā ibn Salamah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent eighteen sacrificial camels with a man, and commanded him concerning them with his command, and he departed, then returned to him and said: “Do you see, if one of them becomes exhausted for us?” He said: “Slaughter it, then dye its sandal in its blood, then place it on its side, and do not eat from it, you or anyone of the people of your company.”
ʿAbd Allāh said: My father said: And Ismāʿīl ibn ʿUlayyah did not hear from Abū al-Tayyāḥ except this ḥadīth.
items.ma-1870: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Ayyūb narrated to us, he said: I do not know whether I heard it from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr or was informed of it from him. He said: I came to Ibn ʿAbbās at ʿArafah while he was eating a pomegranate, and he said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ broke his fast at ʿArafah, and Umm al-Faḍl sent milk to him, and he drank it.” And he said: “May Allah curse so-and-so! They went to the greatest of the days of Ḥajj and wiped out its adornment, and the adornment of Ḥajj is only the talbiyah.”
items.ma-1871: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Ayyūb narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah: that ʿAlī burned people who had apostatised from Islam, and that reached Ibn ʿAbbās, and he said: “I would not have burned them with fire, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Do not punish with the punishment of Allah.' And I would have killed them, because of the saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: 'Whoever changes his religion, kill him.'” That reached ʿAlī — may Allah honour his face — and he said: “Woe to the son of the mother of Ibn ʿAbbās.”
items.ma-1872: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Ayyūb informed us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The evil likeness is not for us: the one who returns to his gift is like the dog that returns to its vomit.”
items.ma-1873: Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, ʿAṭāʾ narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: When {When the victory of Allah and the conquest come} was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “My self has been announced to me” — that he would be taken in that year.
items.ma-1874: Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, from Yazīd, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to combine between the two prayers on a journey: al-Maghrib and al-ʿIshāʾ, and al-Ẓuhr and al-ʿAṣr.
items.ma-1875: Muḥammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, from ʿAmr ibn Abī ʿAmr, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Cursed is whoever reviles his father, cursed is whoever reviles his mother, cursed is whoever slaughters for other than Allah, cursed is whoever alters the boundary-markers of the land, cursed is whoever misleads a blind man from the road, cursed is whoever lies with an animal, cursed is whoever does the deed of the people of Lūṭ.”
items.ma-1876: Muḥammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, from Dāwūd ibn Ḥuṣayn, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned Zaynab his daughter to her husband Abū al-ʿĀṣ ibn al-Rabīʿ by the first marriage, and did not introduce anything new.
items.ma-1877: Marwān ibn Shujāʿ narrated to us, Khuṣayf narrated to me, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that he circumambulated the House with Muʿāwiyah, and Muʿāwiyah began to touch all the corners. Ibn ʿAbbās said to him: “Why do you touch these two corners, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not touch them?” Muʿāwiyah said: “Nothing of the House is to be abandoned.” Ibn ʿAbbās said: {Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have a good example} [al-Aḥzāb: 21]. Muʿāwiyah said: “You have spoken truly.”
items.ma-1878: Marwān narrated to us, Khuṣayf narrated to me, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade combining a paternal aunt with a maternal aunt, and two paternal aunts with two maternal aunts.
items.ma-1879: Marwān narrated to us, Khuṣayf narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only forbade the solid garment of qazz. Ibn ʿAbbās said: As for the warp and the border, we see no harm in it.
items.ma-1880: Maʿmar — meaning Ibn Sulaymān al-Raqqī — narrated to us, he said: Khuṣayf said: More than one narrated to me from Ibn ʿAbbās: about the solid [garment] of it; as for the border, no.
items.ma-1881: ʿAththām ibn ʿAlī al-ʿĀmirī narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray two rakʿahs at night, then turn away and use the siwāk.
items.ma-1882:
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us. And ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: Maʿmar informed us, al-Zuhrī informed us, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥusayn, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting with a group of his Companions — ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: of the Anṣār — he said: A great star was shot, and it lit up. He said: “What did you used to say when something like this happened in the Jāhiliyyah?” He said: “We used to say: A great one is born, or a great one dies.” — I said to al-Zuhrī: “Was it shot in the Jāhiliyyah?” He said: “Yes, but it was made severe when the Prophet ﷺ was sent.” — He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed it is not shot for the death of anyone, nor for his life, but our Rabb, Tabāraka ismuhu, when He decrees a matter, the bearers of the ʿArsh glorify, then the inhabitants of the heaven who are next to them glorify, until the glorification reaches this lowest heaven. Then the inhabitants of the heaven who are next to the bearers of the ʿArsh ask for news, and those who are next to the bearers of the ʿArsh say to the bearers of the ʿArsh: What did your Rabb say? And they inform them, and the people of each heaven inform [the next] heaven, until the news reaches this heaven. And the jinn snatch hearing and are shot. What they bring on its proper form is true, but they mix into it and add.”
ʿAbd Allāh said: My father said: ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: “And the jinn snatch, and are shot.”
items.ma-1883: Muḥammad ibn Muṣʿab narrated to us, al-Awzāʿī narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥusayn, from Ibn ʿAbbās: Men of the Anṣār, of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, narrated to me: that they were sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one night when a star was shot … and he mentioned the ḥadīth, except that he said: “When our Rabb decrees a matter, the bearers of the ʿArsh glorify Him, then those who are next to them, then those who are next to them, until the glorification reaches the lowest heaven. Then those who are next to the bearers of the ʿArsh say to the bearers of the ʿArsh: What did your Rabb say? They say: The truth, and He is al-ʿAlī, al-Kabīr. Then they say: such and such. And the people of the heavens inform one another until the news reaches the lowest heaven.” He said: “And the devils come and listen to the news, and they throw it to their allies and cast it to them. What they bring on its proper form is true, but they add to it, and mix, and diminish.”
items.ma-1884: ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, and from ʿĀʾishah, that the two of them said: When [death] came upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he began to cast a khamīṣah over his face, and when he became distressed, we lifted it from him, and he was saying: “May Allah curse the Jews and the Christians; they took the graves of their prophets as mosques.” ʿĀʾishah says: He was warning them against the like of what they did.
items.ma-1885: ʿAmr ibn al-Haytham narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Abū al-Ḥakam, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that Jibrīl ﵇ came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: “The month has been completed at twenty-nine.”
items.ma-1886: Ibn Abī ʿAdī narrated to us, from Saʿīd, from Qatādah, from ʿIkrimah, he said: I said to Ibn ʿAbbās: “I prayed Ẓuhr at al-Baṭḥāʾ behind a foolish old man, and he said the takbīr twenty-two takbīrs, saying the takbīr when he prostrated and when he raised his head.” He said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: “That is the prayer of Abū al-Qāsim ﵊.”
items.ma-1887:
Ibn Abī ʿAdī narrated to us, from Saʿīd. And Ibn Jaʿfar: Saʿīd narrated to us, in meaning — and Ibn Abī ʿAdī said: from Saʿīd — from Abū Yazīd, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ recited in [some] prayers and was silent, so we recite in what the Prophet of Allah recited in them, and are silent in what he was silent. It was said to him: “Perhaps he used to recite to himself!” He became angry at that and said: “Is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ being accused?!”
And Ibn Jaʿfar and ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: “Do you accuse the Messenger of Allah?”
items.ma-1888: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, from Mālik, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Faḍl, from Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The ayyim has more right over herself than her walī, and the virgin is consulted about herself, and her permission is her silence.”
items.ma-1889: al-Walīd ibn Muslim narrated to us, al-Awzāʿī narrated to us, al-Muṭṭalib ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥanṭab narrated to me: that Ibn ʿAbbās used to perform wuḍūʾ once, once, and he would trace that back to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-1890: Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, he heard Sulaymān ibn Yasār, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a woman from Khathʿam asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the morning of Jamʿ, with al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās riding behind him, and she said: “Indeed the obligation of Allah in the Ḥajj upon His servants has reached my father, a very old man who cannot hold on to the saddle. Do you think that I should perform Ḥajj on his behalf?” He said: “Yes.”
items.ma-1891: Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I and al-Faḍl came, while we were on a she-donkey, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was leading the people in prayer at ʿArafah. We passed by some of the row, dismounted from her, left her grazing, and entered the row, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said nothing to me.
items.ma-1892:
Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ went out on the day of the Conquest, fasting, until, when he was at al-Kadīd, he broke his fast, and only the latter of the acts of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is taken.
It was said to Sufyān: “His statement: 'Only the latter is taken' — is it from the words of al-Zuhrī or the words of Ibn ʿAbbās?” He said: “Thus in the ḥadīth.”
items.ma-1893: Sufyān narrated to us, Al-Zuhrī narrated to us, from ʿUbayd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah asked the Prophet ﷺ about a vow that was upon his mother, who died before fulfilling it, and he said: “Fulfil it on her behalf.”
items.ma-1894: Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that Abū Bakr swore an oath to the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ said to him: “Do not swear.”
items.ma-1895: Sufyān narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ibn Waʿlah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “Any hide that is tanned has become pure.”
items.ma-1896: Sufyān narrated to us, from Ziyād — meaning Ibn Saʿd — from Abū al-Zubayr, from Abū Maʿbad, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Move away from the interior of Muḥassir, and take upon yourselves the like of khadhf pebbles.”
items.ma-1897: Sufyān narrated to us, from Ziyād ibn Saʿd, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Faḍl, from Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, tracing it back to the Prophet ﷺ: “The thayyib has more right over herself than her walī, and the virgin is consulted by her father about herself, and her permission is her silence.”
items.ma-1898: Sufyān narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUqbah, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ was at al-Rawḥāʾ, and met a riding party, and greeted them with salām, and said: “Who are the people?” They said: “The Muslims.” They said: “And who are you?” He said: “The Messenger of Allah.” A woman was startled, took hold of the upper arm of a boy, brought him out of her litter, and said: “O Messenger of Allah, does this one have Ḥajj?” He said: “Yes, and for you is a reward.”
items.ma-1899: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUqbah, from Kurayb, the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās, its meaning.
items.ma-1900: Sufyān narrated to us, Sulaymān ibn Suḥaym narrated to us — Sufyān said: I did not memorise anything else from him — he said: I heard it from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maʿbad ibn ʿAbbās, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ lifted the curtain while the people were in rows behind Abū Bakr, and said: “O people, nothing remains of the glad tidings of prophethood except the righteous dream that a Muslim sees or that is shown to him.” Then he said: “Indeed, I have been forbidden to recite while bowing or prostrating. As for the bowing, magnify the Rabb in it; and as for the prostration, strive in supplication, for it is fitting that you be answered.”
items.ma-1901: Sufyān narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Do not punish with the punishment of Allah ﷿.”
items.ma-1902: Sufyān narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās: I bear witness regarding the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he prayed before the sermon on the ʿĪd, then delivered the sermon, and saw that he had not made the women hear, so he came to them, reminded them, admonished them, and commanded them to give ṣadaqah, and the woman began to throw the earring, the ring, and something.
