items.ma-1903: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim, from al-Shaʿbī, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ drank from a bucket of Zamzam while standing. Sufyān said: Thus I think.
items.ma-1904: Sufyān narrated to us, from Ibn Judʿān, from ʿAmr ibn Ḥarmalah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: The Prophet ﷺ drank, with Ibn ʿAbbās on his right and Khālid ibn al-Walīd on his left, and the Prophet ﷺ said to him: “The drink is yours, and if you wish you may prefer Khālid with it.” He said: “I do not prefer anyone over the leftover of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.”
items.ma-1905: Sufyān narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Khuthaym, from Ibn Abī Mulaykah — if Allah wills — meaning: Ibn ʿAbbās asked permission to enter upon ʿĀʾishah, and the sons of her brother kept at her. She said: “I fear that he will extol me.” When she gave him permission, he said: “Between you and meeting the beloved ones there is nothing except that the soul leaves the body. You were the most beloved of the wives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ loved only what is good. And your necklace fell on the night of al-Abwāʾ, and verses of the Qurʾān were revealed about you, and there is no mosque among the mosques of the Muslims in which your excuse is not recited during the hours of the night and the hours of the day.” She said: “Leave me from your extolling, O Ibn ʿAbbās, for by Allah I would have liked.”
items.ma-1906: Sufyān narrated to us, from Layth, from a man, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that he said to her: “You were only named Mother of the Believers so that you may be happy, and it was your name before you were born.”
items.ma-1907: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Karīm, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās — if Allah wills —: that the Prophet ﷺ forbade breathing into the vessel, or blowing into it.
items.ma-1908: Sufyān narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Sālim, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās, tracing it back to the Prophet ﷺ: “If one of them, when he comes to his wife, says: In the name of Allah, O Allah, keep Satan away from me, and keep Satan away from what You provide us — then a child is decreed between the two of them, Satan will not harm him.”
items.ma-1909: Sufyān narrated to us, ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Rufayʿ narrated to us, he said: I and Shaddād ibn Maʿqil entered upon Ibn ʿAbbās, and Ibn ʿAbbās said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ left nothing except what is between these two covers.” And we entered upon Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, and he said the like of that. He said: And al-Mukhtār used to say: the revelation.
items.ma-1910: Sufyān narrated to us, he said: And Mūsā ibn Abī ʿĀʾishah said: I heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr say: Ibn ʿAbbās said: When Qurʾān came down upon the Prophet ﷺ, [and] he wanted to memorise it, Allah ﷿ said: {Do not move your tongue with it to hasten with it. Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation. So when We have recited it, follow its recitation} [al-Qiyāmah: 17].
items.ma-1911:
Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr, he said: Kurayb informed me from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: When he prayed the Fajr prayer, he lay down until he blew.
And we used to say to ʿAmr: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'My eyes sleep, but my heart does not sleep.'”
items.ma-1912: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās: I spent the night at the home of my maternal aunt Maymūnah, and the Prophet ﷺ stood up during the night. He said: So he performed a light wuḍūʾ, and stood, and Ibn ʿAbbās did as he had done. Then he came and stood and prayed, and he turned him and placed him on his right. Then he prayed with the Prophet ﷺ, then lay down until he blew. The muʾadhdhin came to him, then he stood to the prayer and did not perform wuḍūʾ.
items.ma-1913: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ giving a sermon, and he was saying: “Indeed you will be meeting Allah barefoot, naked, uncircumcised.”
items.ma-1914: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and a man fell from his camel and his neck was broken, and he died, while in iḥrām. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Wash him with water and lote, bury him in his two garments, and do not cover his head, for Allah ﷿ will resurrect him on the Day of Resurrection muhillan.” And on one occasion he said: “yuhillu.”
items.ma-1915: Sufyān narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm ibn Abī Ḥurrah, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: “And do not bring perfume near him.”
items.ma-1916: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His saying ﷿: {And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people} [al-Isrāʾ: 60]. He said: It is a vision of the eye that the Prophet ﷺ saw on the night he was taken on the night journey.
items.ma-1917: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from Jābir ibn Zayd, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said — and on one occasion he said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ giving a sermon, saying —: “Whoever does not find sandals, let him wear khuffayn, and whoever does not find an izār, let him wear trousers.”
items.ma-1918: Sufyān narrated to us, ʿAmr said: Jābir ibn Zayd informed me that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: I prayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ eight together and seven together. He said: I said: “O Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ, I think he delayed Ẓuhr and hastened ʿAṣr, and delayed Maghrib and hastened ʿIshāʾ?” He said: “And I think that.”
items.ma-1919: Sufyān narrated to us, ʿAmr said: Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ said: “Who is she?” He said: I said: “They say Maymūnah.” He said: Ibn ʿAbbās informed me: that the Prophet ﷺ married Maymūnah while he was in iḥrām.
items.ma-1920: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: I am among those whom the Prophet ﷺ sent ahead on the night of al-Muzdalifah among the weak ones of his family. And on one occasion he said: Indeed the Prophet ﷺ sent ahead the weak ones of his family.
items.ma-1921: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only performed the ramal around the Kaʿbah in order to show the polytheists his strength.
items.ma-1922: Sufyān narrated to us; ʿAmr said at first: “So we memorised it,” from Ṭāwūs, and once he said: “Ṭāwūs informed me,” from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had himself cupped while he was in iḥrām.
items.ma-1923: My father said: Sufyān also narrated it to us, and he said: ʿAmr, from ʿAṭāʾ and Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ had himself cupped while he was in iḥrām.
items.ma-1924: My father said: And Sufyān said: from ʿAmr, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “When one of you eats, let him not wipe his hand until he licks it or has it licked.”
items.ma-1925: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Al-Muḥaṣṣab is nothing; it is only a halting-place at which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ alighted.
items.ma-1926: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from ʿAṭāʾ, and Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ delayed it until as much of the night as Allah willed had passed. ʿUmar said to him: O Messenger of Allah, the women and the children have slept. So he went out and said: “If it were not that I would burden my ummah, I would command them to pray it at this hour.”
items.ma-1927: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was commanded to prostrate on seven [parts], and was forbidden to hold back his hair and his garments.
items.ma-1928: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from Ṭāwūs, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: As for that which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade to be sold until it is taken possession of, it is food. And Ibn ʿAbbās said, by his own opinion: And I do not reckon everything [else] to be anything but the like of it.
items.ma-1929: Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān ibn Ṣafwān ibn Umayyah al-Jumaḥī narrated to us, he said: Al-Ḥakam ibn Abān narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed in Madinah, resident, not travelling, seven and eight [rakʿahs].
items.ma-1930: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from ʿAwsajah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: A man died in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and left no heir except a slave whom he had freed, so he gave him his inheritance.
items.ma-1931: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥunayn, from Ibn ʿAbbās: I am amazed at one who advances the month, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has said: “Do not fast until you see it,” or he said: “Fast for its sighting.”
items.ma-1932: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from Saʿīd ibn al-Ḥuwayrith, [who] heard Ibn ʿAbbās [say]: We were with the Prophet ﷺ, and he went to the lavatory, then came out and called for food — and once he said: and food was brought to him — and it was said: O Messenger of Allah, will you not perform wuḍūʾ? He said: “I did not pray, that I should perform wuḍūʾ.”
items.ma-1933: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from Abū Maʿbad, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I used to know the end of the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ only by the takbīr. ʿAmr said: I said to him: Did you narrate it to me? He said: No, I did not narrate it to you.
items.ma-1934: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from Abū Maʿbad, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “No man is to be alone with a woman, and no woman is to travel unless she has with her a dhū maḥram.” A man came and said: My wife has gone out for Ḥajj, and I have enrolled in such-and-such a campaign. He said: “Go and perform Ḥajj with your wife.”
items.ma-1935: Sufyān narrated to us, from Sulaymān ibn Abī Muslim, the maternal uncle of Ibn Abī Najīḥ, [who] heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr say: Ibn ʿAbbās said: Thursday, and what is Thursday?! Then he wept until his tears wet the pebbles — and once he said: his tears. We said: O Abū al-ʿAbbās, and what is Thursday? He said: The pain of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ became severe, and he said: “Bring me [something], that I may write for you a writing after which you will never go astray.” They disputed, and dispute is not fitting in the presence of a Prophet, and they said: What is the matter with him? Has he hajara? — Sufyān said: meaning, he raved — Ask him to clarify. So they went to repeat [it] to him, and he said: “Leave me, for what I am in is better than that to which you call me.” And he commanded three things — and Sufyān once said: he enjoined three things — he said: “Expel the polytheists from the Arabian Peninsula, and reward the delegations in the like of what I used to reward them.” And Saʿīd was silent about the third, so I do not know whether he was silent about it deliberately, and he once said: or he forgot it. And Sufyān once said: Either he left it, or he forgot it.
items.ma-1936: Sufyān narrated to us, from Sulaymān, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās: The people used to disperse in every direction, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Let no one depart until the last of his engagement is at the House.”
items.ma-1937: Sufyān narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kathīr, from Abū al-Minhāl, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ came to Madinah, and they were paying in advance for dates for two years and three. He said: “Whoever pays in advance, let him pay in advance for a known measure and a known weight, to a known term.”
items.ma-1938: Sufyān narrated to us, he said: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Yazīd informed me seventy years ago, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: “I do not know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fasted a day seeking its virtue over the other days, except the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ — and Sufyān once said again: except this day, meaning ʿĀshūrāʾ — and this month, the month of Ramaḍān.”
items.ma-1939: Sufyān narrated to us; ʿUbayd Allāh informed me that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: I am among those whom the Prophet ﷺ sent ahead on the night of al-Muzdalifah among the weak ones of his family.
items.ma-1940: Sufyān narrated to us, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās: The Prophet ﷺ was commanded to prostrate on seven [parts], and was forbidden to hold back hair or a garment.
items.ma-1941: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmmār, from Sālim: Ibn ʿAbbās was asked about a man who killed a believer, then repented, believed, did righteous deeds, and then was guided. He said: Woe to you, and how could there be guidance for him?! I heard your Prophet ﷺ say: “The slain one will come clinging to the killer, saying: O Rabb, ask this one why he killed me?” By Allah, Allah ﷿ revealed it to your Prophet ﷺ, and did not abrogate it after having revealed it. He said: Woe to you, and how could there be guidance for him?!
items.ma-1942: Ibn Idrīs narrated to us, he said: Yazīd informed us, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was shrouded in three garments: in his shirt in which he died, and a Najrānī ḥullah. The ḥullah is two garments.
items.ma-1943: Ibn Idrīs narrated to us; Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād informed us, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had himself cupped between Makkah and Madinah while he was fasting, in iḥrām.
items.ma-1944: Ismāʿīl narrated to us; Hishām informed us, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said concerning the mukātab: “He is freed, in proportion to what he has paid, with the blood-money of a free man, and in proportion to what remains enslaved of him, with the blood-money of a slave.”
items.ma-1945: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, from Khālid al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, [who said]: ʿAmmār, the mawlā of Banū Hāshim, narrated to me, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ died when he was sixty-five years old.
items.ma-1946: Jarīr narrated to us, from Qābūs, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The last hardship that the believer meets is death. And regarding His saying: {on the Day the sky will be like al-muhl} [al-Maʿārij: 8], he said: Like the dregs of oil. And regarding His saying: {the hours of the night} [Āl ʿImrān: 113], he said: The middle of the night. And he said: Do you know what the going of knowledge is? He said: It is the going of the scholars from the earth.
items.ma-1947: Jarīr narrated to us, from Qābūs, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed the man in whose inside there is nothing of the Qurʾān is like a ruined house.”
items.ma-1948: Jarīr narrated to us, from Qābūs, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in Makkah, then was commanded to make the Hijrah, and there was revealed to him: {And say: My Rabb, cause me to enter with a sound entrance and cause me to exit with a sound exit, and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority} [al-Isrāʾ: 80].
items.ma-1949: Jarīr narrated to us, from Qābūs, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Two qiblahs are not fitting in one land, and there is no jizyah upon a Muslim.”
items.ma-1950: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from Sufyān, he said: Al-Mughīrah ibn al-Nuʿmān narrated to me, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “The people will be gathered barefoot, naked, uncircumcised, and the first to be clothed will be Ibrāhīm ﵇.” Then he recited: {As We began the first creation, We shall repeat it} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 104].
items.ma-1951: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from al-Awzāʿī; al-Zuhrī narrated to us, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ drank milk, then rinsed his mouth, and said: “Indeed it has fat.”
items.ma-1952: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿbah; Qatādah narrated to us, he said: I heard Jābir ibn Zayd, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The daughter of Ḥamzah was mentioned to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: “She is the daughter of my brother through suckling.”
items.ma-1953: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us; al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Ḥabīb, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ combined the Ẓuhr and the ʿAṣr, and the Maghrib and the ʿIshāʾ in Madinah, without fear or rain. Ibn ʿAbbās was asked: And what did he intend by that? He said: He intended not to put his ummah in hardship.
items.ma-1954: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us; al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Abū Ẓabyān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: A man of Banū ʿĀmir came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, show me the seal that is between your shoulders, for I am among the most skilled of people in medicine. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: “Shall I not show you a sign?” He said: Yes. He said: So he looked at a palm tree and said: “Call that cluster.” He said: So he called it, and it came leaping until it stood before him. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to it: “Return.” So it returned to its place. The ʿĀmirī said: O family of Banū ʿĀmir, I have never seen, like today, a greater sorcerer than this man.
items.ma-1955: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us; al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Masʿūd ibn Mālik, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I was given victory by the east wind, and ʿĀd were destroyed by the west wind.”
items.ma-1956: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us; al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Ziyād ibn al-Ḥuṣayn, from Abū al-ʿĀliyah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying ﷿: {The heart did not lie about what it saw} [al-Najm: 11], he said: Muḥammad saw his Rabb ﷿ with his heart twice.
items.ma-1957: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, from Abū Mālik al-Ashjaʿī, from Ibn Ḥudayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever has a daughter born to him and does not bury her alive, and does not humiliate her, and does not prefer his child over her — meaning the male — Allah will cause him to enter Paradise because of her.”
items.ma-1958: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us; ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ travelled on a journey and stayed nineteen [days], praying two rakʿahs, two rakʿahs. Ibn ʿAbbās said: So when we travel and stay nineteen, we pray two rakʿahs, two rakʿahs, and when we stay more than that, we pray four.
items.ma-1959: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us; Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: On the day of al-Ṭāʾif, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ freed those of the slaves of the polytheists who came out to him.
items.ma-1960: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us; al-Shaybānī narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade al-muḥāqalah and al-muzābanah. He said: And ʿIkrimah used to dislike the sale of cut green barley.
items.ma-1961: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us; Abū Isḥāq — meaning al-Shaybānī — narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote to the people of Jurash, forbidding them from mixing raisins and dates.
items.ma-1962: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us; al-Shaybānī narrated to us, from al-Shaʿbī, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed over the occupant of a grave after he had been buried.
items.ma-1963: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us; al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Abū ʿUmar, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Raisins used to be soaked for the Prophet ﷺ. He said: So he would drink it that day, and the next, and the day after the next until the evening of the third; then he would give a command about it, and it would be given to drink or poured out.
items.ma-1964: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us; Ajlaḥ narrated to us, from Yazīd ibn al-Aṣamm, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard a man say: What Allah wills and you will. He said: “Rather, what Allah wills alone.”
items.ma-1965: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us; al-Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Yaḥyā ibn al-Jazzār, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed in an open space with nothing in front of him.
items.ma-1966: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us; al-Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥah in a detachment, and that coincided with Friday. He said: So he sent his companions ahead and said: I will stay behind and pray the Friday prayer with the Prophet ﷺ, then catch up with them. He said: When the Messenger ﷺ had prayed, he saw him and said: “What prevented you from going out in the morning with your companions?” He said: He said: I wanted to pray the Friday prayer with you, then catch up with them. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “If you spent what is on the earth, you would not attain their morning journey.”
items.ma-1967: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us; al-Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Najdah al-Ḥarūrī wrote to Ibn ʿAbbās asking him about the killing of boys; and about the khumus, for whom it is; and about a boy, when orphanhood ceases for him; and about the women, whether he used to take them out, or whether they attended the fighting; and about the slave, whether he has a share in the spoils. He said: So Ibn ʿAbbās wrote to him: As for the boys, if you are al-Khaḍir, knowing the disbeliever from the believer, then kill them. As for the khumus, we used to say that it is for us, but our people claimed that it is not for us. As for the women, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to take women out with him, and they would treat the sick and tend the wounded, and they did not attend the fighting. As for the boy, orphanhood ceases for him when he reaches puberty. As for the slave, he has no share in the spoils, but a small gift used to be given to them.
items.ma-1968: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us; al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Muslim al-Baṭīn, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There are no days in which righteous deeds are more beloved to Allah ﷿ than these days” — meaning, the days of the ten. He said: They said: O Messenger of Allah, not even jihād in the way of Allah? He said: “Not even jihād in the way of Allah, except a man who went out with himself and his wealth, and then did not return from that with anything.”
items.ma-1969: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us; al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Abū Ṣāliḥ. He said: And al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Mujāhid — Ibn ʿAbbās is not in it — from the Prophet ﷺ, the like of it, meaning: “There are no days in which the deed in them …”
items.ma-1970: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us; al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Muslim al-Baṭīn, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: A woman came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, my mother has died owing a month of fasting; shall I make it up on her behalf? He said: “Do you see: if your mother had owed a debt, would you not have paid it?” She said: Yes. He said: “Then the debt of Allah ﷿ is more deserving.”
items.ma-1971: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us; Ibn Abī Dhiʾb narrated to us, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbbās, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmayr, the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “If I remain until next year, I will surely fast the ninth day.”
items.ma-1972: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us; Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed the raml in his Ḥajj and in all his ʿumrahs, and Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān and the caliphs.
items.ma-1973: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us; al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAmr al-Fuqaymī narrated to us, from Mihrān Abū Ṣafwān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever wants Ḥajj, let him hasten.”
items.ma-1974: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Muḥammad — meaning al-Muḥāribī — narrated to us; al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, from Ṣafwān al-Jammāl, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever wants Ḥajj, let him hasten.”
items.ma-1975: Ismāʿīl narrated to us; Sufyān al-Thawrī informed us, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed at the eclipse of the sun eight rakʿahs and four prostrations.
items.ma-1976:
Ismāʿīl narrated to us; Hishām informed us, he said: Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr wrote to me, narrating from ʿIkrimah: that ʿUmar used to say about al-ḥarām: It is an oath, which he expiates.
Hishām said: And Yaḥyā wrote to me, narrating from Yaʿlā ibn Ḥakīm, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, that Ibn ʿAbbās used to say about al-ḥarām: It is an oath, which he expiates. And Ibn ʿAbbās said: {There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of Allah an excellent example} [al-Aḥzāb: 21].
items.ma-1977:
Ismāʿīl narrated to us; Mūsā ibn Sālim Abū Jahḍam narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās narrated to me, [he] heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was a commanded slave. He conveyed — by Allah — what he was sent with, and he did not single us out, apart from the people, with anything, except three: he commanded us to complete the wuḍūʾ, and not to eat ṣadaqah, and not to let a donkey mount a horse.
Mūsā said: I met ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥasan and said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd Allāh narrated to me such and such. He said: Horses were few among Banū Hāshim, so he loved that they should become many among them.
items.ma-1978: Ismāʿīl narrated to us; ʿAlī ibn Zayd informed us, he said: ʿUmar ibn Abī Ḥarmalah narrated to me, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I and Khālid ibn al-Walīd entered with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ upon Maymūnah bint al-Ḥārith, and she said: Shall we not feed you from a gift that Umm ʿUfayq gave us? He said: So two roasted lizards were brought, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ spat. Khālid said to him: It is as though you find it loathsome? He said: “Yes.” She said: Shall I not give you to drink some milk that she gave us? He said: “Yes indeed.” He said: So a vessel of milk was brought, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ drank, while I was on his right and Khālid on his left. He said to me: “The drink is yours, and if you wish you may give Khālid preference with it.” I said: I would not give anyone preference over myself with your leftover. Then he said: “Whoever Allah has fed food, let him say: O Allah, bless us in it and feed us better than it. And whoever Allah has given milk to drink, let him say: O Allah, bless us in it and give us more of it. For there is nothing that suffices in place of food and drink except milk.”
items.ma-1979: ʿAffān narrated to us; Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us; ʿAlī ibn Zayd informed us, from ʿUmar ibn Ḥarmalah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from Umm ʿUfayq: She gave her sister Maymūnah two lizards as a gift … and he mentioned it.
items.ma-1980: Abū Muʿāwiyah and Wakīʿ narrated to us, the meaning being one, they said: Al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Mujāhid — Wakīʿ said: I heard Mujāhid — narrating from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ passed by two graves and said: “Indeed they are being punished, and they are not being punished for something major. As for one of them, he did not keep himself clear of urine — Wakīʿ said: of his urine — and as for the other, he used to go about with slander.” Then he took a palm frond and split it into two halves, and planted one in each grave. They said: O Messenger of Allah, why did you do this? He said: “Perhaps their punishment will be lightened for as long as they do not dry.” Wakīʿ said: “taybasā.”
items.ma-1981: Ḥusayn narrated to us; Shaybān narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by a walled garden of the walled gardens of Madinah, and heard the voices of two human beings being punished in their graves … and he mentioned it. And he said: “until they dry,” or: “for as long as they do not dry.”
items.ma-1982: Ismāʿīl narrated to us; Hishām al-Dastuwāʾī informed us, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed the effeminate men and the women who imitate men, and said: “Expel them from your houses.” So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ expelled so-and-so, and ʿUmar expelled so-and-so.
items.ma-1983: Ismāʿīl narrated to us; Ayyūb informed us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I bear witness concerning the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he prayed before the sermon, then gave the sermon, then he saw that he had not made the women hear, so he went to them, with Bilāl beside him spreading out his garment, and he admonished them and commanded them to give ṣadaqah. So the woman began to throw — and Ayyūb pointed to his ear and to his throat, as though he meant the pearl and the necklace.
items.ma-1984: Ismāʿīl narrated to us; Hishām al-Dastuwāʾī narrated to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said concerning the mukātab: “He is freed, in proportion to what he has paid, with the blood-money of a free man, and in proportion to what remains enslaved of him, with the blood-money of a slave.”
items.ma-1985: Ismāʿīl narrated to us; Ḥātim ibn Abī Ṣaghīrah informed us, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from ʿIkrimah, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Fast for its sighting and break the fast for its sighting, and if clouds come between you and it, then complete the count as thirty, and do not go out to meet the month at all.” Ḥātim said: meaning, the count of Shaʿbān.
items.ma-1986: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik; ʿAṭāʾ narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set off from ʿArafah with Usāmah ibn Zayd riding behind him, and the she-camel swerved with him, while he was raising his hands, not passing beyond his head. He proceeded at his gentle pace until he came to Jamʿ. Then he set off the next day with al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās riding behind him, and he did not cease to make the talbiyah until he threw Jamrat al-ʿAqabah.
items.ma-1987: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Ḥabīb ibn Shihāb; my father narrated to me, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on the day he addressed the people at Tabūk: “There is none among the people like a man taking hold of the head of his horse, striving in the way of Allah ﷿, and keeping away from the evils of the people, and like another, in the open country with his livestock, who hosts his guest and gives him his due.
items.ma-1988: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Mālik; Zayd ibn Aslam narrated to me, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ ate a shoulder, then prayed and did not perform wuḍūʾ.
items.ma-1989: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Hishām; Qatādah narrated to me, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the milk of a jallālah ewe, and the mujaththamah, and drinking from the mouth of the waterskin.
items.ma-1990: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj; al-Ḥasan ibn Muslim narrated to me, from Ṭāwūs, he said: I was with Ibn ʿAbbās, and Zayd ibn Thābit said to him: Do you give a fatwā that a menstruating woman may depart before her last engagement is at the House? He said: Yes. He said: Do not give a fatwā about that. He said: If not, then ask so-and-so, the Anṣārī woman, whether the Prophet ﷺ commanded her to do that. Then Zayd returned to Ibn ʿAbbās laughing and said: I see only that you have spoken truly.
items.ma-1991: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no Hijrah after the Conquest, but [there is] jihād and intention, and when you are called to march out, then march out.”
items.ma-1992: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Sufyān; Ṣafwān ibn Sulaym narrated to us, from Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Ibn ʿAbbās — Sufyān said: I know it only to be from the Prophet ﷺ — {or a remnant of knowledge} [al-Aḥqāf: 4], he said: “The line.”
items.ma-1993: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿbah; Mukhawwal narrated to me, from Muslim al-Baṭīn, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite in the Ṣubḥ prayer on Friday: {Alif Lām Mīm. The revelation} and {Has there come}, and in the Friday prayer, Sūrat al-Jumuʿah and {When the hypocrites come to you}.
items.ma-1994: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, he said: ʿUmar ibn ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī al-Khuwār informed me, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ate of what the fire had changed, then prayed and did not perform wuḍūʾ.
items.ma-1995: Yaḥyā narrated to us; Ibn ʿAwn narrated to us, from Muḥammad, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: We travelled with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ between Makkah and Madinah, and he prayed two rakʿahs, fearing none but Allah ﷿.
items.ma-1996: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Hishām; Qatādah narrated to us, from Mūsā ibn Salamah, he said: I said to Ibn ʿAbbās: If I do not catch the prayer in the mosque, how many do I pray at al-Baṭḥāʾ? He said: Two rakʿahs; that is the sunnah of Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ.
items.ma-1997: Yaḥyā narrated to us, he said: Sufyān dictated it to me up to Shuʿbah; he said: I heard ʿAmr ibn Murrah; ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith al-Muʿallim narrated to me; Ṭalīq ibn Qays al-Ḥanafī, the brother of Abū Ṣāliḥ, narrated to me, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to supplicate: “Rabb, help me and do not help against me, and give me victory and do not give victory against me, and wa-mkur lī wa-lā tamkur ʿalayya, and guide me and make guidance easy for me, and give me victory over whoever has wronged me. Rabb, make me ever thankful to You, ever remembering You, ever fearful of You, ever obedient to You, humbly submissive to You, ever sighing and turning back to You. Rabb, accept my repentance, wash away my sin, answer my call, make firm my argument, guide my heart, direct my tongue, and draw out the rancour of my heart.”
items.ma-1998: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿbah; Abū Bishr narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to fast until we said: He does not break the fast, and he used to break the fast until we said: He does not fast. And he did not fast a complete month since he came to Madinah except Ramaḍān.
items.ma-1999: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿbah; Qatādah narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “This and this are equal” — the little finger and the thumb.
items.ma-2000: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn al-Akhnas, he said: Al-Walīd ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, from Yūsuf ibn Māhak, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “No man acquires a portion of knowledge from the stars except that he acquires with it a branch of sorcery; the more he adds, the more it adds.”
items.ma-2001: Yaḥyā narrated to us; al-Ḥusayn ibn Dhakwān narrated to us, from Abū Rajāʾ; Ibn ʿAbbās narrated to me, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “If he intends a good deed and does it, ten are written; and if he does not do it, a good deed is written; and if he intends an evil deed and does it, an evil deed is written; and if he does not do it, a good deed is written.”
items.ma-2002: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwah; Wahb ibn Kaysān narrated to me, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās. He said: And Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās. He said: And al-Zuhrī narrated to me, from ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ate meat or a bone with meat on it, then prayed and did not touch water.
items.ma-2003: Yaḥyā narrated to us; Ibn Jurayj narrated to us; ʿAṭāʾ narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a domestic ewe belonging to Maymūnah died, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Why did you not benefit from its hide? Why did you not tan it, for that is its dhakāh?”
items.ma-2004: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj; al-Ḥasan ibn Muslim narrated to me, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the ʿĪd without adhān or iqāmah.
items.ma-2005: Yaḥyā narrated to us; I heard al-Aʿmash; Muslim narrated to me, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that a woman said: O Messenger of Allah, her mother had a month of fasting owed, and she died; shall I fast it on her behalf? He said: “If your mother had owed a debt, would you have paid it?” She said: Yes. He said: “Then the debt of Allah ﷿ is more deserving of being paid.”
items.ma-2006: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Hishām; Yaḥyā narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed the women who imitate men and the effeminate men, and said: “Expel them from your houses.” He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ expelled so-and-so, and ʿUmar expelled so-and-so.
items.ma-2007: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from al-Awzāʿī, he said: Al-Zuhrī narrated to us, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ drank milk, then rinsed his mouth and said: “Indeed it has fat.”
items.ma-2008: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Sufyān; Sulaymān — meaning al-Aʿmash — narrated to me, from Yaḥyā ibn ʿUmārah, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Abū Ṭālib fell ill, so Quraysh came to him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to him to visit him, and by his head was the seat of a man. Abū Jahl stood up and sat in it. They said: Your nephew speaks ill of our gods. And he said: What is the matter with your people, that they complain of you? He said: “O uncle, I want from them one word by which the Arabs will submit to them, and the non-Arabs will pay jizyah to them.” He said: What is it? He said: “There is no deity except Allah.” So they stood up and said: Has he made the gods one deity? He said: And there was revealed: {Ṣād. By the Qurʾān containing the reminder} [Ṣād: 1], and he recited until he reached: {Indeed, this is a thing to be wondered at} [Ṣād: 5]. ʿAbd Allāh said: My father said: And Abū Usāmah narrated to us; al-Aʿmash narrated to us; ʿAbbād narrated to us … and he mentioned the like of it. And my father said: Al-Ashjaʿī said: Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbbād.
items.ma-2009: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from ʿUyaynah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān; my father narrated to me, he said: A man came to Ibn ʿAbbās and said: I am a man of the people of Khurāsān, and our land is a cold land — and he mentioned kinds of drink. He said: Avoid whatever intoxicates, of raisins or dates or other than that? He said: What do you say about nabīdh of the jar? He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade nabīdh of the jar.
items.ma-2010: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn al-Akhnas, he said: Ibn Abī Mulaykah informed me that Ibn ʿAbbās informed him, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “It is as though I am looking at him, black, bow-legged, dismantling it stone by stone” — meaning the Kaʿbah.
items.ma-2011: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Dhiʾb; Qāriẓ narrated to me, from Abū Ghaṭafān, he said: I saw Ibn ʿAbbās perform wuḍūʾ. He said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Perform istinthār twice, thoroughly, or three times.”
items.ma-2012: Yaḥyā narrated to us; Hishām narrated to us; Qatādah narrated to us, from Abū al-ʿĀliyah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say at times of distress: “There is no deity except Allah, al-ʿAẓīm, al-Ḥalīm. There is no deity except Allah, Rabb of the Mighty Throne. There is no deity except Allah, Rabb of the heavens and the earth, Rabb of the Noble Throne.”
items.ma-2013: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿbah; al-Ḥakam narrated to me, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “I was given victory by the east wind, and ʿĀd were destroyed by the west wind.”
items.ma-2014: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj; ʿAmr ibn Dīnār informed me that Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ informed him that Ibn ʿAbbās informed him: that the Prophet ﷺ married while he was in iḥrām.
items.ma-2015: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj; ʿAmr ibn Dīnār informed me that Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ informed him that Ibn ʿAbbās informed him that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ giving a khuṭbah, and he was saying: “Whoever does not find an izār and finds trousers, let him wear them; and whoever does not find sandals and finds khuffs, let him wear them.” I said: Did he not say: Let him cut them? He said: No.
items.ma-2016: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, he said: Saʿīd ibn al-Ḥuwayrith narrated to me, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ relieved himself, then ate and did not touch water.
items.ma-2017: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Hishām, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: It was revealed to the Prophet ﷺ when he was forty-three [years old], and he stayed in Makkah ten and in Madinah ten, and he was taken when he was sixty-three.
items.ma-2018: Yaḥyā narrated to us; Ḥumayd narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made this ṣadaqah obligatory: so much and so much, and half a ṣāʿ of wheat.
items.ma-2019: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from Abū Jamrah, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: The Prophet ﷺ prayed thirteen [rakʿahs] at night.
items.ma-2020:
Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿbah; Abū Jamrah narrated to me. And Ibn Jaʿfar said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Jamrah, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās [say]: When the delegation of ʿAbd al-Qays came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said: “Which people are the delegation — or he said: the people?” They said: Rabīʿah. He said: “Welcome to the delegation — or he said: the people — neither humiliated nor regretful.” They said: O Messenger of Allah, we have come to you from a distant journey, and between us and you is this clan of the disbelievers of Muḍar, and we are unable to come to you except in a sacred month, so inform us of a matter by which we may enter Paradise and by which we may inform those behind us. And they asked him about drinks, so he commanded them four things and forbade them four things:
He commanded them to have īmān in Allah. He said: “Do you know what īmān in Allah is?” They said: Allah and His Messenger know best. He said: “The testimony that there is no deity except Allah and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah, establishing the prayer, giving zakāh, fasting Ramaḍān, and that you give the khumus from the spoils.”
And he forbade them the gourd, the ḥantam, the naqīr and the pitch-coated vessel — he said: and perhaps he said: the tar-coated vessel — he said: “Memorise them, and inform those behind you of them.”
items.ma-2021: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿbah. And Ibn Jaʿfar said: Shuʿbah narrated to us; Abū Jamrah narrated to me, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: A red qaṭīfah was placed in the grave of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-2022: Yaḥyā ibn Abī Bukayr narrated to us; Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: It was said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he had finished with Badr: Go for the caravan; there is nothing in front of it. He said: Then al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib called out to him: It is not fitting for you. He said: “Why?” He said: Because Allah ﷿ only promised you one of the two groups, and He has given you what He promised you.
items.ma-2023: Yaḥyā ibn Abī Bukayr narrated to us; Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: A man of Banū Sulaym passed by a group of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was driving sheep of his, and he gave them the greeting of peace. They said: He only gave us the greeting in order to seek refuge from us. So they went for him and killed him, and brought his sheep to the Prophet ﷺ, and this verse was revealed: {O you who have believed, when you strike out in the way of Allah, then ascertain} [al-Nisāʾ: 94].
items.ma-2024: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿbah; ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Maysarah narrated to me, from Ṭāwūs, he said: A man came to Ibn ʿAbbās and asked him … And Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd [said]: Shuʿbah informed us; ʿAbd al-Malik apprised me, he said: I heard Ṭāwūs say: A man asked Ibn ʿAbbās — the meaning [being the same] — about His saying ﷿: {Say: I do not ask you for it any payment except the affection in kinship} [al-Shūrā: 23], and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: The kinship of Muḥammad ﷺ. Ibn ʿAbbās said: You have been hasty! There was no clan of Quraysh but that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had kinship with them, so there was revealed: {Say: I do not ask you for it any payment except the affection in kinship}: except that you keep the ties of kinship that are between me and you.
items.ma-2025: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj; ʿAṭāʾ informed us, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to a woman of the Anṣār — Ibn ʿAbbās named her, and I forgot her name —: “What prevented you from performing Ḥajj with us this year?” She said: O Prophet of Allah, we only had two camels for drawing water, and Abū so-and-so and his son — meaning her husband and her son — rode one of the camels and left one camel with which we draw water. The Prophet ﷺ said: “Then when it is Ramaḍān, perform ʿumrah in it, for an ʿumrah in it is equal to a Ḥajj.”
items.ma-2026: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Mūsā ibn Abī ʿĀʾishah, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from ʿĀʾishah and Ibn ʿAbbās: that Abū Bakr kissed the Prophet ﷺ while he was dead.
items.ma-2027: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Sufyān, he said: Mughīrah ibn al-Nuʿmān narrated to me, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ: “The people will be gathered naked, barefoot, uncircumcised, and the first to be clothed will be Ibrāhīm ﵊.” Then he recited: {As We began the first creation, We shall repeat it}.
items.ma-2028: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿbah; Salamah ibn Kuhayl narrated to me, he said: I heard Abū al-Ḥakam say: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās about nabīdh of the jar, and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade nabīdh of the jar and the gourd. And he said: Whoever is pleased to prohibit what Allah and His Messenger prohibited, let him prohibit nabīdh.
items.ma-2029: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Fiṭr; Abū al-Ṭufayl narrated to us, he said: I said to Ibn ʿAbbās: Your people claim that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed the raml at the House, and that it is a sunnah. He said: They spoke truly and they lied. I said: How did they speak truly and lie? He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did perform the raml at the House, and it is not a sunnah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his companions performed the raml while the polytheists were on the mountain of Quʿayqiʿān, and it reached him that they were saying that weakness was in them, so he commanded them to perform the raml in order to show them that there was strength in them.
items.ma-2030: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿbah; Muḥammad ibn Juḥādah narrated to us, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās. And Wakīʿ said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Juḥādah, he said: I heard Abū Ṣāliḥ narrating after he had grown old, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed the women who visit graves, and those who build mosques over them and place lamps on them.
items.ma-2031: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn al-Mubārak, he said: Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr narrated to me that ʿUmar ibn Muʿattib informed him that Abū Ḥasan, the mawlā of Abū Nawfal, informed him: that he sought a fatwā from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning a male slave who had a female slave as his wife; he divorced her with two divorces, then both were freed. Is it fitting for him to propose to her? He said: Yes; the Messenger of Allah ﷺ judged that.
items.ma-2032: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿbah; and Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar [said]: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning the one who comes to his wife while she is menstruating: “He gives ṣadaqah of a dīnār, or of half a dīnār.” ʿAbd Allāh said: My father said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Bahz did not raise it.
items.ma-2033: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Mujālid, from al-Shaʿbī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever speaks on the day of Jumuʿah while the imām is giving the khuṭbah is like the donkey carrying books, and the one who says to him: Be silent, has no Jumuʿah.”
items.ma-2034: Ibn Numayr narrated to me; Hishām narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: If only the people would reduce from a third to a quarter, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The third is a lot.”
items.ma-2035: Ibn Numayr narrated to us; al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us; al-Minhāl ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: that a man came to Ibn ʿAbbās and said: Was it revealed to the Prophet ﷺ ten in Makkah and ten in Madinah? He said: Who says that? It was revealed to him fifteen in Makkah and ten in Madinah, sixty-five and more.
items.ma-2036: Ibn Numayr narrated to us; Fuḍayl — meaning Ibn Ghazwān — narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said in the Farewell Ḥajj: “O people, what day is this?” They said: This is a sacred day. He said: “What land is this?” They said: A sacred land. He said: “And what month is this?” They said: A sacred month. He said: “Indeed your wealth, your blood and your honour are sacred upon you, like the sanctity of this day of yours, in this land of yours, in this month of yours.” Then he repeated it several times, then raised his head to the sky and said: “O Allah, have I conveyed?” several times. Ibn ʿAbbās said: By Allah, it was truly a bequest to his Rabb ﷿. Then he said: “Let the one who is present convey to the one who is absent. Do not return after me as disbelievers, some of you striking the necks of others.”
items.ma-2037: Ibn Numayr narrated to us; Mūsā ibn Muslim al-Ṭaḥḥān al-Ṣaghīr narrated to us, he said: I heard ʿIkrimah raising the ḥadīth — as I think — to Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever leaves the snakes alone for fear of seeking them out is not of us; we have not been at peace with them since we fought them.”
items.ma-2038: Ibn Numayr narrated to us; ʿUthmān ibn Ḥakīm narrated to us, he said: Saʿīd ibn Yasār informed me, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite in the Fajr prayer in the first rakʿah: {We have believed in Allah and in what was revealed to us and what was revealed to Ibrāhīm} to the end of the verse [al-Baqarah: 136], and in the second rakʿah: {We have believed in Allah, and bear witness that we are Muslims} [Āl ʿImrān: 52].
items.ma-2039: Wakīʿ narrated to us; Sufyān narrated to us, from Hishām ibn Isḥāq ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kinānah, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out humble, imploring, lowly, plainly dressed, unhurried, and led the people in two rakʿahs as he prays at the ʿĪd; he did not give a khuṭbah like this khuṭbah of yours.
items.ma-2040: Ibn Numayr narrated to us; Ḥajjāj informed us, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: When the Prophet ﷺ left Makkah, ʿAlī went out with the daughter of Ḥamzah, and ʿAlī, Jaʿfar and Zayd disputed over her before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. ʿAlī said: She is the daughter of my uncle, and I brought her out. Jaʿfar said: She is the daughter of my uncle, and her maternal aunt is with me. And Zayd said: She is the daughter of my brother. Zayd was bound in brotherhood to Ḥamzah; the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had made them brothers. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Zayd: “You are my mawlā and her mawlā,” and he said to ʿAlī: “You are my brother and my companion,” and he said to Jaʿfar: “You resemble me in my physical form and my character, and she is to her maternal aunt.”
items.ma-2041: Yaʿlā narrated to us; Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, from al-Qaʿqāʿ ibn Ḥakīm, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Waʿlah, he said: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās about the sale of wine, and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had a friend from Thaqīf, or from Daws, and he met him in Makkah in the year of the Conquest with a skin of wine that he was giving to him as a gift. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “O Abū so-and-so, did you not know that Allah has forbidden it?” The man turned to his servant and said: Go and sell it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “O Abū so-and-so, what did you command him?” He said: I commanded him to sell it. He said: “Indeed the One who forbade drinking it has forbidden selling it.” Then he gave a command about it, and it was poured out in al-Baṭḥāʾ.
items.ma-2042: Yaʿlā narrated to us; Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to present the Book to Jibrīl ﵇ every Ramaḍān. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ woke on the morning after the night in which he presented what he presented, he woke more generous than the sent wind; he was not asked for anything except that he gave it. Then, in the month after which he died, he presented it to him twice.
items.ma-2043: Yaʿlā narrated to us; ʿUmar ibn Dharr narrated to us, from his father, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Jibrīl: “What prevents you from visiting us more than you visit us?” He said: So there was revealed: {And we do not descend except by the command of your Rabb} to the end of the verse [Maryam: 64].
items.ma-2044:
Jaʿfar ibn ʿAwn narrated to us; Ibn Jurayj informed us, from ʿAṭāʾ, he said: We attended with Ibn ʿAbbās the funeral of Maymūnah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, at Sarif. He said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: This is Maymūnah. When you lift her bier, do not jolt it and do not shake it, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had nine women, and he used to apportion [his time] among eight, and for one he did not apportion.
ʿAṭāʾ said: The one for whom he did not apportion was Ṣafiyyah.
items.ma-2045: Yaʿlā narrated to us; ʿUthmān narrated to us, from Saʿīd, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: What the Messenger of Allah ﷺ most often prayed in the two rakʿahs before Fajr was: {We have believed in Allah and in what was revealed to us and what was revealed to Ibrāhīm and Ismāʿīl} to the end of the verse, and in the other: {We have believed in Allah, and bear witness that we are Muslims}.
items.ma-2046: Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us; ʿUthmān ibn Ḥakīm narrated to us, he said: I asked Saʿīd ibn Jubayr about fasting in Rajab, what do you think of it? He said: Ibn ʿAbbās narrated to me: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to fast until we said: He does not break the fast, and he would break the fast until we said: He does not fast.
items.ma-2047: Yaʿlā ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us; Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The best of your kohls is antimony; it clears the sight and makes the hair grow.”
items.ma-2048: Asbāṭ ibn Muḥammad narrated to us; ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, he said: Ibn ʿAbbās met me and said: Have you married? He said: I said: No. He said: Marry. Then he met me after that and said: Have you married? He said: I said: No. He said: Marry, for the best of this ummah was the one with the most women.
items.ma-2049: Asbāṭ narrated to us; Abū Isḥāq al-Shaybānī narrated to us, from Ḥammād, from Ibrāhīm, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When you send the dog and it eats from the game, do not eat, for it only held it for itself; and when you send it and it kills and does not eat, then eat, for it only held it for its owner.” ʿAbd Allāh said: And in my father's book it was: from Ibrāhīm, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās, and my father struck it out: thus Asbāṭ said.
items.ma-2050: Shujāʿ ibn al-Walīd narrated to us, from Abū Janāb al-Kalbī, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Three are obligatory upon me and voluntary for you: the Witr, the naḥr, and the Ḍuḥā prayer.”
items.ma-2051: Abū Khālid Sulaymān ibn Ḥayyān narrated to us, he said: I heard al-Aʿmash, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ set off from Muzdalifah before the rising of the sun.
items.ma-2052: Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us; Ayyūb informed us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Seek it in the last ten, in the ninth [night] remaining, or the fifth remaining, or the seventh remaining.”
items.ma-2053: Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth narrated to us; Ḥajjāj ibn Arṭāh narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not fight a people until he had called them.
items.ma-2054: Ḥafṣ narrated to us; Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿĀbis, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to command his daughters and his wives to go out on the two ʿĪds.
items.ma-2055: Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā ibn Abī Zāʾidah narrated to us; my father narrated to me, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Arqam ibn Shuraḥbīl, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: When the Prophet ﷺ fell ill, he commanded Abū Bakr to lead the people in prayer. Then he found some lightness and went out. When Abū Bakr sensed him, he wanted to step back, but the Prophet ﷺ signalled to him, so he sat beside Abū Bakr, on his left, and began from the verse at which Abū Bakr had arrived.
items.ma-2056: Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā narrated to us; Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Abū al-Qāsim, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ threw the jamrah — Jamrat al-ʿAqabah — on the day of naḥr, riding.
items.ma-2057: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān, from ʿAbd al-Karīm al-Jazarī, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Do not find fault with one who fasts while travelling, nor with one who breaks the fast; the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fasted while travelling and broke the fast.
items.ma-2058: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Isrāʾīl or another, from Jābir, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent to the people of a village four farsakhs away — or he said: two farsakhs — on the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ, and he commanded whoever had eaten not to eat the rest of his day, and whoever had not eaten to complete his fast.
items.ma-2059: Wakīʿ narrated to us; Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a man came as a Muslim in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then his wife came as a Muslim after him. He said: O Messenger of Allah, she had become Muslim with me. So the Prophet ﷺ returned her to him.
items.ma-2061: Wakīʿ narrated to us; Zamʿah ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Ibn ʿAbbās. And Salamah ibn Wahrām, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed on a carpet.
items.ma-2062: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿĀbis, he said: I said to Ibn ʿAbbās: Did you attend the ʿĪd with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? He said: Yes, and had it not been for my position with him, I would not have attended it because of my youth. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out and prayed at the house of Kathīr ibn al-Ṣalt two rakʿahs, then gave a khuṭbah; he did not mention adhān or iqāmah.
items.ma-2063: Wakīʿ narrated to us; Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Bakr ibn Abī al-Jahm ibn Ṣukhayr, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the prayer of fear at Dhū Qarad — a land of the lands of Banū Sulaym. The people formed two rows behind him: one row facing the enemy and one row behind him. He led the row next to him in one rakʿah, then these stepped back to the places of those, and those to the places of these, and he led them in another rakʿah.
items.ma-2064:
Wakīʿ narrated to us; Usāmah ibn Zayd narrated to us, he said: I asked Ṭāwūs about the subḥah while travelling — and al-Ḥasan ibn Muslim ibn Yannāq was sitting — and al-Ḥasan ibn Muslim said, while Ṭāwūs was listening: Ṭāwūs narrated to us from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made obligatory the prayer in residence and in travel. So as you pray in residence before it and after it, pray in travel before it and after it.
Wakīʿ once said: and pray it in travel.
items.ma-2065: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Isrāʾīl, from Jābir, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I was commanded with the two rakʿahs of Ḍuḥā and with the Witr, and it was not written.”
items.ma-2067: Wakīʿ narrated to us; Zamʿah ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Wahrām, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed through the valley of ʿUsfān when he made Ḥajj, he said: “O Abū Bakr, what valley is this?” He said: The valley of ʿUsfān. He said: “Hūd and Ṣāliḥ passed through it on red young camels, their halters of palm-fibre, their izārs ʿabāʾ and their ridāʾs nimār, making the talbiyah, performing Ḥajj to the Ancient House.”
items.ma-2068: Wakīʿ narrated to us; Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Yaḥyā ibn ʿUbayd, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that nabīdh used to be made for the Prophet ﷺ on the night of Thursday, and he would drink it on Thursday and Friday — he said: and I think he said: and Saturday — and when it was ʿAṣr time, if any of it remained, he would give it to the servants to drink, or he would command about it and it would be poured out.
items.ma-2069: Wakīʿ narrated to us; Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā al-Thaʿlabī, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever speaks about the Qurʾān without knowledge, let him take his seat in the Fire.”
items.ma-2070: Wakīʿ narrated to us; Sufyān narrated to us, from Ādam ibn Sulaymān, the mawlā of Khālid ibn Khālid, he said: I heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: When this verse was revealed: {If you show what is within yourselves or conceal it, Allah will hold you to account for it} [al-Baqarah: 284], he said: Something entered their hearts from it such as had not entered their hearts from anything. He said: So the Prophet ﷺ said: “Say: We have heard and we have obeyed and we have submitted.” So Allah cast īmān into their hearts, and Allah ﷿ revealed: {The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Rabb, and the believers; each one has believed in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers; we make no distinction between any of His messengers. And they said: We have heard and we have obeyed; Your forgiveness, our Rabb, and to You is the final return. Allah does not charge a soul except [with] its capacity; for it is what it has earned and against it is what it has earned. Our Rabb, do not hold us to account if we forget or err. Our Rabb, and do not lay upon us a burden as You laid it upon those before us. Our Rabb, and do not make us bear that for which we have no strength. And pardon us, and forgive us, and have mercy upon us. You are our Mawlā, so give us victory over the disbelieving people} [al-Baqarah: 285–286]. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: This Ādam is the father of Yaḥyā ibn Ādam.
items.ma-2071: Wakīʿ narrated to us; Zakariyyā ibn Isḥāq al-Makkī narrated to us, from Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣayfī, from Abū Maʿbad, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Muʿādh ibn Jabal to Yemen, he said: “You are coming to a people, the People of the Book. So call them to the testimony that there is no deity except Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah. If they obey you in that, then inform them that Allah ﷿ has made obligatory upon them five prayers in every day and night. If they obey in that, then inform them that Allah ﷿ has made obligatory upon them a ṣadaqah in their wealth, taken from their rich and returned to their poor. If they obey you in that, then beware of the choicest of their wealth, and fear the supplication of the wronged, for between it and Allah ﷿ there is no veil.”
items.ma-2072: Wakīʿ narrated to us; Sufyān narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed wuḍūʾ once, once.
items.ma-2073: Wakīʿ narrated to us; Ibn Abī Dhiʾb narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that when the Prophet ﷺ prostrated, the whiteness of his armpits could be seen.
items.ma-2074: Wakīʿ narrated to us; Ibn Sulaymān ibn al-Ghasīl narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ gave a khuṭbah to the people, and upon him was a greasy headband.
items.ma-2075: Wakīʿ narrated to us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿīd ibn Abī Hind narrated to me, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān, from his mother Fāṭimah bint Ḥusayn, from Ibn ʿAbbās. And Ṣafwān [said]: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿīd ibn Abī Hind informed us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān, from his mother, Fāṭimah bint Ḥusayn, that she heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Do not prolong looking at the lepers.”
items.ma-2076: Wakīʿ narrated to us; Hishām narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I would love it if the people reduced from a third to a quarter in the bequest, because the Prophet ﷺ said: “The third is a lot, or: large.”
items.ma-2077: Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us; Fiṭr narrated to us, from ʿĀmir ibn Wāthilah, he said: I said to Ibn ʿAbbās: Your people claim that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed the raml, and that it is a sunnah. He said: My people spoke truly and they lied. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed the raml, and it is not a sunnah, but he came while the polytheists were on the mountain of Quʿayqiʿān, and they were saying that in him and his companions there was weakness, hardship and severity, so he commanded them, and they performed the raml at the House, to show them that no hardship had befallen them.
items.ma-2078: Wakīʿ narrated to us; Ibn Dharr narrated to us, from his father, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Jibrīl ﵇: “Will you not visit us more than you visit us?” So there was revealed: {And we do not descend except by the command of your Rabb; to Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us} to the end of the verse.
items.ma-2079: Wakīʿ narrated to us; Sufyān narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Laylā, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ offered, among his sacrificial camels, a camel that had belonged to Abū Jahl, its nose-ring being of silver.
items.ma-2080: Wakīʿ narrated to us; Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Jābir, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a cheese was brought to the Prophet ﷺ. He said: So his companions began striking it with sticks, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Put down the knife, mention the name of Allah, and eat.”
items.ma-2081: Wakīʿ narrated to us; Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Jābir, from Abū Jaʿfar and ʿAṭāʾ, they said: The aḍḥā is a sunnah. And ʿIkrimah said, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I was commanded with the aḍḥā and the Witr, and it was not written.”
items.ma-2082: Wakīʿ narrated to us; Sufyān and Misʿar narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from al-Ḥasan al-ʿUranī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent us ahead, the young boys of Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, on donkeys of ours from Jamʿ — Sufyān said: by night — and he began patting our thighs and saying: “My little sons, do not throw the jamrah until the sun rises.” And Sufyān added: Ibn ʿAbbās said: I do not think anyone with understanding throws until the sun rises.
items.ma-2083: Wakīʿ narrated to us; Sufyān narrated to us, he said: Salamah ibn Kuhayl narrated to us, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ got up at night, relieved himself, then washed his face and his hands, then came and slept.
items.ma-2084: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ slept until he snored, then got up and prayed and did not perform wuḍūʾ.
items.ma-2085: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Salamah, from al-Ḥasan — meaning al-ʿUranī — he said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: We do not know whether the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite in the Ẓuhr and the ʿAṣr; but we recite.
items.ma-2086: Wakīʿ narrated to us; Ḥammād ibn Najīḥ narrated to us, he heard it from Abū Rajāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I looked into Paradise and saw that most of its people were the poor, and I looked into the Fire and saw that most of its people were women.”
items.ma-2087: Wakīʿ narrated to us; Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, he said: I heard Ibn ʿUmar say: We used to practise mukhābarah and saw nothing wrong in it, until Rāfiʿ ibn Khadīj claimed that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had forbidden it. ʿAmr said: I mentioned it to Ṭāwūs, and Ṭāwūs said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only said: “That one of you grant his brother the land is better for him than that he take for it a known kharāj.”
items.ma-2088: Wakīʿ narrated to us; Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: When the prohibition of wine was revealed, they said: O Messenger of Allah, what of our brothers who died while they were drinking it? So there was revealed: {There is no blame upon those who have believed and done righteous deeds for what they have eaten} to the end of the verse [al-Māʾidah: 93].
items.ma-2089: Wakīʿ narrated to us; Sufyān narrated to us, from Salamah, from al-Ḥasan al-ʿUranī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent us ahead, the young boys of Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, from Jamʿ by night, on donkeys of ours, and he began patting our thighs and saying: “My little sons, do not throw the jamrah until the sun rises.”
items.ma-2090: Wakīʿ narrated to us; Sufyān narrated to us, from Salamah, from al-Ḥasan al-ʿUranī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When you have thrown the jamrah, everything has become lawful for you except women.” A man said: And perfume? Ibn ʿAbbās said: As for me, I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ smearing his head with sukk; is that perfume or not?!
items.ma-2091: Wakīʿ narrated to us; Sufyān narrated to us, from Jābir, from ʿĀmir, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ had himself cupped at the two neck veins and between the two shoulders.
items.ma-2092: Wakīʿ narrated to us; Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Jahḍam, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade us to let a donkey mount a horse.
items.ma-2093: Wakīʿ narrated to us; Sharīk narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: A caravan came to Madinah, and the Prophet ﷺ bought from it and made a profit of ūqiyyahs, and he divided it among the widows of Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib and said: “I will not buy anything whose price I do not have.”
items.ma-2094: Wakīʿ narrated to us; Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Karīm al-Jazarī, from Qays ibn Ḥabtar, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the mahr of a prostitute, the price of a dog, and the price of wine.
items.ma-2095: Wakīʿ narrated to us; Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Yaḥyā ibn al-Jazzār, from Ṣuhayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ was praying, and two girls of Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib came until they took hold of his knees, and he separated between the two.
items.ma-2096: Wakīʿ and Ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, the meaning being one, they said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Mughīrah ibn al-Nuʿmān, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood among us with an admonition and said: “You will be gathered to Allah barefoot, naked, uncircumcised, {as We began the first creation, We shall repeat it — a promise upon Us; indeed, We are doers}. And the first of creation to be clothed will be Ibrāhīm, the Khalīl of al-Raḥmān ﷿.” He said: “Then some of you will be taken to the left — Ibn Jaʿfar said: and men from my ummah will be brought, and they will be taken to the left — and I will say: O Rabb, my companions. He said: And it will be said to me: You do not know what they innovated after you; they have not ceased to be turning back on their heels since you left them. So I will say as the righteous slave said: {And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them} — the verse — up to: {Indeed, You are al-ʿAzīz, al-Ḥakīm} [al-Māʾidah: 117].”
items.ma-2097: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Manṣūr, from Dharr ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Hamdānī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaddād, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, I tell myself something such that to fall from the sky is more beloved to me than to speak of it. He said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Allāhu Akbar, Allāhu Akbar, Allāhu Akbar. Praise is for Allah, who has returned his scheme to whispering.”
items.ma-2098: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When you disagree about the road, make it seven cubits; and whoever builds a building, let him support it with the wall of his neighbour.”
items.ma-2099: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from al-Masʿūdī, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that when the Prophet ﷺ set off from ʿArafah, a people hurried, and he said — or they were called —: Righteousness is not in the hastening of horses, nor of mounts.” He said: “So I did not see any [mount] raising its foreleg, running, until we came to Jamʿ.”
items.ma-2100: Wakīʿ narrated to us; Sufyān narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Water is not made impure by anything.”
items.ma-2101: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that one of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ bathed from janābah, and the Prophet ﷺ bathed — or performed wuḍūʾ — from what remained of her [water].
items.ma-2102: ʿAlī ibn Isḥāq narrated to us; ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us; Sufyān informed us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that one of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ bathed from janābah, and the Prophet ﷺ performed wuḍūʾ with what remained of it. She mentioned that to him, and he said: “Indeed water is not made impure by anything.”
items.ma-2103: ʿAmr ibn Muḥammad Abū Saʿīd al-ʿAnqazī narrated to us; Sufyān informed us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from ʿImrān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forsook his wives for a month. When twenty-nine had passed, Jibrīl came to him and said: Your oath has been fulfilled, and the month is complete.”
items.ma-2104: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Fiṭr. And Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd said: Fiṭr narrated to us, from Shuraḥbīl Abū Saʿd, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Whoever has two sisters and treats them well for as long as they are in his company, he will enter Paradise by them.” And Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd said: “Two daughters reach maturity for him, and he does good to them for as long as they are in his company, except that Allah Taʿālā admits him to Paradise.”
items.ma-2105: Bishr ibn al-Sarī narrated to us; Sufyān narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never fought a people except that he called them first.
items.ma-2106: Yazīd ibn Hārūn narrated to us; Ibn Abī Dhiʾb informed us. And Rawḥ said: Ibn Abī Dhiʾb narrated to us, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbbās, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmayr — the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās — from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “If I live — Rawḥ said: if I remain safe — until next year, I will surely fast the ninth day,” meaning ʿĀshūrāʾ.
items.ma-2107: Yazīd narrated to me, he said: Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq informed us, from Dāwūd ibn al-Ḥuṣayn, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: It was said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: Which of the religions is most beloved to Allah? He said: “The tolerant Ḥanīfiyyah.”
items.ma-2108: Yazīd narrated to us; Hishām informed us. And Ibn Jaʿfar said: Hishām narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had himself cupped while in iḥrām, a cupping on his head; Yazīd said: because of an ailment that he had.
items.ma-2109: Yazīd narrated to us; Hishām informed us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ was taken while his coat of mail was pledged with a man of the Jews for thirty ṣāʿs of barley, which he had taken as provision for his dependants.
items.ma-2110: Yazīd narrated to us, he said: Hishām informed us. And Ibn Jaʿfar said: Hishām narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sent — or the Qurʾān was revealed to him — when he was forty years old, and he stayed in Makkah thirteen years and in Madinah ten years. He said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died when he was sixty-three.
items.ma-2111: Yazīd narrated to us; Ḥajjāj informed us, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to free any of the slaves who came to him ahead of their masters, if they became Muslim, and on the day of al-Ṭāʾif he freed two men.
items.ma-2112: Yazīd narrated to us; Sufyān informed us; and Yaʿlā [said]: Sufyān narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from al-Minhāl, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to seek refuge for Ḥasan and Ḥusayn, saying: “I seek refuge for you both in Kalimāt Allāh al-tāmmah, from every devil and every venomous creature, and from every harmful eye.” And he used to say: “Ibrāhīm, my father, used to seek refuge by them for Ismāʿīl and Isḥāq.”
items.ma-2113: Yazīd narrated to us; Sufyān ibn Ḥusayn informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: A man saw a dream, and he came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: I saw as if a canopy were dripping honey and ghee, and the people were taking from it, some taking much, some taking little, and some in between. And as if a rope were connected to the sky — and Yazīd once said: as if a rope were let down from the sky — and you came and took hold of it and ascended, and Allah raised you high. Then a man came after you and took hold of it and ascended, and Allah raised him high. Then a man came after you two and took hold of it and ascended, and Allah raised him high. Then a man came after you all and took hold of it, and it was cut for him, then it was joined for him, and he ascended, and Allah raised him high. Abū Bakr said: Permit me, O Messenger of Allah, and I will interpret it. So he permitted him, and he said: As for the canopy: it is Islām. As for the honey and the ghee: it is the sweetness of the Qurʾān, some taking much, some taking little, and some in between. As for the rope: it is what you are upon; you ascend and Allah raises you high. Then after you there will be a man upon your path, who will ascend and Allah will raise him high. Then after you two there will be a man who will take as you two took, and he will ascend and Allah will raise him high. Then after you all there will be a man for whom it will be cut, then it will be joined for him, and he will ascend and Allah will raise him high. He said: Have I been right, O Messenger of Allah? He said: “You have been right, and you have erred.” He said: I swear, O Messenger of Allah, that you will tell me. He said: “Do not swear.”
items.ma-2114: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us; Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ … and he mentioned its meaning.
items.ma-2115: Yazīd narrated to us; Shuʿbah informed us. And Muḥammad said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “This is an ʿumrah by which we have enjoyed [the benefit]. So whoever does not have a hady with him, let him leave iḥrām completely. For the ʿumrah has entered into the Ḥajj until the Day of Resurrection.”
items.ma-2116: Yazīd narrated to us; Ibn Abī Dhiʾb informed us, from Saʿīd ibn Khālid, from Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Dhuʾayb, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to them while they were sitting and said: “Shall I not tell you of the best of people in station?” They said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah. He said: “A man holding the head of his horse in the way of Allah until he dies or is killed. Shall I inform you of the one who is next to him?” They said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah. He said: “A man secluded in a mountain pass, establishing the prayer, giving zakāh, and keeping away from the evils of people.
