Shall I inform you of the worst of people in station?” They said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah. He said: “The one who is asked by [the name of] Allah and does not give by it.”
items.ma-2117: Yazīd narrated to us; Misʿar ibn Kidām informed us, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd, from his brother, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning the hides of carrion, he said: “Indeed its tanning has removed its filth, or its foulness, or its impurity.”
items.ma-2118: Yazīd narrated to us; Ḥajjāj informed us, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ: that he circumambulated the House on his she-camel, touching the Stone with his crook, and [between] al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah. And Yazīd once said: on his mount, touching the Stone.
items.ma-2119: Yazīd narrated to us, Ḥusayn ibn Dhakwān informed us, from ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from Ṭāwūs, that Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn ʿAbbās raised it to the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “It is not lawful for a man to give a gift and then take it back, except the father in what he gives his child. The likeness of the one who gives a gift and then takes it back is like the likeness of the dog: it ate until, when it was full, it vomited, and then returned to its vomit.”
items.ma-2120: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Ḥusayn al-Muʿallim narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said … and he mentioned the like of it.
items.ma-2121: Yazīd narrated to me, Saʿīd informed us, from Qatādah, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded the one who comes to his wife while she is menstruating to give ṣadaqah of a dīnār, or half a dīnār.
items.ma-2122: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb narrated to us, from Saʿīd, from Qatādah, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, the like of it. And ʿAbd al-Karīm Abū Umayyah narrated it, the like of it, with its isnād.
items.ma-2123: Yazīd narrated to me, Hishām informed us, from Yaḥyā, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ cursed the effeminate among men and the women who act like men, and said: “Remove them from your houses.” So the Prophet ﷺ removed so-and-so, and ʿUmar removed so-and-so.
items.ma-2124: Yazīd narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah informed us, Bukayr ibn al-Akhnas narrated to us, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that Allah ﷿ made the prayer obligatory upon the tongue of your Prophet: four [rakʿahs] upon the resident, two rakʿahs upon the traveller, and one rakʿah upon the one in fear.
items.ma-2125: Yazīd – meaning Ibn Hārūn – narrated to me, Sharīk ibn ʿAbd Allāh informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Tamīmī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I was commanded to use the tooth-stick, until I thought – or I reckoned – that a Qurʾān would be revealed to me about it.”
items.ma-2126: Yazīd narrated to us, Hammām ibn Yaḥyā informed us, ʿAṭāʾ narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the Kaʿbah, and in it were six pillars, and he stood by each pillar and did not pray.
items.ma-2127: Yazīd narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah informed us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from Yūsuf ibn Mihrān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: When ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn died, a woman said: “Enjoy Paradise, ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn.” So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked at her with the look of an angry man and said: “And what makes you know?” She said: “O Messenger of Allah, your horseman and your companion.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “By Allah, I am the Messenger of Allah, and I do not know what will be done with me.” So the people feared for ʿUthmān. Then when Zaynab, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, died, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Join our good predecessor, ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn.” Then the women wept, and ʿUmar began to strike them with his whip, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took hold of his hand and said: “Gently, O ʿUmar.” Then he said: “Weep, but beware of the shrieking of Satan.” Then he said: “Whatever comes from the eye and the heart is from Allah and from mercy, and whatever comes from the hand and the tongue is from Satan.”
items.ma-2128: Yazīd narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Zayd informed us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed Dhū al-Ḥulayfah as the mīqāt for the people of Madinah, al-Juḥfah for the people of al-Shām, Yalamlam for the people of Yemen, and Qarn for the people of Najd, and he said: “They are a mīqāt for their own people and for whoever passes by them who is not of their people – he intends Ḥajj and ʿumrah. Whoever's home is beyond the mīqāt, his ihlāl is from where he begins, and likewise, and likewise, even the people of Makkah: their ihlāl is from where they begin.”
items.ma-2129: Yazīd narrated to us, Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim informed us, from Yaʿlā ibn Ḥakīm, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Māʿiz ibn Mālik, when he came to him and confessed to him of zinā: “Perhaps you kissed or touched?” He said: “No.” He said: “Then did you have intercourse with her?” He said: “Yes.” So he gave the order concerning him, and he was stoned.
items.ma-2130: Yazīd narrated to us, Ṣāliḥ ibn Rustum Abū ʿĀmir narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Mulaykah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Ṣubḥ prayer was established, and a man stood up praying the two rakʿahs, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pulled him by his garment and said: “Do you pray Ṣubḥ as four?!”
items.ma-2131:
Yazīd narrated to us, ʿAbbād ibn Manṣūr informed us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: When it was revealed: {And those who accuse chaste women, then do not bring four witnesses, flog them eighty lashes and do not accept any testimony from them ever} [al-Nūr: 4], Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah – and he was the chief of the Anṣār – said: “Was it revealed like this, O Messenger of Allah?” So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “O company of the Anṣār, do you not hear what your chief is saying?” They said: “O Messenger of Allah, do not blame him, for he is a man of great protective jealousy. By Allah, he never married a woman except a virgin, and he never divorced a woman of his, so none of us dared to marry her, because of the intensity of his jealousy.” Then Saʿd said: “By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I know that it is the truth and that it is from Allah, but I am amazed that if I were to find a vile creature with a man lying between her thighs, I would not be permitted to provoke him or stir him until I bring four witnesses. By Allah, I would not bring them until he has fulfilled his need.”
He said: They stayed only a short while, until Hilāl ibn Umayyah came – and he was one of the three whose repentance was accepted – and he came from his land in the evening and found a man with his wife, so he saw with his eyes and heard with his ears, but he did not provoke him until the morning came. Then he went early to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: “O Messenger of Allah, I came to my wife in the evening and found a man with her, and I saw with my eyes and heard with my ears.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked what he had brought, and it weighed heavily upon him, and the Anṣār gathered and said: “We have been tried by what Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah said. Now the Messenger of Allah ﷺ will strike Hilāl ibn Umayyah and invalidate his testimony among the Muslims.” Then Hilāl said: “By Allah, I hope that Allah will make a way out for me from it.” And Hilāl said: “O Messenger of Allah, I see how heavily what I have brought weighs upon you, and Allah knows that I am truthful.”
By Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was about to command that he be struck, when revelation came down upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ – and when revelation came down upon him they would recognise it by the darkening of his skin, meaning – so they held back from him until he had finished with the revelation, and there was revealed: {And those who accuse their spouses and have no witnesses except themselves, then the testimony of one of them [is]} [al-Nūr: 6], the entire verse. Then it was lifted from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: “Receive glad tidings, O Hilāl, for Allah has made for you relief and a way out.” Hilāl said: “I had been hoping for that from my Rabb ﷿.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Send for her.” So they sent for her, and she came, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited it to them both, and reminded them, and informed them that the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe than the punishment of this world. Hilāl said: “By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I have told the truth about her.” She said: “He has lied.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Let them invoke curses between them.” So Hilāl was told: “Testify.” So he testified four testimonies by Allah that he was of the truthful. Then when it came to the fifth, it was said: “O Hilāl, fear Allah, for the punishment of this world is lighter than the punishment of the Hereafter, and this is the decisive one that makes the punishment obligatory upon you.” He said: “No, by Allah, Allah will not punish me for it, just as He did not flog me for it.” So he testified the fifth time: that the curse of Allah be upon him if he was of the liars. Then it was said to her: “Testify four testimonies by Allah that he is of the liars.” Then when it came to the fifth, it was said to her: “Fear Allah, for the punishment of this world is lighter than the punishment of the Hereafter, and this is the decisive one that makes the punishment obligatory upon you.” She hesitated for a while, then said: “By Allah, I will not disgrace my people.” So she testified the fifth time: that Ghaḍab Allāh ʿalayhā if he was of the truthful. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ separated them, and decreed that her child not be called to a father, and that neither she nor her child be accused because of him, and whoever accuses her or accuses her child, the ḥadd is upon him. And he decreed that she has no house from him and no sustenance, because they separate without divorce and without her being widowed. And he said: “If she brings him forth reddish-fair, thin-buttocked, slender-shanked, then he is Hilāl's; and if she brings him forth dusky-brown, curly-haired, big-boned like a camel, thick-calved, full in the buttocks, then he is for the one she was accused with.” Then she brought him forth dusky-brown, curly-haired, big-boned like a camel, thick-calved, full in the buttocks. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Were it not for the oaths, I would have had a matter to deal with concerning her.”
ʿIkrimah said: “Afterwards he became a governor over Egypt, and he used to be called to his mother, and was not called to a father.”
items.ma-2132: Yazīd narrated to us, Hishām al-Dastuwāʾī informed us, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from Abū Sallām, from al-Ḥakam ibn Mīnāʾ, from Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn ʿAbbās: that they both bore witness against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said, while he was upon the planks of the minbar: “Peoples will surely cease their abandoning of the Friday [prayers], or Allah ﷿ will surely seal upon their hearts, and they will surely be written among the heedless.”
items.ma-2133: Yazīd narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah informed us, from Farqad al-Sabakhī, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a woman came with her child to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: “O Messenger of Allah, he has a touch of madness, and it seizes him at our meal, and spoils our meal for us.” He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wiped his chest and supplicated for him, and he vomited once, and there came out from his mouth something like a black puppy, and he was healed.
items.ma-2134: Bahz narrated to us, Hammām informed us, Qatādah narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir asked the Prophet ﷺ and said that his sister had vowed to walk to the House, and he complained to him of her weakness. So the Prophet ﷺ said: “Indeed Allah is free of need of your sister's vow. Let her ride, and let her offer a camel.”
items.ma-2135: Muʿādh ibn Muʿādh narrated to us, Ḥājib ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, my uncle al-Ḥakam ibn al-Aʿraj narrated to me, who said: I came to Ibn ʿAbbās while he was reclining by Zamzam, so I sat with him, and he was a good companion. I said: “Inform me about the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ.” He said: “About which aspect of it do you ask?” I said: “About its fast: which day should I fast?” He said: “When you see the crescent of Muḥarram, then count, and when you wake up on the ninth, wake up fasting from it.” I said: “Was it thus that Muḥammad ﷺ used to fast it?” He said: “Yes.”
items.ma-2136: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, who said: I heard Layth say: I heard Ṭāwūs narrating from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “Teach, and make things easy, and do not make things difficult, and when one of you becomes angry, let him be silent.”
items.ma-2137: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Yazīd Abū Khālid, who said: I heard al-Minhāl ibn ʿAmr narrating, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “There is no Muslim servant who visits a sick person whose appointed time has not arrived, and says seven times: I ask Allah the Great, Rabb of the Great Throne, to cure you, except that he is granted well-being.”
items.ma-2138: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from al-Minhāl ibn ʿAmr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith, from Ibn ʿAbbās – Abū Muʿāwiyah said: I think he raised it – he said: “Whoever visits a sick person and says, I ask Allah the Great, Rabb of the Great Throne, to cure you, seven times, Allah will cure him, if he has been delayed” meaning in his appointed time. ʿAbd Allāh said: My father said: And Yazīd narrated it to us without doubting its being raised, and he agreed with him on the isnād.
items.ma-2139: Yazīd narrated to us, Hammām informed us, from Qatādah, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir came to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned that his sister had vowed to walk to the House. He said: “Command your sister to ride, and let her offer a camel.”
items.ma-2140: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Bishr, who said: I heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrating, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a woman vowed to perform Ḥajj, and she died, so her brother came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked him about that. He said: “Do you see: if your sister had a debt, would you have paid it?” He said: “Yes.” He said: “Then pay what is due to Allah ﷿, for He is more deserving of fulfilment.”
items.ma-2141: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar and Rawḥ narrated to us, both said: Shuʿbah narrated to us; Rawḥ said: I heard Muslim al-Qurrī; Muḥammad said: from Muslim al-Qurrī, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ assumed ihlāl for ʿumrah, and his Companions assumed ihlāl for Ḥajj – Rawḥ said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions assumed ihlāl for Ḥajj – and whoever had no hady with him left iḥrām. Among those who had no hady with him were Ṭalḥah and another man, and the two left iḥrām.
items.ma-2142: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, who said: I heard Yaḥyā ibn al-Mujabbir al-Taymī narrating, from Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that a man came to him and said: "Do you see a man who killed a man deliberately?" He recited: {His recompense is Jahannam, abiding therein, and Ghaḍiba Allāh ʿalayhi and has cursed him and has prepared for him a great punishment} [al-Nisāʾ: 93]. He said: "It was revealed among the last of what was revealed; nothing abrogated it until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taken, and no revelation came down after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He said: "Do you see if he repented and believed and did righteous deeds, then was guided?" He said: "And how can he have repentance, when I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "May his mother be bereaved of him: a man who killed a man deliberately comes on the Day of Resurrection taking hold of his killer with his right hand, or with his left, and taking hold of his own head with his right hand, or with his left, his jugular veins gushing blood in front of the Throne, saying: O Rabb, ask Your servant why he killed me?"
items.ma-2143: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Yaḥyā Abū ʿUmar, who said: They mentioned nabīdh in the presence of Ibn ʿAbbās, and he said: Nabīdh used to be prepared for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the waterskin – Shuʿbah said: like the night of Monday – and he would drink it on Monday and on Tuesday until ʿAṣr; and if anything remained of it, he would give it to the servants to drink, or pour it out. Shuʿbah said: And I think he said: and on Wednesday until ʿAṣr; and if anything remained of it, he would give it to the servants to drink, or pour it out.
items.ma-2144: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAdī ibn Thābit and ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās – he said: One of them raised it to the Prophet ﷺ – he said: “Indeed Jibrīl used to thrust clay into the mouth of Pharaoh, fearing that he would say: There is no deity except Allah.”
items.ma-2145: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “In a salaf for the ḥabal al-ḥabalah there is ribā.”
items.ma-2146: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Ḥabīb – meaning Ibn al-Shahīd – from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Mulaykah, who said: I was present with Ibn al-Zubayr and Ibn ʿAbbās, and Ibn al-Zubayr said to Ibn ʿAbbās: “Do you remember when we met the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, as he had come from a journey?” He said: “Yes, and he carried me and so-and-so – a boy from Banū Hāshim – and left you.”
items.ma-2147: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “A man will enter upon you who looks with the eye of a Satan, or with the two eyes of a Satan.” He said: Then a blue-eyed man entered and said: “O Muḥammad, for what did you revile me – or insult me, or something like this?” He said: And he began to swear. He said: Then this verse was revealed in al-Mujādilah: {And they swear upon the lie while they know} [al-Mujādilah: 14], and the other verse.
items.ma-2148:
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said about the Dajjāl: “One-eyed, pure white, radiant, as though his head were an aṣalah, the most similar of people to ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn Qaṭan. And if the doomed ones perish, indeed your Rabb is not one-eyed.”
Shuʿbah said: I narrated it to Qatādah, and he narrated to me something like this.
items.ma-2149: Muʿādh ibn Hishām narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from Qatādah, from ʿIkrimah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās: that a man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: “O Prophet of Allah, I am a very old man, ailing; standing is hard for me, so command me [to a particular] night, that perhaps Allah may grant me success in it to [find] Laylat al-Qadr.” He said: “Hold to the seventh.”
items.ma-2150: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Ḥamzah: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by me while I was playing with the boys, so I hid from him behind a door, and he called me and patted me with a pat, then sent me to Muʿāwiyah.
items.ma-2151: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to me, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Bishr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to fast until we said: He does not intend to break his fast; and he would break his fast until we said: He does not intend to fast. And he did not fast a month consecutively other than Ramaḍān since he came to Madinah.
items.ma-2152: Hushaym narrated to us, Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād informed us, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: The Prophet ﷺ assumed ihlāl for Ḥajj, and when he arrived he performed ṭawāf of the House and between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, and he did not shorten [his hair], and he did not leave iḥrām because of the hady; and he commanded whoever had not driven the hady to perform ṭawāf, and to perform saʿy, and to shorten or shave, and then to leave iḥrām.
items.ma-2153: Hushaym narrated to us, Jābir al-Juʿfī informed us, Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by a pot, and took from it a bone with some meat, or a shoulder, and ate it, then prayed and did not perform wuḍūʾ.
items.ma-2154: Hushaym narrated to us, Ibn Abī Laylā informed us, from Dāwūd ibn ʿAlī, from his father, from his grandfather Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Fast the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ, and differ in it from the Jews: fast a day before it, or a day after it.”
items.ma-2155: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Jābir, from al-Shaʿbī, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he had himself cupped, would be cupped at the two akhdaʿ [veins]. He said: So he called a boy belonging to Banū Bayāḍah and he cupped him, and he gave the cupper his wage, a mudd and a half. He said: And he spoke to his mawālī, and they reduced half a mudd from him, and it had been two mudds upon him.
items.ma-2156: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Jābir, who said: I heard al-Shaʿbī narrating from Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn ʿAbbās, both of them said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laid down the prayer in travel as two rakʿahs, and it is complete, and the Witr in travel is a sunnah.
items.ma-2157: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Jābir, from ʿAmmār, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “Whoever builds a mosque for Allah, even if like the scraped hollow of a sandgrouse for its eggs, Allah will build for him a house in Paradise.”
items.ma-2158: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar and Ḥajjāj narrated to us, both said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, who said: I heard Abū Jamrah al-Ḍubaʿī say: I performed tamattuʿ, and some people forbade me from that, so I came to Ibn ʿAbbās and asked him about that, and he commanded me to do it. He said: Then I went to the House and slept, and a comer came to me in my sleep and said: “An accepted ʿumrah and a righteous Ḥajj.” He said: So I came to Ibn ʿAbbās and informed him of what I had seen, and he said: “Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest; the sunnah of Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ.” And he said: “For the hady: a camel, or a cow, or a sheep, or a share in a blood [sacrifice].” ʿAbd Allāh said: Shuʿbah did not transmit with an isnād from Abū Jamrah except one [ḥadīth], and Abū Jamrah is more reliable than Abū Ḥamzah.
items.ma-2159: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Safar, from Saʿīd ibn Shufayy, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The people began asking him about the prayer in travel, and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he went out from his family, would pray only two rakʿahs until he returned to his family.
items.ma-2160: Aswad narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Saʿīd ibn Shufayy, who said: I was with Ibn ʿAbbās … and he mentioned the ḥadīth.
items.ma-2161: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the mujaththamah and the jallālah, and drinking from the mouth of the waterskin.
items.ma-2162: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Saʿīd narrated to us, from al-Naḍr ibn Anas, who said: I was with Ibn ʿAbbās while he was giving rulings to the people, not attributing any of his rulings to the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, until a man from the people of Iraq came to him and said: “I am a man from the people of Iraq, and I make these images.” Ibn ʿAbbās said to him: “Come near” – either twice or three times – so he came near. Ibn ʿAbbās said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever makes an image in the world will be charged on the Day of Resurrection with blowing the spirit into it, and he will not be able to blow.”
items.ma-2163: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, from Mālik, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Faḍl, from Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The ayyim has more right over herself than her guardian, and the virgin is asked permission concerning herself, and her permission is her silence.”
items.ma-2164: I read to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān: from Mālik, from Makhramah ibn Sulaymān, from Kurayb the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās, that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās informed him: that he spent the night at the house of Maymūnah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, and she was his maternal aunt. He said: I lay down along the width of the pillow, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his wife lay along its length. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ slept, until when the night was halved, or a little before it, or a little after it, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ woke up and sat, wiping the sleep from his face with his hand. Then he recited the ten verses, the endings of Sūrat Āl ʿImrān. Then he stood to a hanging waterskin and performed wuḍūʾ from it, and made his wuḍūʾ good. Then he stood praying. Ibn ʿAbbās said: So I stood and did the like of what he had done, then I went and stood at his side, and he placed his right hand on my head and took my right ear and twisted it. Then he prayed two rakʿahs, then two rakʿahs, then two rakʿahs, then two rakʿahs, then two rakʿahs, then two rakʿahs, then he prayed Witr. Then he lay down until the muʾadhdhin came to him, and he stood and prayed two light rakʿahs, then went out and prayed Ṣubḥ.
items.ma-2165: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from ʿAmmār ibn Abī ʿAmmār, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: I saw the Prophet ﷺ in a dream at midday, dishevelled and dust-covered, with a bottle in which was blood, which he was gathering – or he was following something in it. He said: I said: “O Messenger of Allah, what is this?” He said: “The blood of al-Ḥusayn and his companions; I have not ceased following it since today.” ʿAmmār said: So we memorised that day, and we found that he was killed on that day.
items.ma-2166: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from ʿImrān Abū al-Ḥakam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Quraysh said to the Prophet ﷺ: “Supplicate your Rabb for us to make al-Ṣafā gold for us, and we will believe in you.” He said: “And will you do it?” They said: “Yes.” He said: So he supplicated, and Jibrīl came to him and said: “Your Rabb recites the salām upon you, and says: If you wish, al-Ṣafā will become gold for them, and whoever among them disbelieves after that, I will punish him with a punishment with which I do not punish anyone among the worlds; and if you wish, I will open for them the door of repentance and mercy.” He said: “Rather the door of repentance and mercy.”
items.ma-2167: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Qatādah, who said: I heard Abū al-ʿĀliyah say: The cousin of your Prophet ﷺ narrated to me – meaning Ibn ʿAbbās – he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “It is not fitting for anyone to say: I am better than Yūnus ibn Mattā.” And he ascribed him to his father.
items.ma-2168: I read to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān: from Mālik, from Abū al-Zubayr al-Makkī, from Ṭāwūs al-Yamānī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to teach them the supplication as he taught them a sūrah of the Qurʾān, saying: “Say: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of Jahannam, and I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave, and I seek refuge in You from the trial of the Masīḥ al-Dajjāl, and I seek refuge in You from the trial of life and death.”
items.ma-2169: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd narrated to us, from Dāwūd – meaning Ibn Abī al-Furāt – from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ prayed with the people on the day of Fiṭr two rakʿahs without adhān or iqāmah, then delivered a sermon after the prayer, then took Bilāl by the hand and went to the women and addressed them. Then, after he had turned away from them, he commanded Bilāl to go to them and command them to give ṣadaqah.
items.ma-2170: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, my father narrated to us from his book: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Umawī narrated to us, he said: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Ṭāriq, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “O Allah, You made the first of Quraysh taste an exemplary punishment, so make the last of them taste a bounty.”
items.ma-2171: Muḥammad ibn Rabīʿah narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan ibn Muslim, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: I was present at the ʿĪd with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Abū Bakr, ʿUmar and ʿUthmān, and every one of them prayed before the sermon, without adhān or iqāmah.
items.ma-2172: Muḥammad ibn Rabīʿah narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Jābir, from the Prophet ﷺ, the like of that.
items.ma-2173: Muʾammal narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from al-Ḥasan ibn Muslim, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the ʿĪd, then delivered a sermon; and Abū Bakr prayed, then delivered a sermon; and ʿUmar, then delivered a sermon; and ʿUthmān, then delivered a sermon, without adhān or iqāmah.
items.ma-2174: al-Qāsim ibn Mālik Abū Jaʿfar narrated to us, from Ḥanẓalah al-Sadūsī, from Shahr ibn Ḥawshab, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the ʿĪd as two rakʿahs, reciting in them only Umm al-Kitāb, not adding anything to it.
items.ma-2175: Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥakīm narrated to us, al-Ḥakam – meaning Ibn Abān – narrated to us, who said: I heard ʿIkrimah say: Ibn ʿAbbās said: The ʿanazah was planted in front of the Prophet ﷺ at ʿArafāt, and he prayed toward it, while the donkey passed by behind the ʿanazah.
items.ma-2176: ʿAbd al-Quddūs ibn Bakr ibn Khunays narrated to us, al-Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ besieged the people of al-Ṭāʾif, and two slaves came out to him, and he freed them, one of them Abū Bakrah; and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to free slaves when they came out to him.
items.ma-2177: al-Qāsim ibn Mālik al-Muzanī Abū Jaʿfar narrated to us, from Ayyūb ibn ʿĀʾidh, from Bukayr ibn al-Akhnas, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Indeed Allah ﷿ made the prayer obligatory upon the tongue of your Prophet ﷺ: in residence four, in travel two rakʿahs, and in fear one rakʿah.
items.ma-2178: ʿAmmār ibn Muḥammad, the son of the sister of Sufyān al-Thawrī, narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Sālim, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Is one of you unable, when he comes to his wife, to say: In the name of Allah, O Allah, keep Satan away from me, and keep Satan away from what You provide for me? For if Allah decrees a child between the two of them in that, Satan will never harm him.”
items.ma-2179: ʿAlī ibn ʿĀṣim narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Saʿīd, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās said to me: “O Saʿīd, do you have a wife?” He said: I said: “No.” He said: “Then when you return, marry.” He said: So I returned to him, and he said: “O Saʿīd, have you married?” He said: I said: “No.” He said: “Marry, for the best of this ummah was the one with the most women.”
items.ma-2180: ʿAlī ibn ʿĀṣim narrated to us, Abū ʿAlī al-Raḥabī narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, Ibn ʿAbbās informed us, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ washed himself from janābah, and when he came out he saw a patch on his left shoulder that the water had not reached, so he took from his hair and wetted it, then went on to the prayer.
items.ma-2181: Abū al-Yamān narrated to us, Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh narrated to us, from Thaʿlabah ibn Muslim al-Khathʿamī, from Abū Kaʿb the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, that it was said to him: “O Messenger of Allah, Jibrīl ﵇ has been slow in coming to you.” He said: “And why should he not be slow in coming to me, when you are around me and you do not use the tooth-stick, nor trim your nails, nor clip your moustaches, nor clean your rawājib.”
items.ma-2182: Hāshim ibn al-Qāsim narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Khālid Yazīd, from al-Minhāl ibn ʿAmr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “Whoever comes to a sick person whose appointed time has not arrived, and says seven times: I ask Allah the Great, Rabb of the Great Throne, to cure him, except that he is granted well-being.”
items.ma-2183: Hāshim narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim, from al-Shaʿbī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Prophet ﷺ passed by me near Zamzam, and called for water and asked for a drink, so I brought him a bucket of Zamzam water, and he drank while standing.
items.ma-2184:
Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd al-Hāshimī narrated to us, Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd narrated to us, who said: Ṣāliḥ ibn Kaysān and the son of the brother of Ibn Shihāb narrated to me, both of them from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās. And Yaʿqūb said: My father narrated to us, from Ṣāliḥ: Ibn Shihāb said: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh informed me that Ibn ʿAbbās informed him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥudhāfah with his letter to Kisrā, and he handed it to the chief of al-Baḥrayn, [and] the chief of al-Baḥrayn was to hand it to Kisrā. Yaʿqūb said: So the chief of al-Baḥrayn handed it to Kisrā, and when he read it he tore it up.
Ibn Shihāb said: I think Ibn al-Musayyab said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ invoked against them that they be torn to pieces with every [kind of] tearing.
items.ma-2185: Hāshim narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ fasted on the day of the conquest of Makkah until he came to Qudayd, and a cup of milk was brought to him, and he broke his fast, and commanded the people to break their fast.
items.ma-2186: Hāshim narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was cupped at al-Qāḥah while he was fasting.
items.ma-2187: Ḥujayn ibn al-Muthannā and Yūnus narrated to us, both said: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz – meaning Ibn Abī Salamah – narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUqbah, from Kurayb the mawlā of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Prophet ﷺ passed by a woman who had a boy of hers with her in a miḥaffah, and she took hold of his upper arm and said: “O Prophet of Allah, does this one have Ḥajj?” He said: “Yes, and for you is a reward.”
items.ma-2188: Yūnus narrated to us, Ḥammād – meaning Ibn Zayd – narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn, that Ibn ʿAbbās narrated, saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gnawed the meat from a shoulder, then stood and prayed, and did not perform wuḍūʾ.
items.ma-2189:
Yūnus narrated to us, Ḥammād – meaning Ibn Zayd – narrated to us, from Abū al-Tayyāḥ, from Mūsā ibn Salamah, who said: Sinān ibn Salamah and I went out, and we had two camels with us, and they became too weak to go on, on the road. Sinān said to me: “Would you care to go to Ibn ʿAbbās?” So we went to him, and Sinān asked him … and he mentioned the ḥadīth.
He said: And Ibn ʿAbbās said: al-Juhanī asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: “O Messenger of Allah, my father is a very old man who has not performed Ḥajj?” He said: “Perform Ḥajj on behalf of your father.”
items.ma-2190: Yūnus narrated to us, Fulayḥ narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Waʿlah, who said: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās and said: “We are in a land of ours in which there are vineyards, and most of its yield is wine?” He said: A man from Daws came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with a rāwiyah of wine that he was presenting to him as a gift, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: “Did you know that Allah has forbidden it after you [left]?” So the owner of the rāwiyah turned to a person who was with him and commanded him, and the Prophet ﷺ said: “With what did you command him?” He said: “To sell it.” He said: “Did you know that the One Who forbade drinking it has forbidden selling it and eating its price?” He said: So he ordered the mazādah, and it was poured out.
items.ma-2191: Yūnus and Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us, the meaning, both said: Ḥammād – meaning Ibn Zayd – narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilābah, from Ibn ʿAbbās – I do not know it except that he raised it – he said: When he alighted at a stopping-place and the stopping-place pleased him, he would delay the Ẓuhr until he combined Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr; and when he travelled and no stopping-place was suitable for him, he would delay the Ẓuhr until he came to the stopping-place and combined Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr. Ḥasan said: When he travelled and alighted at a stopping-place.
items.ma-2192: Yūnus narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from Abū Bishr, from Maymūn ibn Mihrān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade every beast of prey that has a fang, and every bird that has a talon.
items.ma-2193: Yūnus narrated to us, Ḥammād – meaning Ibn Zayd – narrated to us, from Kathīr ibn Shinẓīr, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The beginning of the īḍāʿ was only from the side of the Bedouin: they used to stand at the two flanks of the people until they hung up sticks, quivers and wooden bowls, and when they set off in haste, those would rattle, and so they scattered the people. He said: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was seen with the dhifrā of his she-camel touching her withers, while he was saying with his hand: “O people, hold to tranquillity. O people, hold to tranquillity.”
items.ma-2194:
Yūnus narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Ḥumayd and Ayyūb, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ slept until snoring was heard from him, then stood and prayed, and did not perform wuḍūʾ.
ʿIkrimah said: The Prophet ﷺ was protected.
items.ma-2195: Yūnus and ʿAffān narrated to us, both said: Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Ayyūb – ʿAffān said: Ayyūb informed us – and Qays, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ delayed the ʿIshāʾ one night until the people slept, then they woke, then they slept, then they woke. Qays said: Then ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb came and said: “The prayer, O Messenger of Allah.” He said: So he went out and prayed with them, and he did not mention that they performed wuḍūʾ.
items.ma-2196: Yūnus and Ḥasan narrated to us, both said: Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Kurayb ibn Abī Muslim, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in the house of Maymūnah bint al-Ḥārith, and stood to pray at night. He said: So I stood on his left, and he took me by my hand and stood me on his right. Then he prayed, then slept until he breathed heavily; then Bilāl came to him with the adhān, so he stood and prayed and did not perform wuḍūʾ. Ḥasan said – meaning in his ḥadīth: I was with the Prophet ﷺ in the house of Maymūnah, and when he had completed his prayer he slept until he breathed heavily.
items.ma-2197: Yūnus narrated to us, Shaybān narrated to us, Qatādah narrated to us, from Abū al-ʿĀliyah: The cousin of your Prophet ﷺ, Ibn ʿAbbās, narrated to us, who said: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: “On the night I was taken by night, I saw Mūsā ibn ʿImrān, a tawny man, tall, curly-haired, as though he were of the men of Shanūʾah; and I saw ʿĪsā ibn Maryam of medium build, [inclining] to redness and whiteness, with lank hair.”
items.ma-2198: Ḥusayn narrated to us in the tafsīr of Shaybān, from Qatādah, who said: Abū al-ʿĀliyah narrated: The cousin of your Prophet, Ibn ʿAbbās, narrated to us, who said: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said … and he mentioned the like of it.
items.ma-2199: Muḥammad ibn Rabīʿah narrated to us, ʿAbbād ibn Manṣūr narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ decreed concerning the son of the woman who underwent liʿān that he not be called to a father, and that whoever accuses her, or accuses her child, is flogged the ḥadd; and he decreed that she has no sustenance from him and no lodging, because the two of them separate without divorce and without her being widowed.
items.ma-2200: Yūnus narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Ḥumayd, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ married Maymūnah bint al-Ḥārith while the two of them were in iḥrām.
items.ma-2201: Yūnus narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ al-ʿAṭṭār, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “He should give ṣadaqah of a dīnār, and if he does not find it, then half a dīnār” – meaning the one who approaches his wife while she is menstruating.
items.ma-2202: Yūnus narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from Simāk, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ met Māʿiz ibn Mālik and said: “Is what has reached me about you true?” He said: “And what has reached you about me?” He said: “It has reached me that you committed fornication with the slave-girl of the family of so-and-so?” He said: “Yes.” So he sent him back until he had testified four times, then ordered his stoning.
items.ma-2203: Yūnus narrated to us, Ḥammād – meaning Ibn Salamah – narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from Yūsuf ibn Mihrān, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that Jibrīl ﵇ said to the Prophet ﷺ: “If you had seen me while I was taking from the silt of the sea and thrusting it into the mouth of Pharaoh.”
items.ma-2204: Yūnus narrated to us, Ḥammād – meaning Ibn Zayd – narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me with the baggage from Jamʿ by night.
items.ma-2205: Yūnus narrated to us, from Ḥammād – meaning Ibn Salamah – from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from Yūsuf ibn Mihrān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Jibrīl ﵇ said to me: The prayer has been made beloved to you, so take of it what you wish.”
items.ma-2206: Yūnus and ʿAffān narrated to us, both said: Ḥammād – meaning Ibn Salamah – narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd – ʿAffān said: ʿAlī ibn Zayd informed us – from Yūsuf ibn Mihrān, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a man came to ʿUmar and said: “A woman came to do business with him, so I took her into the inner chamber, and I got from her what is short of intercourse.” He said: “Woe to you! Perhaps she is one [whose husband is] absent in the cause of Allah?” He said: “Yes.” He said: “Then go to Abū Bakr and ask him.” He said: So he came to him and asked him, and he said: “Perhaps she is one [whose husband is] absent in the cause of Allah?” He said: And he said the like of what ʿUmar said. Then he came to the Prophet ﷺ and said to him the like of that, and he said: “Perhaps she is one [whose husband is] absent in the cause of Allah?” And the Qurʾān was revealed: {And establish the prayer at the two ends of the day and at the nearer hours of the night. Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds} [Hūd: 114] to the end of the verse. He said: “O Messenger of Allah, is it for me in particular, or for the people in general?” So ʿUmar struck his chest with his hand and said: “No, and no delight of the eye; rather it is for the people in general.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “ʿUmar has spoken the truth.”
items.ma-2207: Yūnus narrated to us, Ḥammād – meaning Ibn Salamah – narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from Yūsuf ibn Mihrān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came with Usāmah ibn Zayd riding behind him, and we gave him to drink of this drink, and he said: “You have done well; do thus.”
items.ma-2208: Marwān ibn Shujāʿ narrated to us, he said: I do not remember him except as Sālim al-Afṭas al-Jazarī Ibn ʿAjlān; he narrated to me, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Healing is in three: a drink of honey, an incision of the cupping instrument, and a cauterisation with fire; and I forbid my ummah from cauterisation.”
items.ma-2209: Isḥāq ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us, Ibrāhīm – meaning Ibn Saʿd – narrated to me, from al-Zuhrī. [ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad said:] My father said: And Yaʿqūb: My father narrated to me, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The polytheists used to part their hair, and the People of the Book used to let it hang loose – Yaʿqūb said: their hair – and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ liked, and it pleased him, to conform with the People of the Book – Yaʿqūb said: in some of what he had not been commanded; Isḥāq said: in that concerning which he had not been commanded – so he let his forelock hang loose, then afterwards he parted it.
items.ma-2210: Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us, Abū Khaythamah narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Khuthaym, from Abū al-Ṭufayl, who said: I saw Muʿāwiyah performing ṭawāf of the House, with ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās on his left, and I was following the two of them at their backs, listening to their speech. Muʿāwiyah began to touch the corner of the Stone, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās said to him: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not touch these two corners.” Muʿāwiyah would say: “Leave me alone, O Ibn ʿAbbās, for none of it is abandoned.” Ibn ʿAbbās began to add nothing to it; whenever he placed his hand on either of the two corners, he said that to him.
items.ma-2211: Yūnus narrated to us, Dāwūd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Prophet ﷺ performed ʿumrah four times: an ʿumrah from al-Ḥudaybiyah, and the ʿumrah of al-Qaḍāʾ in Dhū al-Qaʿdah of the following year, and the third ʿumrah from al-Jiʿirrānah, and the fourth, which was with his Ḥajj.
items.ma-2212:
Ibrāhīm ibn Abī al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī al-Zinād narrated to us, from his father, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah ibn Masʿūd, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Allah ﷿ revealed: {And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, those are the disbelievers} [al-Māʾidah: 44], and {those are the wrongdoers}, and {those are the transgressors}. He said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: Allah revealed them concerning the two groups of the Jews; and one of them had overpowered the other in the Jāhiliyyah, until they agreed and made peace that for every slain man whom the mighty one killed of the humble one, the blood-money was fifty wasqs, and for every slain man whom the humble one killed of the mighty one, the blood-money was a hundred wasqs.
They remained so until the Prophet ﷺ came to Madinah, and both groups were humbled at the coming of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on that day had not yet become prevailing, and had not yet subdued them to himself, and he was in a [state of] truce. Then the humble one killed a slain man of the mighty one, so the mighty one sent to the humble one: “Send us a hundred wasqs.” The humble one said: “Has this ever been among two tribes whose religion is one, and whose lineage is one, and whose land is one, the blood-money of some of them being half the blood-money of others? We only gave you this because of your wronging us and out of fear of you; but now that Muḥammad has come, we will not give it to you.” War almost flared up between them, then they agreed to make the Messenger of Allah ﷺ [judge] between them. Then the mighty one reflected and said: “By Allah, Muḥammad will not give you from them twice what he gives them from you, and they have spoken the truth; they gave us this only out of wronging by us and overpowering of them. So slip to Muḥammad someone who will ascertain his opinion for you: if he gives you what you want, you will make him judge, and if he does not give you, you will beware and not make him judge.” So they slipped to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ some people from among the hypocrites, to ascertain for them the opinion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and when [they] came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Allah informed His Messenger of their whole affair and of what they wanted, and Allah ﷿ revealed: {O Messenger, let them not grieve you who hasten into disbelief, from those who said: We believe} up to His words: {And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, those are the transgressors} [al-Māʾidah: 41-47]. Then he said: “Concerning those two [groups], by Allah, it was revealed, and them Allah ﷿ meant.”
items.ma-2213: ʿAlī ibn ʿĀṣim narrated to us, Khālid informed us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever listens in on the speech of a people while they dislike it, molten lead will be poured into his ear; and whoever feigns a dream will be punished until he ties a grain of barley, and he will not be able to tie it; and whoever makes an image will be charged with blowing, and he will not be able to blow.”
items.ma-2214: ʿAlī ibn ʿĀṣim narrated to us, Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmr ibn Ghallāb informed us, from al-Ḥakam ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Aʿraj, who said: I was with Ibn ʿAbbās in the house of al-Siqāyah, and he was using a cloak of his as a pillow. He said: I said: “O Abū ʿAbbās, inform me about ʿĀshūrāʾ.” He said: “About which aspect of it?” He said: I said: “About fasting it.” He said: “When you sight the crescent of Muḥarram, count nine, then wake up on the ninth day fasting.” He said: I said: “Was it thus that Muḥammad ﷺ used to fast it?” He said: “Yes.”
items.ma-2215: ʿAlī ibn ʿĀṣim narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Khuthaym informed me, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “This Stone will come on the Day of Resurrection with two eyes with which it sees and a tongue with which it speaks, testifying for whoever touched it in truth.”
items.ma-2216: ʿAlī ibn ʿĀṣim narrated to us, Dāwūd narrated to us: ʿIkrimah narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: There were some of the captives on the day of Badr who had no ransom, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made their ransom that they teach the children of the Anṣār writing. He said: A boy came one day weeping to his father, and he said: “What is the matter with you?” He said: “My teacher struck me.” He said: “The vile one, seeking vengeance for Badr! By Allah, you will never go to him.”
items.ma-2217: ʿAlī ibn ʿĀṣim narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded, on the day of Uḥud, concerning the martyrs, that the iron and the hides be removed from them, and said: “Bury them in their blood and their garments.”
items.ma-2218: ʿAlī ibn ʿĀṣim narrated to us, from Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a man of the Anṣār apostatised from Islam and joined the polytheists, so Allah Taʿālā revealed: {How shall Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief} to the end of the verse [Āl ʿImrān: 86]. His people sent it to him, so he returned repenting, and the Prophet ﷺ accepted that from him and let him go.
items.ma-2219: ʿAlī narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Khuthaym informed us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Wear white among your garments, for it is among the best of your garments, and shroud your dead in it; and among the best of your kohls is ithmid, which clears the sight and makes the hair grow.”
items.ma-2220: ʿAlī ibn ʿĀṣim narrated to us, from al-Jurayrī, from Abū al-Ṭufayl; and from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Khuthaym, from Abū al-Ṭufayl, both of them from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did ramal for three rounds around the House; when he reached the Yamānī corner he walked until he came to the Stone, then did ramal again, and he walked four circuits. He said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: And it was a sunnah.
items.ma-2221: ʿAlī ibn ʿĀṣim narrated to us, al-Ḥadhdhāʾ informed us, from Barakah Abū al-Walīd, Ibn ʿAbbās informed us, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting in the mosque, facing al-Ḥujar. He said: He looked at the sky and laughed, then said: “May Allah curse the Jews: fats were forbidden to them and they sold them and ate their prices; and indeed Allah ﷿, when He forbids a people the eating of a thing, forbids them its price.”
items.ma-2222: ʿAlī ibn ʿĀṣim narrated to us, Abū al-Muʿallā al-ʿAṭṭār informed us, al-Ḥasan al-ʿUranī narrated to us, who said: It was mentioned in the presence of Ibn ʿAbbās that the dog, the donkey and the woman cut off the prayer. He said: “How evil is what you have done in equating a Muslim woman with a dog and a donkey! I have seen myself come on a donkey while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was praying with the people, until when I was near him, facing him, I dismounted from it and let it go, and entered with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ into his prayer. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not repeat his prayer, and he did not forbid me what I had done. And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was praying with the people, and a girl came passing through the rows until she took refuge with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not repeat his prayer, and he did not forbid her what she had done. And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was praying in a mosque, and a kid came out from one of the rooms of the Prophet ﷺ and went to pass in front of him, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prevented him.” Ibn ʿAbbās said: “Will you not say: the kid cuts off the prayer?!”
items.ma-2223: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maymūn Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Raqqī narrated to us, who said: al-Ḥasan – meaning Abū al-Malīḥ – informed us, from Ḥabīb – meaning Ibn Abī Marzūq – from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Whoever arrives performing Ḥajj and performs ṭawāf of the House and between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, his Ḥajj has ended and has become an ʿumrah; such is the sunnah of Allah ﷿ and the sunnah of His Messenger ﷺ.
items.ma-2224: Zayd ibn al-Ḥubāb narrated to us, Sayf informed us, Qays ibn Saʿd al-Makkī informed me, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave judgement on the basis of a witness and an oath.
items.ma-2225: Ismāʿīl ibn Yazīd al-Raqqī Abū Yazīd narrated to us, Furāt narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Karīm, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Abū Jahl said: “If I see the Messenger of Allah praying at the Kaʿbah, I will come to him until I tread upon his neck.” He said: Then he said: “If he had done so, the angels would have seized him in plain sight; and if the Jews had wished for death, they would have died and seen their seats in the Fire; and if those who were to invoke a mutual curse with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had gone out, they would have returned finding neither wealth nor family.”
items.ma-2226: Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Malik narrated to us, ʿUbayd Allāh narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Karīm, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Abū Jahl said … and he mentioned its meaning.
items.ma-2227: Naṣr ibn Bāb Abū Sahl narrated to us, in Shawwāl of the year one hundred and eighty-one, from al-Ḥajjāj, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed ṭawāf of the House and began to touch the Stone with his curved staff, then came to al-Siqāyah after he had finished, while the sons of his paternal uncle were drawing from it, and he said: “Hand it to me.” So the bucket was raised to him and he drank, then said: “Were it not that the people would take it as a nusuk and overcome you over it, I would draw with you.” Then he went out and performed ṭawāf between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah.
items.ma-2228: Naṣr ibn Bāb narrated to us, from al-Ḥajjāj, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was cupped while fasting and in iḥrām, and he fainted. He said: So for that reason he disliked cupping for the one who is fasting.
items.ma-2229:
Naṣr ibn Bāb narrated to us, from al-Ḥajjāj, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ freed, on the day of al-Ṭāʾif, those of the slaves who came out to him.
Naṣr ibn Bāb narrated to us, from al-Ḥajjāj, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on the day of al-Ṭāʾif: “Whoever of the slaves comes out to us is free.” So some slaves came out, among them Abū Bakrah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ freed them.
items.ma-2230: Naṣr ibn Bāb narrated to us, he said: al-Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: The Muslims killed a man of the polytheists on the day of the Trench, and they offered money for his corpse, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Hand their corpse over to them, for he is foul in his corpse, foul in his blood-money.” So he did not accept anything from them.
items.ma-2231: Naṣr ibn Bāb narrated to us, al-Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ threw the jimār at the declining of the sun, or after the declining of the sun.
items.ma-2232: Naṣr ibn Bāb narrated to us, from al-Ḥajjāj, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: Indeed the people of Badr were three hundred and thirteen men, and the Muhājirūn were seventy-six, and the defeat of the people of Badr was when seventeen [nights] had passed, on Friday, in the month of Ramaḍān.
items.ma-2233: ʿAbd Allāh said: I found in my father's book, in his own handwriting: Mahdī ibn Jaʿfar al-Ramlī narrated to us, al-Walīd – meaning Ibn Muslim – narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Be lenient, and leniency will be shown to you.”
items.ma-2234: ʿAbd Allāh said: I found in my father's book, in his own handwriting: Mahdī ibn Jaʿfar al-Ramlī narrated to us, al-Walīd – meaning Ibn Muslim – narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam ibn Muṣʿab, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, from his father, from his grandfather ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever increases in seeking forgiveness, Allah will make for him a relief from every worry, and a way out from every hardship, and will provide for him from where he does not reckon.”
items.ma-2235:
ʿAffān narrated to us, Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim informed us, Qays ibn Saʿd informed us, from Yazīd ibn Hurmuz, who said: Najdah ibn ʿĀmir wrote to Ibn ʿAbbās asking him about things, and I was present with Ibn ʿAbbās when he read his letter and when he wrote his reply. Ibn ʿAbbās said: “By Allah, were it not that I wish to turn him back from an evil he is falling into, I would not write to him, and no delight of the eye.” He said: So he wrote to him: “You asked me about the share of the near relatives which Allah ﷿ mentioned: who are they? We used to think that they were the relatives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, but our people refused that to us.”
And he asked him about the orphan: when does his orphanhood end? And that when he reaches [the age of] marriage and sound judgement is perceived in him, his property is handed over to him, and his orphanhood has ended.
And he asked him: Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ kill any of the children of the polytheists? So he said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not kill any of them, and you, do not kill, unless you know what al-Khaḍir knew of the boy whom he killed.”
And he asked him about the woman and the slave: did they have a defined share when they attended the fighting? And that they had no defined share, except that they be given a gift from the spoils of the Muslims.
items.ma-2236: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād informed us, from ʿAmmār ibn Abī ʿAmmār, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to deliver the sermon facing a palm trunk before he took the minbar; and when he took the minbar and moved to it, [the trunk] yearned for him. So he came to it and embraced it, and it grew still. He said: “Had I not embraced it, it would have yearned until the Day of Resurrection.”
items.ma-2237: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, from Thābit, from Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ, the like of it.
items.ma-2238: ʿAffān narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, Mūsā ibn Sālim Abū Jahḍam narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās narrated to us, who said: I and some young men of Quraysh entered upon Ibn ʿAbbās. He said: They asked him whether the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite in Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr. He said: “No.” He said: They said: “Perhaps he used to recite to himself!” He said: “Scratching! This is evil. Indeed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was a servant under command; he conveyed what he was sent with. And he did not single us out from the people except with three: he commanded us to complete the wuḍūʾ, not to eat ṣadaqah, and not to put a donkey to a horse.”
items.ma-2239: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent off some people of Banū Hāshim by night – Shuʿbah said: I think he said: their weak ones – and commanded them not to throw at the Jamrah until the sun rose. Shuʿbah doubted “their weak ones.”
items.ma-2240: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, who said: Ibn Ṭāwūs informed me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed Dhū al-Ḥulayfah as the mīqāt for the people of Madinah, al-Juḥfah for the people of al-Shām, Qarn for the people of Najd, and Yalamlam for the people of Yemen. He said: “They are for them, and for whoever comes upon them from others than them, of those who intend Ḥajj and ʿumrah; from where he began, until that reaches the people of Makkah.”
items.ma-2241: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Saʿīd narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaqīq, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to take from the heads while he was fasting.
items.ma-2242: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Hishām narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: [It] was sent down upon the Prophet ﷺ when he was forty years old, and he was in Makkah thirteen [years] and in Madinah ten, and he died when he was sixty-three.
items.ma-2243: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Hishām narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was cupped, a cupping, on his head, while he was in iḥrām.
items.ma-2244: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal, from al-Shaʿbī, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called for a drink. He said: So I brought him a bucket of Zamzam water, and he drank standing.
items.ma-2245: Isḥāq ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Malik narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that he came to his maternal aunt Maymūnah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood from the night to a water-vessel and performed wuḍūʾ, then stood and prayed. He said: And I stood and performed wuḍūʾ, then stood on his left. He said: So he took me by my hand and turned me around from behind him until he stood me on his right.
items.ma-2246: Surayj ibn al-Nuʿmān narrated to us, Hushaym narrated to us, Ḥuṣayn informed us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: I have memorised the sunnah entirely, except that I do not know whether the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite in Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr or not; and I do not know how he used to recite this word: {And I have reached, of old age, ʿutiyyā} [Maryam: 8], or “ʿusiyyā”?
items.ma-2247: Rawḥ narrated to us, Zakariyyā ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn Dīnār narrated to us, that Ibn ʿAbbās used to say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Fruit is not sold until it provides food.”
items.ma-2248: ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Khālid ibn al-Ḥārith narrated to us, Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah, from Abū Nahīk, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever seeks refuge with Allah, grant him refuge; and whoever asks you by Wajh Allāh, give him.”
items.ma-2249: Abū Dāwūd narrated to us, from Zamʿah, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was cupped, and gave the cupper his wage.
items.ma-2250: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from Abū al-Zubayr, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The ʿumrā belongs to the one to whom it was granted as ʿumrā, and the ruqbā to the one to whom it was granted as ruqbā; and the one who returns to his gift is like the one who returns to his vomit.”
items.ma-2251: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from Abū al-Zubayr, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever is granted an ʿumrā, it is valid for the one to whom it was granted as ʿumrā; and whoever grants a ruqbā, it is valid for the one to whom it was granted as ruqbā; and whoever gives a gift, then returns to it, is like the one who returns to his vomit.”
items.ma-2252: Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, from Zāʾidah, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions prayed toward Bayt al-Maqdis for sixteen months, then afterwards the qiblah was turned.
items.ma-2253: Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubārak informed us, al-Ḥajjāj ibn Arṭāh informed us, from al-Ḥakam, from Abū al-Qāsim, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ threw at Jamrat al-ʿAqabah, then slaughtered, then shaved.
items.ma-2254: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, who said: Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd ibn Nuwayfiʿ, the mawlā of the family of al-Zubayr, narrated to me, from Kurayb the mawlā of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās: that Ḍimām ibn Thaʿlabah, the brother of Banū Saʿd ibn Bakr, when he became Muslim, asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the obligations of Islam, of prayer and other than it, so he enumerated to him the five prayers, not adding to them, then the zakāh, then the fast of Ramaḍān, then Ḥajj to the House, then informed him of what Allah had forbidden to him. When he had finished he said: “I bear witness that there is no deity except Allah, and I bear witness that you are the Messenger of Allah, and I will do what you have commanded me, not adding and not decreasing.” He said: Then he turned away, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “If the one with the two braids is truthful, he will enter Paradise.”
items.ma-2255: Surayj ibn al-Nuʿmān narrated to us, Hushaym narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Laylā, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ handed over Khaybar, its land and its palm trees, on a sharing basis, for half.
items.ma-2256: ʿAlī ibn ʿĀṣim narrated to us, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād, from Miqsam and Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I was given five that none before me was given, and I do not say it boastfully: I was sent to every red and black, and there is none of the red or black who enters my ummah except that he is of them; and the earth was made a mosque for me.”
items.ma-2257: Yūnus ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz – meaning al-Dabbāgh – narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh al-Dānāj, ʿIkrimah the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās narrated to us, who said: I prayed behind Abū Hurayrah, and he would say the takbīr when he bowed and when he prostrated. He said: So I mentioned that to Ibn ʿAbbās, and he said: “May you have no mother! Is that not the sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?”
items.ma-2258:
ʿAbd al-Wahhāb narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Yaḥyā ibn al-Jazzār, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: Two girls of Banū Hāshim passed by and came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was praying, and took hold of his knees, and he did not turn away.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: And I and a man of the Anṣār passed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was praying, and we were on a donkey, so we came and entered into the prayer.
items.ma-2259: ʿAlī ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh informed us, Khālid al-Ḥadhdhāʾ informed us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ carried some of the boys of Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib: one behind him and one in front of him.
items.ma-2260: Muʿammar ibn Sulaymān – meaning al-Raqqī – narrated to us, from al-Ḥajjāj, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “There is no marriage except with a guardian, and the ruler is the mawlā of whoever has no mawlā.”
items.ma-2261: Muʿammar ibn Sulaymān al-Raqqī narrated to us, he said: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿĀʾishah, from the Prophet ﷺ, the like of it.
items.ma-2262: Marwān ibn Muʿāwiyah al-Fazārī narrated to us, Ḥumayd ibn ʿAlī al-ʿUqaylī narrated to us, al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Muzāḥim narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed two rakʿahs when he travelled, and four when he stayed. He said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: So whoever prays four in travel is like one who prays two in residence. He said: And Ibn ʿAbbās said: The prayer was shortened only once, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed two rakʿahs and the people prayed one rakʿah each.
items.ma-2263: Yaḥyā ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, Ibn Lahīʿah informed us, from Abū al-Aswad, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed the woman who joins [hair] and the woman for whom it is joined, and the men who liken themselves to women, and the women who liken themselves to men.
items.ma-2264: Ismāʿīl ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, al-Masʿūdī narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set off from ʿArafāt, the people hastened, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded a caller to call: “O people, righteousness is not in the hastening of horses nor of riding-camels.” He said: So I did not see a [camel] raising her foreleg, galloping, until he alighted at Jamʿ.
items.ma-2265: Ismāʿīl ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, Ibn Abī Dhiʾb narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that Usāmah ibn Zayd was riding behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of ʿArafah, and he entered the mountain pass, and dismounted and passed water, then performed wuḍūʾ, and mounted, and did not pray.
items.ma-2266: Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn Shihāb, that Sulaymān ibn Yasār informed him that Ibn ʿAbbās informed him: that a woman from Khathʿam sought a ruling from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the Farewell Ḥajj, while al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās was riding behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and she said: “O Messenger of Allah, the obligation of Allah in Ḥajj has reached my father as a very old man who cannot sit firm upon the mount; will it suffice for him that I perform Ḥajj on his behalf?” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: “Yes.” Then al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās began to look toward her, and she was a beautiful woman, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took hold of al-Faḍl and turned his face to the other side.
items.ma-2267: Ḥusayn ibn Ḥasan al-Ashqar narrated to us, Abū Kudaynah narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Abū al-Ḍuḥā, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: A Jew passed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was sitting. He said: “How do you say, O Abū al-Qāsim, on the day Allah places the heaven on this – and he pointed with the forefinger – and the earth on this, and the water on this, and the mountains on this, and the rest of creation on this?” – in all of that he was pointing with his fingers. He said: So Allah ﷿ revealed: {And they did not appraise Allah with the due of His appraisal} [al-Zumar: 67].
items.ma-2268: Ḥusayn al-Ashqar narrated to us, Abū Kudaynah narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Abū al-Ḍuḥā, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ woke one day, and there was no water in the camp. A man came to him and said: “O Messenger of Allah, there is no water in the camp.” He said: “Do you have anything?” He said: “Yes.” He said: “Bring it to me.” He said: So he brought him a vessel with a little water in it. He said: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ placed his fingers on the mouth of the vessel and spread his fingers apart. He said: Then springs gushed forth from between his fingers, and he commanded Bilāl and said: “Call out among the people: The blessed ablution water!”
items.ma-2269: Yūnus narrated to us, Ḥammād – meaning Ibn Zayd – narrated to us, from al-Zubayr – meaning Ibn Khirrīt – from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaqīq, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās addressed us one day after ʿAṣr until the sun set and the stars appeared, and the people began calling to him: The prayer, the prayer! And among the people was a man from Banū Tamīm who kept saying: The prayer, the prayer! He said: So he became angry and said: “Are you teaching me the sunnah? I witnessed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ combine Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr, and Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ.” ʿAbd Allāh said: So I found in myself something about that, and I met Abū Hurayrah and asked him, and he agreed with him.
items.ma-2270: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from Yūsuf ibn Mihrān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: When the verse of the debt was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The first to deny was Ādam ﵇ – or: the first to deny was Ādam – indeed Allah ﷿, when He created Ādam, wiped his back and brought out from it whatever is a dhāriʾ until the Day of Resurrection, and began to present his offspring to him, and he saw among them a man shining. He said: O my Rabb, who is this? He said: This is your son Dāwūd. He said: O my Rabb, how long is his lifespan? He said: Sixty years. He said: My Rabb, increase his lifespan. He said: No, unless I increase it from your lifespan. And the lifespan of Ādam was a thousand years, so He added to him forty years; and Allah ﷿ wrote a document against him of that, and made the angels witness against him. Then when Ādam was at the point of death, and the angels came to him to take him, he said: There remain forty years of my lifespan. It was said: You gave them to your son Dāwūd. He said: I did not do so. And Allah ﷿ brought out the document against him, and the angels testified against him.”
items.ma-2271: ʿAffān narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, Abū Bishr narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not recite to the jinn, and did not see them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out with a group of his Companions, heading for the market of ʿUkāẓ, and a barrier had been placed between the devils and the news of the heaven, and shooting stars had been sent upon them. He said: So the devils returned to their people, and they said: “What is the matter with you?” They said: “A barrier has been placed between us and the news of the heaven, and shooting stars have been sent upon us.” He said: They said: “Nothing has come between you and the news of the heaven except something that has occurred; so strike through the easts of the earth and its wests, and see what this is that has come between you and the news of the heaven.” He said: So they set off, striking through the easts of the earth and its wests, seeking what this was that had come between them and the news of the heaven. He said: Then the group who had headed toward Tihāmah turned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was at Nakhlah, heading for the market of ʿUkāẓ, and he was praying the Fajr prayer with his Companions. He said: When they heard the Qurʾān, they listened to it, and said: “This, by Allah, is what has come between you and the news of the heaven.” He said: And thereupon, when they returned to their people, they said: “O our people, {indeed we have heard a wondrous Qurʾān that guides to the right course, so we have believed in it}” – the verse [al-Jinn: 2]. And Allah revealed to His Prophet ﷺ: {Say: It has been revealed to me that} and what was revealed to him was only the saying of the jinn.
items.ma-2272: ʿAffān narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṭāwūs narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed Dhū al-Ḥulayfah as the mīqāt for the people of Madinah, al-Juḥfah for the people of al-Shām, Qarn al-Manāzil for the people of Najd, and Yalamlam for the people of Yemen: they are for them, and for everyone who comes upon them from others than them, of those who intend Ḥajj and ʿumrah; and whoever is within that, then from where he began, even the people of Makkah, from Makkah.
items.ma-2273: ʿAffān narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṭāwūs narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married Maymūnah while he was in iḥrām.
items.ma-2274: ʿAffān narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṭāwūs narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: They used to regard ʿumrah in the months of Ḥajj as among the most wicked of wickedness on earth, and they would make Muḥarram Ṣafar, and say: “When the sore has healed, and the trace has faded, and Ṣafar has passed, the ʿumrah becomes lawful for whoever performs ʿumrah.” Then when the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions arrived on the morning of the fourth, assuming ihlāl for Ḥajj, he commanded them to make it an ʿumrah, and this seemed great to them, and they said: “O Messenger of Allah, which release?” He said: “The whole release.” And in his book: “for the morning.”
items.ma-2275: ʿAffān narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṭāwūs narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade a man to sell food until he has taken full possession of it. He said: I said to him: “How is that?” He said: “That is dirhams for dirhams, and the food is deferred.”
items.ma-2276: ʿAffān narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṭāwūs narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah ibn Khālid, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ stood at night to pray, so I stood and performed wuḍūʾ, then stood on his left, and he pulled me, dragged me, and stood me on his right. Then he prayed thirteen rakʿahs, his standing in them being the same.
items.ma-2277: ʿAffān narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, Ayyūb narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Mulaykah, who said: ʿUrwah said to Ibn ʿAbbās: “Until when will you lead the people astray, O Ibn ʿAbbās?!” He said: “What is that, O ʿUrayyah?” He said: “You command us with ʿumrah in the months of Ḥajj, while Abū Bakr and ʿUmar forbade it!” Ibn ʿAbbās said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did it.” ʿUrwah said: “The two of them were more followers of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and more knowing of him than you.”
items.ma-2278: ʿAffān narrated to us, Hammām narrated to us, Qatādah informed us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir came to the Prophet ﷺ and said that his sister had vowed to walk to the House. He said: “Indeed Allah ﷿ is surely free of need of your sister's vow. Let her perform Ḥajj riding, and let her offer a camel.”
items.ma-2279: ʿAffān narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, Khālid narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed Allah ﷿ made Makkah ḥarām, so it was not lawful for anyone who was before me, and it is not lawful for anyone after me; it was made lawful for me only for an hour of the day. Its grass is not cut, its trees are not cut down, its game is not scared away, and its luqaṭah is not picked up except by one who will announce it.” Al-ʿAbbās said: “Except the idhkhir, for our goldsmiths and our graves.” He said: “Except the idhkhir.”
items.ma-2280: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Abū Yaḥyā, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that two men disputed before the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ asked the claimant for proof, and he had no proof, so he made the defendant swear, and he swore by Allah, besides Whom there is no deity except Him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “You have indeed done it, but you have been forgiven for your sincerity in saying: There is no deity except Allah.”
