items.ma-2281: ʿAffān narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, al-Mughīrah ibn al-Nuʿmān, a shaykh of al-Nakhaʿ, narrated to us, who said: I heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrating, who said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood among us with an exhortation and said: “O people, you will be gathered to Allah barefoot, naked, uncircumcised: {As We began the first creation, We shall repeat it – a promise binding upon Us. Indeed We are ever doers} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 104]. Beware, indeed the first of creation to be clothed on the Day of Resurrection is Ibrāhīm. And indeed some people of my ummah will be brought and taken to the left side, and I will say: My Companions! And it will be said to me: You do not know what they innovated after you. Then I will say as the righteous servant said: {And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them; then when You took me, You were the Watcher over them, and You are, over everything, Witness} up to: {For they are Your servants, and if You forgive them, then indeed You, You are the Almighty, the Wise} [al-Māʾidah: 117-118]. Then it will be said: These did not cease to be turned back on their heels since you left them.” Shuʿbah said: He dictated it to Sufyān, and Sufyān dictated it to me in its place.
items.ma-2282: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Mughīrah ibn al-Nuʿmān, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood among us with an exhortation … and he mentioned it.
items.ma-2283: ʿAffān narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, Abū Bishr narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: Indeed what you call al-Mufaṣṣal is the Muḥkam. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ died when I was ten years old, and I had recited the Muḥkam.
items.ma-2284: ʿAffān narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Wāḥid narrated to us, al-Ḥajjāj ibn Arṭāh narrated to us, Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, he said – meaning Ḥajjāj –: And al-Ḥakam narrated to me, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was shrouded in two white garments and in a red cloak.
items.ma-2285: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib informed us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that Ibrāhīm brought Ismāʿīl ﵉ and Hājar, and placed them in Makkah at the place of Zamzam; and he mentioned the ḥadīth. Then she came from al-Marwah to Ismāʿīl, and the spring had gushed forth, and she began to scoop out the spring with her hand like this, until the water gathered from its side, then she would take it with her cup and put it in her waterskin. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “May Allah have mercy on her; had she left it, it would have been a flowing spring running until the Day of Resurrection.”
items.ma-2286: ʿAffān narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAṭāʾ narrated to us, that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: Indeed the Prophet ﷺ ate either a roasted forearm or a shoulder, then prayed, and did not perform wuḍūʾ and did not touch water.
items.ma-2287: ʿAffān narrated to us, Khālid narrated to us, Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād narrated to us, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: We arrived with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as pilgrims, and he commanded them, so they made it an ʿumrah. Then he said: “If I had faced of my affair what I have turned my back on, I would have done as they did; but the ʿumrah has entered into the Ḥajj until the Day of Resurrection.” Then he interlaced his fingers, some of them in others. So the people left iḥrām, except those who had a hady with them. And ʿAlī came from Yemen, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: “With what did you assume ihlāl?” He said: “I assumed ihlāl with that with which you assumed ihlāl.” He said: “Do you have a hady with you?” He said: “No.” He said: “Then stay as you are, and for you is a third of my hady.” He said: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had with him a hundred camels.
items.ma-2288: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, from Farqad al-Sabakhī, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a woman came with a son of hers to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: “O Messenger of Allah, this son of mine has madness, and it seizes him at our midday meal and our evening meal, and spoils it for us.” So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wiped his chest and supplicated, and he vomited a vomit – ʿAffān said: I asked a Bedouin and he said: some of it after another – and there came out of his belly something like a black puppy, and he ran off.
items.ma-2289: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took a bone out of a pot, and prayed, and did not perform wuḍūʾ.
items.ma-2290: ʿAffān narrated to us, Abān al-ʿAṭṭār narrated to us, Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr narrated to us, from Zayd, from Abū Sallām, from al-Ḥakam ibn Mīnāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās and from Ibn ʿUmar, that both of them heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Peoples will surely cease their abandoning of the Friday [prayers], or Allah will surely seal upon their hearts, then they will surely be written among the heedless.”
items.ma-2291: Khalaf ibn al-Walīd narrated to us, Khālid narrated to us, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed the effeminate among men and the women who act like men. He said: So I said: “What are the women who act like men?” He said: “Those among women who liken themselves to men.”
items.ma-2292: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, ʿAlī ibn Zayd informed us, from a man, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed over al-Najāshī.
items.ma-2293: ʿAffān narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, Bukayr ibn al-Akhnas narrated to us, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Allah made the prayer obligatory upon the tongue of your Prophet: in residence four, in travel two rakʿahs, and in fear one rakʿah.
items.ma-2294: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, he said: ʿAlī ibn Zayd informed us, from Yūsuf ibn Mihrān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is none of the children of Ādam but has erred, or intended a sin – not Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā; and it is not fitting for anyone to say: I am better than Yūnus ibn Mattā.”
items.ma-2295: ʿAffān narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Yaḥyā ibn al-Jazzār, that Ibn ʿAbbās said: A boy of Banū Hāshim and I passed by on a donkey, and we left it eating of the herbage in front of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he did not turn away; and two girls came running hard until they took hold of the knees of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he did not turn away.
items.ma-2296: ʿAffān narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: Qatādah informed me, he said: I heard Abū Ḥassān narrating from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ prayed the Ẓuhr at Dhū al-Ḥulayfah, then called for his camel, or his camel was brought to him, and he marked the right side of its hump, then wiped the blood from it, and garlanded it with two sandals. Then his mount was brought, and when he sat upon it and it stood up with him on al-Baydāʾ, he assumed ihlāl for Ḥajj.
items.ma-2297: ʿAffān narrated to us, Abān ibn Yazīd narrated to us, Qatādah narrated to us, from Abū al-ʿĀliyah al-Riyāḥī, from the cousin of your Prophet – meaning Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ used to supplicate with these supplications in distress: “There is no deity except Allah, the All-Knowing, the Great; there is no deity except Allah, Rabb of the Great Throne; there is no deity except Allah, Rabb of the seven heavens and Rabb of the Noble Throne.”
items.ma-2298: ʿAffān narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Qatādah, who said: I heard Abū al-ʿĀliyah say: I heard the cousin of your Prophet ﷺ, Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ. And Bahz said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, Qatādah informed me, from Abū al-ʿĀliyah, who said: The cousin of your Prophet ﷺ narrated to me, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “It is not fitting for a servant – ʿAffān said: a servant of mine – to say: I am better than Yūnus ibn Mattā.” And he ascribed him to his father.
items.ma-2299:
ʿAffān narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, Abū Bishr informed me, who said: I heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrating from Ibn ʿAbbās: that his maternal aunt Umm Ḥufayd presented to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ghee, lizards and dried curd. He said: So he ate of the ghee and of the dried curd, and left the lizards out of distaste, and they were eaten at the table of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; and had it been ḥarām, it would not have been eaten at the table of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
I said: Who said: “had it been ḥarām”? He said: Ibn ʿAbbās.
items.ma-2300: ʿAffān narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn Dīnār said: Ṭāwūs reported to me, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: I was commanded to prostrate on seven, and not to gather up hair or garment. Then he said another time: Your Prophet ﷺ was commanded to prostrate on seven, and not to gather up hair or garment.
items.ma-2301: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, he said: ʿAlī ibn Zayd informed me, from Yūsuf ibn Mihrān, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that Jibrīl said to the Prophet ﷺ: “The prayer has been made beloved to you, so take of it what you wish.”
items.ma-2302: ʿAffān narrated to us, Abū al-Aḥwaṣ narrated to us, he said: Simāk informed us, from ʿIkrimah, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: I was approached while I was asleep in Ramaḍān, and it was said to me: Tonight is Laylat al-Qadr. He said: So I stood, drowsy, and clung to one of the ropes of the tent of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he was praying. He said: And I looked at that night, and it was the night of the twenty-third.
items.ma-2303: ʿAffān narrated to us, Thābit – meaning Ibn Yazīd – narrated to us, Hilāl narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ used to spend consecutive nights hungry, and his family finding no supper. He said: And the greater part of their bread was barley bread.
items.ma-2304: ʿAffān narrated to us, Sulaymān ibn Kathīr Abū Dāwūd al-Wāsiṭī narrated to us, who said: I heard Ibn Shihāb narrating, from Abū Sinān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: He addressed us – meaning the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: “O people, Ḥajj has been prescribed upon you.” He said: Then al-Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis stood and said: “Every year, O Messenger of Allah?” He said: “If I were to say it, it would become obligatory, and if it became obligatory you would not act upon it – or: you would not be able to act upon it. Ḥajj is once; whoever adds, it is voluntary.”
items.ma-2305: ʿAffān narrated to us, Hammām narrated to us, Qatādah narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ performed ṭawāf seven times, and performed ṭawāf at a run, and he ran only [because] he liked to show the people his strength.
items.ma-2306: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd al-Hāshimī narrated to us, Abū Zubayd informed us, from al-Aʿmash, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the Ẓuhr at Minā on the day of Tarwiyah.
items.ma-2307: Qutaybah ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, from Abū al-Aswad, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Let none of you prevent his brother from his mirfaq, that he place it on his wall.”
items.ma-2308: Qutaybah ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, from Ibn Hubayrah, from Maymūn al-Makkī: that he saw Ibn al-Zubayr, ʿAbd Allāh, and he prayed with them, gesturing with his palms when he stood, and when he bowed, and when he prostrated, and when he rose to stand; so he would stand and gesture with his hands. He said: So I went to Ibn ʿAbbās and said to him: “I have seen Ibn al-Zubayr pray a prayer that I have not seen anyone pray,” and I described to him this gesture. He said: “If you wish to look at the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then follow the prayer of Ibn al-Zubayr.”
items.ma-2309: Qutaybah ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā narrated to us, from Dāwūd, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Quraysh said to the Jews: “Give us something we may ask this man about.” They said: “Ask him about the spirit.” So they asked him, and it was revealed: {And they ask you about the spirit. Say: The spirit is of the command of my Rabb, and you have not been given of knowledge except a little} [al-Isrāʾ: 85]. They said: “We have been given much knowledge: we have been given the Torah, and whoever has been given the Torah has been given much good.” He said: So Allah ﷿ revealed: {Say: If the sea were ink for the words of my Rabb, the sea would be exhausted} [al-Kahf: 109].
items.ma-1740:
Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, Muḥammad ibn Muslim ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Shihāb narrated to me, from Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām al-Makhzūmī, from Umm Salamah daughter of Abū Umayyah ibn al-Mughīrah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, she said: When we settled in the land of Abyssinia, we had as neighbour there the best of neighbours, al-Najāshī. We were safe in our religion, and we worshipped Allah without being harmed, and we heard nothing that we disliked. When that reached Quraysh, they took counsel together to send to al-Najāshī, concerning us, two strong men, and to give al-Najāshī gifts of the novel things of the goods of Makkah. The most admired of what came to him from it was leather, so they gathered a great deal of leather for him, and they left no patrician among his patricians without giving him a gift. Then they sent that with ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Rabīʿah ibn al-Mughīrah al-Makhzūmī and ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil al-Sahmī, and they gave the two their instructions, and said to them: "Give each patrician his gift before you speak to al-Najāshī about them, then present his gifts to al-Najāshī, then ask him to surrender them to you before he speaks to them."
She said: So the two went out and came to al-Najāshī, while we were with him in the best of homes and with the best of neighbours. There remained no patrician among his patricians to whom they did not give his gift before speaking to al-Najāshī. Then they said to each patrician among them: "Foolish youths from among us have inclined to the land of the king. They have left the religion of their people and have not entered your religion, and they have come with an invented religion that neither we nor you know. The nobles of their people have sent us to the king concerning them, to return them to them. So when we speak to the king about them, advise him to surrender them to us and not to speak to them, for their own people have a keener eye on them and know better what they found fault with in them." So they said to the two: "Yes."
Then the two brought their gifts near to al-Najāshī, and he accepted them from the two. Then they spoke to him and said to him: "O King, foolish youths from among us have inclined to your land. They have left the religion of their people and have not entered your religion, and they have come with an invented religion that neither we nor you know. The nobles of their people, their fathers, their paternal uncles and their clans, have sent us to you concerning them, so that you return them to them, for they have a keener eye on them and know better what they found fault with in them and reproached them for." She said: And nothing was more hateful to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Rabīʿah and ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ than that al-Najāshī should hear their speech. Then his patricians around him said: "They have spoken truly, O King. Their own people have a keener eye on them and know better what they found fault with in them. So surrender them to the two, and let the two return them to their lands and their people." She said: Al-Najāshī became angry, then said: "By Allah — then I will not surrender them to the two, nor will I plot against a people who have neighboured me and settled in my lands and chosen me over others, until I summon them and ask them what these two say about their affair. If they are as the two say, I will surrender them to the two and return them to their people, and if they are otherwise, I will protect them from the two and treat them well in neighbourliness for as long as they neighbour me."
She said: Then he sent for the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and summoned them. When his messenger came to them, they gathered, then some of them said to others: "What will you say to the man when you come to him?" They said: "We will say, by Allah, what we were taught and what our Prophet ﷺ commanded us, whatever may come of it." When they came to him, al-Najāshī had summoned his bishops, and they had spread out their books around him. He asked them and said: "What is this religion for which you have left your people, and have not entered my religion, nor the religion of anyone of these nations?" She said: And the one who spoke to him was Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib. He said to him: "O King, we were a people of Jāhiliyyah. We worshipped idols, ate carrion, committed indecencies, severed the ties of kinship, and treated neighbours badly; the strong among us would devour the weak. We were upon that until Allah sent to us a Messenger from among us, whose lineage and truthfulness, trustworthiness and chastity we know. He called us to Allah, that we should declare His oneness and worship Him, and cast off what we and our fathers used to worship besides Him of stones and idols. And he commanded us to truthful speech, to fulfilling the trust, to maintaining the ties of kinship, to good neighbourliness, and to refraining from the forbidden things and from bloodshed. And he forbade us from indecencies, false speech, consuming the property of the orphan, and slandering a chaste woman. And he commanded us to worship Allah alone, associating nothing with Him, and he commanded us to prayer, zakāh and fasting" — she said: and he enumerated to him the matters of Islam — "so we believed him, and had faith in him, and followed him in what he brought."
And we worshipped Allah alone and associated nothing with Him, and we held forbidden what he forbade us, and held lawful what he made lawful for us. Then our people attacked us and tortured us and tried to turn us from our religion, to return us from the worship of Allah to the worship of idols, and that we should deem lawful what we used to deem lawful of vile things. So when they overpowered us, wronged us, made things hard for us, and came between us and our religion, we went out to your land, and chose you over others, and desired your neighbourhood, and hoped that we would not be wronged with you, O King." She said: Al-Najāshī said to him: "Do you have with you anything of what he brought from Allah?" She said: Jaʿfar said to him: "Yes." Al-Najāshī said to him: "Then recite it to me." So he recited to him an opening portion of {Kāf, Hāʾ, Yāʾ, ʿAyn, Ṣād}. She said: By Allah, al-Najāshī wept until his beard was wet, and his bishops wept until their books were wet, when they heard what he recited to them. Then al-Najāshī said: "Indeed this and what Mūsā brought come out of a single niche. Go, for by Allah I will never surrender them to you, nor will I plot against them."
Umm Salamah said: When the two had left him, ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ said: "By Allah, tomorrow I will tell him of a fault of theirs, and then I will uproot their greenery with it." She said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Rabīʿah, who was the more God-fearing of the two men among us, said to him: "Do not do it, for they have ties of kinship, even if they have opposed us." He said: "By Allah, I will inform him that they claim that ʿĪsā ibn Maryam is a servant." She said: Then he went to him the next morning and said to him: "O King, they say a grave thing about ʿĪsā ibn Maryam. So send for them and ask them about what they say concerning him." She said: So he sent for them to ask them about him — she said: and nothing like it had ever befallen us — and the people gathered, and some of them said to others: "What will you say about ʿĪsā when he asks you about him?" They said: "By Allah, we will say about him what Allah said and what our Prophet brought, whatever may come of it." When they entered upon him, he said to them: "What do you say about ʿĪsā ibn Maryam?" Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib said to him: "We say about him what our Prophet brought: He is the servant of Allah and His Messenger and His spirit and His word, which He cast to Maryam, the virgin, the detached one." She said: Al-Najāshī struck his hand to the ground and took from it a stick, then said: "ʿĪsā ibn Maryam did not exceed what you said by [the measure of] this stick." His patricians snorted around him when he said what he said. He said: "Even if you snort, by Allah. Go, for you are sūyūm in my land — and the sūyūm are the secure ones — whoever reviles you will be fined, then whoever reviles you will be fined, then whoever reviles you will be fined. I would not love to have a dabr of gold while I harmed a man of you" — and the dabr in the tongue of the Abyssinians is the mountain — "Return to the two their gifts, for we have no need of them, for by Allah, Allah did not take a bribe from me when He restored to me my kingdom, that I should take a bribe in it, and the people did not obey in my case, that I should obey them in it." She said: So the two went out from him in disgrace, what they had brought returned to them, and we remained with him in the best of homes with the best of neighbours.
She said: By Allah, while we were in that state, there came upon him — meaning someone who disputed with him over his kingdom. She said: By Allah, we never knew a grief greater than the grief we felt at that, out of fear that that one would prevail over al-Najāshī, and a man would come who did not recognise our right as al-Najāshī recognised it. She said: And al-Najāshī marched, and between the two of them was the breadth of the Nile. She said: The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Who is the man who will go out until he attends the clash of the people, then come to us with the news?" She said: Al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām said: "I." She said: And he was among the youngest of the people in age. She said: So they inflated a waterskin for him, and he put it on his chest, then swam upon it until he came out to the side of the Nile where the people were meeting, then went on until he was present with them. She said: And we supplicated to Allah for al-Najāshī, that he prevail over his enemy and be established in his lands, and the affair of the Abyssinians became united under him, and we were with him in the best of abodes, until we came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was in Makkah.
